questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: The visceral layer of the serous pericardium has a second name. What is it?
options: The parietal pericardium
The fibrous pericardium
The endocardium
The epicardium
questions.why: The visceral layer of the serous pericardium is the same membrane as the epicardium, the outermost layer of the heart wall. It is called visceral because it lies on the organ, and epicardium because it sits on top of the heart muscle. Recognizing both names prevents counting it twice when listing the layers around the heart.
notes: The parietal pericardium is the serous layer that lines the inside of the fibrous pericardium. It is the wall-side layer, not the layer on the heart.
The fibrous pericardium is the tough, outermost sac that anchors the heart in the mediastinum. It is separate from the serous layers and does not touch the heart surface.
The endocardium is the innermost layer of the heart wall, lining the chambers and valves. Pick it for a question about the lining inside the heart.
Correct. The visceral pericardium is the epicardium.
questions.answerText: The epicardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Moving from the outside inward toward the heart muscle, which order lists the layers and space around the heart correctly?
options: Epicardium, pericardial cavity, parietal serous pericardium, fibrous pericardium
Parietal serous pericardium, fibrous pericardium, pericardial cavity, epicardium
Pericardial cavity, fibrous pericardium, epicardium, parietal serous pericardium
Fibrous pericardium, parietal serous pericardium, pericardial cavity, epicardium
questions.why: The outermost layer is the tough fibrous pericardium, which anchors the heart and prevents overfilling. Lining its inner surface is the parietal layer of the serous pericardium, then comes the pericardial cavity with its film of fluid, and finally the visceral layer, the epicardium, lies on the heart itself. The parietal-then-visceral pattern is the same in every serous membrane.
notes: This is the correct sequence written in reverse, from the heart outward. It would be the answer if the question asked for the order from the inside out.
This order puts the serous parietal layer outside the fibrous sac. The fibrous pericardium is the outermost layer, with the parietal serous layer lining its inner surface.
This order starts with the cavity, which is a space between two serous layers and cannot be the outermost structure. It also separates the fibrous pericardium from the parietal layer fused to it.
Correct. Fibrous, parietal, cavity, visceral.
questions.answerText: Fibrous pericardium, parietal serous pericardium, pericardial cavity, epicardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Fluid building up in the pericardial cavity, called cardiac tamponade, can stop the heart from pumping well. Using the structure of the pericardium, why does this happen?
options: The fluid drains into the pleural cavities and collapses the lungs
The fluid seeps into the heart muscle and makes it beat too fast
The stiff fibrous sac lets the fluid squeeze the heart and limit filling
The fluid passes into the chambers and thins the blood
questions.why: The fibrous pericardium is a tough, inelastic sac of dense connective tissue that normally anchors the heart and keeps it from overfilling. When fluid collects in the pericardial cavity inside it, the sac cannot stretch to make room, so the fluid squeezes the heart from outside. The chambers cannot fill fully, and the heart pumps less blood with each beat.
notes: The pericardial cavity is a closed space, separate from the pleural cavities. The fluid stays trapped around the heart, which is what makes it dangerous.
The pericardial cavity is outside the heart wall, so the fluid does not enter the heart muscle. The problem is pressure on the heart from outside.
Correct. The inelastic sac turns extra fluid into pressure on the heart.
The pericardial cavity does not connect with the inside of the heart chambers. The fluid stays in the sac and compresses the heart.
questions.answerText: The stiff fibrous sac lets the fluid squeeze the heart and limit filling

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: In which division of the thoracic cavity does the heart sit?
options: The retroperitoneal space
The left pleural cavity
The peritoneal cavity
The mediastinum
questions.why: The heart sits in the mediastinum, the central compartment of the thoracic cavity between the two lungs. The mediastinum runs from the sternum in front to the vertebral column behind and also holds the great vessels, trachea, and esophagus. The heart rests on the diaphragm within it and tilts to the left.
notes: The retroperitoneal space lies behind the peritoneum on the posterior abdominal wall, where the kidneys sit. Pick it for the kidneys or pancreas, not the heart.

Each pleural cavity is the space around one lung, on either side of the mediastinum. The heart tilts toward the left, but it lies between the pleural cavities, so pick the pleural cavity for a question about the lungs.
The peritoneal cavity is inside the abdominopelvic cavity, below the diaphragm, and holds organs like the stomach and intestines. Pick it for an abdominal organ, not the heart.
Correct. The heart sits in the mediastinum, between the two lungs.
questions.answerText: The mediastinum

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What is the blunt, rounded inferior tip of the heart called?
options: The base
The auricle
The coronary sulcus
The apex
questions.why: The apex is the rounded inferior tip of the heart, pointing down, forward, and to the left. It is formed by the tip of the left ventricle. The heart's orientation can feel upside down at first, because the apex points downward while the base is the broad surface at the top.
notes: The base is the broad superior surface of the heart, where the great vessels enter and leave. Pick the base if the question asked about the surface opposite the tip.
An auricle is a small wrinkled pouch on each atrium. Pick it if the question asked about the ear-shaped flap that slightly increases atrial capacity.
The coronary sulcus is the groove that circles the heart between the atria and the ventricles, carrying coronary vessels. Pick it for a question about that surface groove.
Correct. The apex is the pointed inferior tip, formed by the left ventricle.
questions.answerText: The apex

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What is the broad superior surface of the heart, where the great vessels attach, called?
options: The sternocostal surface
The diaphragmatic surface
The apex
The base
questions.why: The base is the broad superior surface of the heart, formed mostly by the left atrium, where the great vessels enter and leave. The name can be confusing because the base sits at the top, opposite the apex at the bottom. Thinking of the heart as a cone resting on its tip helps, since the wide end of a cone is its base.
notes: The sternocostal surface is the anterior surface, mostly right ventricle, lying behind the sternum and ribs. Pick it if the question asked which surface faces the front of the chest.
The diaphragmatic surface is the inferior surface, mostly left ventricle, resting on the diaphragm. Pick it if the question asked which surface sits on the diaphragm.
The apex is the rounded inferior tip of the heart, formed by the left ventricle. Pick it if the question asked about the tip that points down and to the left.
Correct. The base is the broad superior surface where the great vessels attach.
questions.answerText: The base

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What is the double-walled sac that encloses the heart called?
options: The peritoneum
The pericardium
The pleura
The endocardium
questions.why: The pericardium is the double-walled sac around the heart. Its outer part is the tough fibrous pericardium, and inside that is the serous pericardium, a thin membrane with one layer lining the sac and one layer on the heart's surface. The prefix peri means around and cardi means heart, so the name describes exactly what it does.
notes: The peritoneum is the serous membrane that lines the abdominopelvic cavity and covers its organs. Pick it for a question about the abdomen.
Correct. The pericardium is the double-walled sac that encloses the heart.
The pleura is the double-layered serous membrane around each lung. Pick the pleura if the question asked about the membrane covering the lungs.
The endocardium is the smooth inner lining of the heart chambers, not a sac outside the heart. Pick it if the question asked what lines the chambers.
questions.answerText: The pericardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which layer of the heart wall is the thick, muscular middle layer that contracts?
options: The endocardium
The myocardium
The epicardium
The fibrous pericardium
questions.why: The myocardium is the thick middle layer of the heart wall, made of cardiac muscle arranged in spiralling bundles. It makes up about 95 percent of the wall's thickness and is the layer that actually contracts to pump blood. The prefix myo means muscle, which is a quick way to remember its job.
notes: The endocardium is the thin, smooth inner lining of the chambers and valves. Pick it if the question asked what lines the inside of the heart.
Correct. The myocardium is the thick cardiac muscle layer that contracts.
The epicardium is the thin outer layer of the heart wall, a serous membrane with fat and coronary vessels in it. Pick it if the question asked about the outermost wall layer.
The fibrous pericardium is the tough outer sac around the heart, not part of the heart wall. Pick it if the question asked what anchors the heart in the mediastinum.
questions.answerText: The myocardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which layer forms the smooth inner lining of the heart chambers?
options: The myocardium
The parietal pericardium
The endocardium
The epicardium
questions.why: The endocardium is the innermost layer of the heart wall, a smooth endothelium that lines the chambers. Its smoothness lets blood flow past without clotting or catching. The prefix endo means within, which matches its position on the inside of the heart.
notes: The myocardium is the thick muscular middle layer that contracts. Pick it if the question asked about the layer that pumps blood.
The parietal layer of the serous pericardium lines the inside of the fibrous sac, facing the pericardial cavity. Pick it for a question about the lining of the sac, not the lining of the chambers.
Correct. The endocardium is the smooth endothelial lining of the chambers.
The epicardium is the outer layer of the heart wall, on the heart's surface. Pick it if the question asked about the outermost layer of the wall.
questions.answerText: The endocardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
options: Three
Four
Five
Two
questions.why: The human heart has four chambers, two atria above and two ventricles below. The atria are thin-walled receiving chambers, and the ventricles are thick-walled pumping chambers. Having a separate right and left pair lets the heart run the pulmonary and systemic circuits side by side without mixing the blood.
notes: A three-chambered heart, with two atria and one shared ventricle, is found in amphibians such as frogs. The human heart has a separate ventricle on each side.
Correct. The heart has four chambers: right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle.
There is no fifth chamber. Students sometimes count an auricle as a chamber, but an auricle is only a pouch on an atrium.
Two is the number of atria, or the number of ventricles, but not the total. Pick two if the question asked how many ventricles the heart has.
questions.answerText: Four

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which heart chamber has the thickest wall?
options: The left ventricle
The left atrium
The right atrium
The right ventricle
questions.why: The left ventricle has the thickest wall of the four chambers because it pumps blood out through the aorta to the entire body. Pushing blood through the whole systemic circuit takes much more force than any other chamber needs. In a cross section of the ventricles, the left ventricle looks like a thick ring and the right like a thinner crescent beside it.
notes: Correct. The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps to the entire body.
The left atrium is a thin-walled receiving chamber that only moves blood a short distance into the left ventricle. Pick it if the question asked which chamber receives the pulmonary veins.
The right atrium is a thin-walled receiving chamber for blood from the body. Pick it if the question asked which chamber receives the venae cavae.
The right ventricle is thicker than the atria but much thinner than the left ventricle, since it pumps only to the nearby lungs. Pick it if the question asked which chamber pumps to the lungs.
questions.answerText: The left ventricle

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What is the thick wall between the two ventricles called?
options: The fibrous pericardium
The interventricular septum
The coronary sulcus
The interatrial septum
questions.why: The interventricular septum is the thick muscular wall that divides the right ventricle from the left ventricle. Inter means between, and septum means a dividing wall, so the name reads as the wall between the ventricles. It keeps oxygen-poor blood on the right separate from oxygen-rich blood on the left.
notes: The fibrous pericardium is the tough outer sac around the whole heart. Pick it if the question asked what anchors the heart in the mediastinum.
Correct. The interventricular septum divides the two ventricles.
The coronary sulcus is a groove on the outer surface of the heart between the atria and ventricles, carrying coronary vessels. It is a surface groove, not an internal wall.
The interatrial septum is the thinner wall between the two atria, where the fossa ovalis is found. Pick it if the question asked about the wall between the atria.
questions.answerText: The interventricular septum

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What is the small wrinkled pouch on each atrium called?
options: A cusp
A papillary muscle
An auricle
The fossa ovalis
questions.why: An auricle is a small, wrinkled, ear-shaped pouch that projects from each atrium and slightly increases its capacity. The name comes from the Latin for little ear. On a heart model, the auricles are easy to spot as flaps on the front of each atrium, next to the base of the great arteries.
notes: A cusp is one flap of a heart valve. Pick it if the question asked about the leaflets that close a valve opening.
A papillary muscle is a cone-shaped muscle projection inside a ventricle that anchors the chordae tendineae. Pick it if the question asked what anchors the valve cords.
Correct. An auricle is the wrinkled pouch on each atrium.
The fossa ovalis is an oval depression in the interatrial septum, the remnant of a fetal opening. It is a dip inside the heart, not a pouch on the outside.
questions.answerText: An auricle

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: The epicardium, the outer layer of the heart wall, is the same membrane as which layer of the pericardium?
options: The fibrous pericardium
The parietal layer of the serous pericardium
The visceral layer of the serous pericardium
The pericardial cavity
questions.why: The serous pericardium has two layers. The visceral layer lies directly on the heart's surface, and that same membrane is called the epicardium when you describe it as part of the heart wall. Visceral means on an organ and parietal means on a wall, which is a pattern that repeats for the pleura and peritoneum.
notes: The fibrous pericardium is the tough outer sac of dense connective tissue. Pick it if the question asked what anchors the heart and prevents overfilling.
The parietal layer lines the inside of the fibrous pericardium, facing the heart across the pericardial cavity. Pick it if the question asked which serous layer lines the sac.
Correct. The epicardium and the visceral layer of the serous pericardium are the same membrane.
The pericardial cavity is the fluid-filled space between the visceral and parietal layers. It is a space, not a membrane, so pick it for a question about where pericardial fluid sits.
questions.answerText: The visceral layer of the serous pericardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What is the space between the parietal and visceral layers of the serous pericardium called?
options: The mediastinum
The pericardial cavity
The pleural cavity
The medullary cavity
questions.why: The serous pericardium is folded into two layers, a parietal layer lining the sac and a visceral layer on the heart. The thin space between them is the pericardial cavity, and it holds a small film of serous fluid. That fluid lets the two layers slide over each other as the heart beats.
notes: The mediastinum is the central region of the thoracic cavity that holds the heart. It contains the whole pericardium, so pick it for a question about where the heart sits.
Correct. The pericardial cavity is the space between the two serous layers.
The pleural cavity is the space between the two layers of pleura around a lung. Pick it if the question asked about the space around the lungs.
The medullary cavity is the hollow center of a long bone's shaft, filled with marrow. Pick it for a question about bone anatomy.
questions.answerText: The pericardial cavity

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which part of the pericardium is the tough outer layer of dense connective tissue that anchors the heart in the mediastinum?
options: The fibrous pericardium
The endocardium
The parietal layer of the serous pericardium
The epicardium
questions.why: The fibrous pericardium is the tough, inelastic outer layer of the pericardial sac. It is made of dense connective tissue, which anchors the heart to surrounding structures in the mediastinum. Because it does not stretch, it also keeps the heart from overfilling with blood.
notes: Correct. The fibrous pericardium is the tough outer layer that anchors the heart.
The endocardium is the smooth lining of the heart chambers. Pick it if the question asked what lines the inside of the heart.
The parietal layer of the serous pericardium is a thin membrane lining the inside of the fibrous sac. Pick it if the question asked which serous layer faces the pericardial cavity from the outside.
The epicardium is the thin serous membrane on the heart's surface, the outer layer of the heart wall. Pick it if the question asked about the outermost layer of the heart wall rather than the sac.
questions.answerText: The fibrous pericardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which chamber forms most of the base of the heart?
options: The right atrium
The left ventricle
The right ventricle
The left atrium
questions.why: The base of the heart is its broad superior and posterior surface, and it is formed mostly by the left atrium. This is where the four pulmonary veins enter, so the base is crowded with great vessels. The opposite end, the apex, is formed by the left ventricle.
notes: The right atrium forms the right border of the heart and receives the venae cavae. Pick it if the question asked which chamber receives blood from the body.
The left ventricle forms the apex and most of the inferior, diaphragmatic surface. Pick it if the question asked which chamber forms the tip of the heart.
The right ventricle forms most of the anterior, or sternocostal, surface of the heart. Pick it if the question asked which chamber lies right behind the sternum.
Correct. The left atrium forms most of the base of the heart.
questions.answerText: The left atrium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which layer of the heart wall is a thin serous membrane on the heart's outer surface, with fat and the coronary vessels running in it?
options: The myocardium
The endocardium
The fibrous pericardium
The epicardium
questions.why: The epicardium is the outermost layer of the heart wall. It is a thin serous membrane, the same membrane as the visceral layer of the serous pericardium. Fat and the coronary arteries and veins run within it, which is why the surface of a real heart looks yellowish along its grooves.
notes: The myocardium is the thick middle layer of cardiac muscle that contracts. Pick it if the question asked about the layer that pumps blood.
The endocardium is the smooth inner lining of the chambers and valves. Pick it if the question asked what lines the inside of the heart.
The fibrous pericardium is the tough outer sac around the heart, not part of the heart wall. Pick it for the layer that anchors the heart in the mediastinum.
Correct. The epicardium is the thin serous outer layer where fat and coronary vessels run.
questions.answerText: The epicardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which chamber forms most of the anterior surface of the heart, lying just behind the sternum and ribs?
options: The left ventricle
The right atrium
The left atrium
The right ventricle
questions.why: The heart is rotated in the chest so that its right side faces forward. As a result, the right ventricle forms most of the anterior, or sternocostal, surface, lying right behind the sternum and ribs. The left ventricle sits more to the left and underneath, forming the apex and resting on the diaphragm.
notes: The left ventricle forms the apex and most of the inferior surface on the diaphragm. Pick it if the question asked which chamber forms the tip of the heart.
The right atrium forms the right border of the heart. Pick it if the question asked which chamber receives the venae cavae.
The left atrium forms most of the base, on the posterior side of the heart. Pick it if the question asked which chamber faces back toward the vertebral column.
Correct. The right ventricle forms most of the anterior surface of the heart.
questions.answerText: The right ventricle

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: After a chest injury, blood leaks into the space between the visceral and parietal layers of the serous pericardium and begins to compress the heart. Where is the blood collecting?
options: In the pericardial cavity
In the mediastinum outside the pericardium
In a heart chamber
In the pleural cavity
questions.why: The space between the visceral and parietal serous layers is the pericardial cavity, which normally holds only a thin film of fluid. Because the fibrous pericardium around it does not stretch, blood collecting there has nowhere to go and squeezes the heart. This compression is called cardiac tamponade, and it limits how much the heart can fill.
notes: Correct. Blood between the serous layers collects in the pericardial cavity.

The mediastinum is the region that contains the pericardium, but blood outside the pericardial sac would not be trapped between the serous layers. Pick it for bleeding into the central chest outside the heart's sac.
A heart chamber holds circulating blood inside the heart. Blood in a chamber is normal and does not press on the heart from outside.
The pleural cavity is the space around a lung. Blood there, called a hemothorax, compresses the lung rather than the heart.
questions.answerText: In the pericardial cavity

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What are the parallel muscular ridges on the inner walls of the atria and auricles called?
options: The pectinate muscles
The trabeculae carneae
The chordae tendineae
The papillary muscles
questions.why: The pectinate muscles are parallel ridges of muscle on the inner walls of the atria and auricles. Their name comes from the Latin for comb, because the ridges line up like the teeth of a comb. In the right atrium, a ridge called the crista terminalis separates the rough pectinate wall from the smooth posterior wall.
notes: Correct. The pectinate muscles are the comb-like ridges inside the atria and auricles.
The trabeculae carneae are irregular muscular ridges on the inner walls of the ventricles, not the atria. Pick them if the question asked about ridges inside the ventricles.
The chordae tendineae are fibrous cords, not muscle ridges, that tie the atrioventricular valve cusps to the papillary muscles. Pick them for the cords that hold the valves.
The papillary muscles are cone-shaped projections in the ventricles that anchor the chordae tendineae. Pick them if the question asked what anchors the valve cords.
questions.answerText: The pectinate muscles

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which list gives the three layers of the heart wall in order from outermost to innermost?
options: Epicardium, then myocardium, then endocardium
Endocardium, then myocardium, then epicardium
Epicardium, then endocardium, then myocardium
Myocardium, then epicardium, then endocardium
questions.why: The heart wall is built from outside in as epicardium, myocardium, and endocardium. The prefixes give the order away: epi means upon, myo means muscle, and endo means within. So the thin membrane on the surface is outside, the thick muscle is in the middle, and the smooth lining is inside.
notes: Correct. From outside in, the layers are the epicardium, myocardium, and endocardium.
This list is the right layers in reverse, from innermost to outermost. Pick it if the question asked for the order from inside out.
This list places the endocardium in the middle, but the endocardium is the inner lining that touches the blood. The thick myocardium sits between the two thin layers.
This list puts the muscle layer on the outside. The myocardium is covered on its outer surface by the epicardium, so it cannot be outermost.
questions.answerText: Epicardium, then myocardium, then endocardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: The heart sits in the mediastinum, tilted to the left. Which structure does it rest on?
options: The sternum
The diaphragm
The first rib
The liver
questions.why: The heart sits in the mediastinum between the lungs and rests on the diaphragm, the dome-shaped muscle that separates the thoracic and abdominal cavities. Its inferior surface, formed mostly by the left ventricle, is even called the diaphragmatic surface. The heart tilts so that about two thirds of its mass lies left of the midline.
notes: The sternum lies in front of the heart, with the right ventricle just behind it. Pick the sternum if the question asked which bone lies anterior to the heart.
Correct. The heart rests on the diaphragm.
The first rib is high in the thorax near the base of the neck, well above the heart. Pick it for a question about the top of the thoracic cage.
The liver lies below the diaphragm in the abdominal cavity, under the heart but separated from it by the diaphragm. Pick it for the large organ in the upper right abdomen.
questions.answerText: The diaphragm

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: The term myocardial infarction names the heart wall layer that dies in a heart attack. Which layer is it?
options: The endocardium
The myocardium
The epicardium
The fibrous pericardium
questions.why: Myocardial means relating to the myocardium, the thick middle layer of cardiac muscle that contracts. An infarction is an area of tissue that dies when its blood supply is cut off. In a heart attack a blocked coronary artery starves part of the myocardium of oxygen, so the pumping muscle itself is damaged.
notes: The endocardium is the thin inner lining of the chambers. Pick it for inflammation of the heart lining, called endocarditis.
Correct. A myocardial infarction is death of part of the myocardium.
The epicardium is the thin outer serous layer where the coronary vessels run. The blockage may sit in a vessel on this surface, but the tissue that dies is the muscle it supplies.
The fibrous pericardium is the tough sac around the heart, not part of the heart wall. Pick it if the question asked what anchors the heart in the mediastinum.
questions.answerText: The myocardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which layer of the heart wall lines the chambers and also covers the surfaces of the heart valves?
options: The epicardium
The myocardium
The visceral pericardium
The endocardium
questions.why: The endocardium is a smooth endothelium that lines every chamber and folds over the valve cusps, so the valves are covered by the same lining. It is continuous with the inner lining of the great vessels. A smooth, unbroken lining lets blood flow without catching or clotting.
notes: The epicardium is the outer layer of the heart wall, on the heart's surface. Pick it if the question asked about the layer where the coronary vessels run.
The myocardium is the muscular middle layer that contracts. Valve cusps contain no cardiac muscle, so pick the myocardium for the pumping layer.
The visceral pericardium is the same membrane as the epicardium, on the outside of the heart. Pick it if the question asked which serous layer covers the heart's surface.
Correct. The endocardium lines the chambers and covers the valves.
questions.answerText: The endocardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What is the smooth-walled posterior part of the right atrium, where the venae cavae empty, called?
options: The aortic vestibule
The conus arteriosus
The sinus venarum
The coronary sinus
questions.why: The sinus venarum is the smooth-walled posterior part of the right atrium, where the superior and inferior venae cavae empty. Its name means the sinus of the veins. A ridge called the crista terminalis separates this smooth part from the rough, pectinate-ridged anterior wall of the atrium.
notes: The aortic vestibule is the smooth outflow tract of the left ventricle, leading to the aortic valve. Pick it for the left ventricle's exit path.
The conus arteriosus is the smooth outflow tract of the right ventricle, leading up to the pulmonary valve. Pick it if the question asked about the smooth exit path of the right ventricle.
Correct. The sinus venarum is the smooth posterior part of the right atrium that receives the venae cavae.
The coronary sinus is a vein on the posterior heart that drains the cardiac veins into the right atrium. It is a vessel, not a region of the atrial wall.
questions.answerText: The sinus venarum

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What are the irregular muscular ridges on the inner walls of the ventricles called?
options: The pectinate muscles
The papillary muscles
The trabeculae carneae
The chordae tendineae
questions.why: The trabeculae carneae are the irregular, criss-crossing muscular ridges on the inner walls of both ventricles. The name means little beams of flesh, which describes their rough, beam-like look. They are different from the papillary muscles, which are larger cone-shaped projections that anchor the valve cords.
notes: The pectinate muscles are parallel ridges found in the atria and auricles, not the ventricles. Pick them if the question asked about the ridges inside the atria.
The papillary muscles are cone-shaped projections in the ventricles that anchor the chordae tendineae. They are in the same chamber, but pick them for the structures that hold the valve cords.
Correct. The trabeculae carneae are the irregular ridges on the inner ventricle walls.
The chordae tendineae are fibrous cords, not muscle ridges, that tie the atrioventricular valve cusps to the papillary muscles. Pick them for the cords that hold the valves.
questions.answerText: The trabeculae carneae

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which wall separates the two atria and contains the fossa ovalis?
options: The interventricular septum
The fibrous pericardium
The crista terminalis
The interatrial septum
questions.why: The interatrial septum is the thin wall between the right and left atria. On its right atrial side is the fossa ovalis, an oval depression that marks where the fetal foramen ovale once let blood pass between the atria. The interatrial septum is much thinner than the muscular interventricular septum below it.
notes: The interventricular septum is the thick wall between the two ventricles. Pick it if the question asked about the wall separating the right and left ventricles.
The fibrous pericardium is the tough outer sac around the heart. Pick it for the layer that anchors the heart in the mediastinum.
The crista terminalis is a ridge inside the right atrium that separates its smooth posterior wall from its rough anterior wall. It is a ridge within one atrium, not the wall between the two.
Correct. The interatrial septum divides the atria and contains the fossa ovalis.
questions.answerText: The interatrial septum

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which layer of the serous pericardium lines the inner surface of the fibrous pericardium?
options: The parietal layer
The epicardium
The endocardium
The visceral layer
questions.why: The serous pericardium has two layers. The parietal layer lines the inside of the fibrous pericardium, and the visceral layer covers the heart's surface. Parietal refers to a wall and visceral refers to an organ, and the same naming pattern is used for the pleura around the lungs and the peritoneum in the abdomen.
notes: Correct. The parietal layer lines the inner surface of the fibrous pericardium.
The epicardium is another name for the visceral layer, on the surface of the heart. Pick it for the outermost layer of the heart wall.
The endocardium is the inner lining of the heart chambers, not part of the pericardium. Pick it if the question asked what lines the inside of the heart.
The visceral layer lies directly on the heart's surface, not on the fibrous sac. Pick it if the question asked which serous layer covers the heart.
questions.answerText: The parietal layer

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Fluid builds up in the pericardial cavity and squeezes the heart from outside, so it cannot fill properly. What is this condition called?
options: Cardiac tamponade
Pleural effusion
Myocardial infarction
Mitral valve prolapse
questions.why: The pericardial cavity normally holds only a thin film of fluid. Because the fibrous pericardium around it does not stretch, extra fluid or blood in that space presses inward on the heart. This compression is cardiac tamponade, and it limits how much the chambers can fill between beats.
notes: Correct. Fluid in the pericardial cavity squeezing the heart is cardiac tamponade.
A pleural effusion is fluid collecting in the pleural cavity around a lung. It compresses the lung rather than the heart, so pick it for fluid around a lung.
A myocardial infarction is death of heart muscle from a blocked coronary artery. Pick it for a heart attack, not for fluid around the heart.
Mitral valve prolapse is when the mitral valve cusps bulge back into the left atrium as the ventricle contracts. Pick it for a valve problem, not outside compression of the heart.
questions.answerText: Cardiac tamponade

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: The wall of the left ventricle is much thicker than the wall of the right ventricle. Why does this difference make sense?
options: The left ventricle holds a much larger volume of blood than the right
It must push blood through the whole body at higher pressure
The left ventricle pumps blood to the lungs, which are farther from the heart
The left ventricle carries oxygen-rich blood, which is heavier to move
questions.why: The right ventricle only has to send blood a short distance through the low-pressure pulmonary circuit. The left ventricle must drive blood through the whole systemic circuit, from the head to the toes, which requires much higher pressure. Producing that pressure takes more muscle, so the left ventricle has the thickest wall even though both ventricles pump about the same volume with each beat.
notes: Both ventricles pump about the same volume of blood with each beat, since whatever goes through the lungs must come back to the body. The difference is pressure, not volume.
Correct. The left ventricle needs more muscle to generate the high pressure of the systemic circuit.
This reverses the two ventricles. The right ventricle pumps to the lungs, which are close to the heart, and the left ventricle pumps to the body.
Oxygen-rich blood is not meaningfully heavier than oxygen-poor blood. This is a misconception, since the wall thickness comes from the pressure each circuit requires.
questions.answerText: It must push blood through the whole body at higher pressure

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: A thin film of serous fluid fills the pericardial cavity. What does this fluid do during every heartbeat?
options: It stores extra blood for the next beat
It supplies oxygen to the outer layers of the heart wall
It reduces friction as the serous layers slide
It keeps the heart from overfilling with blood
questions.why: The heart moves with every beat, roughly a hundred thousand times a day, and its surface would rub against the sac around it. The serous fluid in the pericardial cavity lets the visceral and parietal layers slide smoothly over each other with very little friction. The same idea applies to the pleural fluid around the lungs and the peritoneal fluid in the abdomen.
notes: Blood for the next beat is held in the chambers, mainly the atria, not in the pericardial cavity. Blood in the pericardial cavity is a problem that compresses the heart.
Oxygen reaches the heart wall through the coronary arteries, which run in the epicardium. Pick this for a question about the coronary circulation.
Correct. The serous fluid reduces friction as the heart beats.
Keeping the heart from overfilling is a job of the fibrous pericardium, the tough inelastic outer sac. Pick this for the fibrous pericardium, not the serous fluid.
questions.answerText: It reduces friction as the serous layers slide

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: In the adult heart, the septum completely separates the right side from the left side. Why is this full separation important?
options: It anchors the four heart valves in place
It keeps oxygen-poor and oxygen-rich blood from mixing
It mixes the two bloods so oxygen levels even out
It lets the right and left sides beat at different times
questions.why: The right side of the heart handles oxygen-poor blood on its way to the lungs, and the left side handles oxygen-rich blood on its way to the body. A complete septum keeps these two streams apart. When there is a hole in the septum, called a septal defect, the bloods can mix and the blood sent to the body carries less oxygen.
notes: The valves are anchored by the fibrous skeleton, rings of dense connective tissue around the four valve openings. Pick this for a question about the fibrous skeleton.
Correct. Full separation keeps the two bloods apart so the body gets fully oxygenated blood.
Mixing the two bloods would lower the oxygen content of blood sent to the body, which is the problem a septal defect causes. The septum exists to prevent mixing, not allow it.
The two sides of the heart contract together, not at different times. The septum is a dividing wall, not a timing device.
questions.answerText: It keeps oxygen-poor and oxygen-rich blood from mixing

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which description best defines the heart?
options: A hollow muscular organ that pumps blood
A spongy organ where blood exchanges gases
A gland that releases hormones into blood
A solid organ that filters old blood cells
questions.why: The heart is a hollow, muscular organ about the size of a closed fist. Its four chambers fill with blood, and its muscular wall (the myocardium) contracts to push that blood through the vessels. It sits in the mediastinum between the lungs and drives blood through two circuits, one to the lungs and one to the body.
notes: Correct. The heart is a hollow muscular pump for the blood.
A spongy organ where blood exchanges gases describes a lung. Pick the lungs for the organs where blood picks up O2 and releases CO2.
A gland that releases hormones into the blood is an endocrine gland, such as the thyroid. Pick that for a question about hormone-secreting organs.
A solid organ that filters old blood cells is the spleen, a lymphatic organ in the upper left abdomen. Pick the spleen for a question about removing worn out red blood cells.
questions.answerText: A hollow muscular organ that pumps blood

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which direction does the apex of the heart point?
options: Up, back, and to the right
Straight up toward the neck
Down, forward, and to the left
Down, back, and to the right
questions.why: The apex is the blunt, rounded tip of the heart, formed by the left ventricle. Because the heart sits tilted in the mediastinum, the apex points down, forward, and to the left, and about two thirds of the heart's mass lies to the left of the midline. This tilt is why the heartbeat is felt best on the left side of the chest.
notes: Up, back, and to the right is roughly the opposite of the apex. The base of the heart faces up and back, so students who mix up apex and base may pick this.
The great vessels at the base point upward toward the neck, not the apex. Pick upward for the direction the aortic arch and venae cavae lead from the base.
Correct. The apex points inferiorly, anteriorly, and to the left.
The apex points down, but toward the front and the left. Choosing the right side ignores the leftward tilt of the heart.
questions.answerText: Down, forward, and to the left

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What is the base of the heart?
options: The pointed inferior tip of the left ventricle
The broad superior surface where great vessels attach
The anterior surface lying under the sternum
The inferior surface resting on the diaphragm
questions.why: Although the word base sounds like it should be on the bottom, the base of the heart is its broad superior surface, formed mostly by the left atrium. This is where the great vessels, such as the aorta, pulmonary trunk, and venae cavae, enter and leave the heart. The apex is the opposite end, the pointed tip at the bottom.
notes: The pointed inferior tip of the left ventricle is the apex. Pick apex for the part of the heart that points down and to the left.
Correct. The base is the broad top surface where the great vessels attach.
The anterior surface under the sternum is the sternocostal surface, formed mostly by the right ventricle. Pick it for the surface facing the front of the chest.
The inferior surface resting on the diaphragm is the diaphragmatic surface, formed mostly by the left ventricle. Pick it for the surface touching the diaphragm.
questions.answerText: The broad superior surface where great vessels attach

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What double-walled sac encloses the heart?
options: The pleura
The mediastinum
The pericardium
The peritoneum
questions.why: The pericardium is the double-walled sac around the heart. Its outer fibrous layer anchors the heart and prevents overfilling, and its inner serous layer forms a fluid-filled space that lets the heart beat without friction. Peri means around and cardium means heart.
notes: The pleura is the serous membrane around each lung. Pick it for the sac that surrounds a lung in the thoracic cavity.
The mediastinum is the central region of the thoracic cavity that holds the heart, not a sac or membrane. Pick it for the space between the lungs where the heart sits.
Correct. The pericardium is the sac around the heart.
The peritoneum is the serous membrane lining the abdominopelvic cavity and covering its organs. Pick it for a membrane around the stomach or intestines.
questions.answerText: The pericardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What is the tough, inelastic outer layer of the pericardium called?
options: The endocardium
The fibrous pericardium
The visceral layer of the serous pericardium
The parietal layer of the serous pericardium
questions.why: The fibrous pericardium is the outermost layer of the pericardial sac, made of dense connective tissue. It is tough and does not stretch much, which lets it anchor the heart in the mediastinum and keep the heart from overfilling. The thinner serous pericardium lies inside it.
notes: The endocardium is the smooth inner lining of the heart chambers and valves. Pick it for the innermost layer of the heart wall, not part of the sac.
Correct. The fibrous pericardium is the tough outer layer.
The visceral layer of the serous pericardium lies on the heart surface and is also called the epicardium. Pick it for the membrane stuck to the heart itself.
The parietal layer of the serous pericardium is a thin serous membrane that lines the inside of the fibrous pericardium. Pick it for the layer directly beneath the fibrous sac.
questions.answerText: The fibrous pericardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What does the fibrous pericardium do?
options: It lines the chambers with a smooth surface
It covers the heart with a fat-filled surface
It contracts to pump blood out
It anchors the heart and prevents overfilling
questions.why: The fibrous pericardium is made of dense, inelastic connective tissue. Because it is tough and attached to surrounding structures, it holds the heart in place in the mediastinum. Because it does not stretch much, it also keeps the heart from overfilling with blood.
notes: Lining the chambers with a smooth surface is the job of the endocardium. Pick it for the innermost layer that blood flows across.
The surface layer with fat and coronary vessels is the epicardium, the visceral layer of the serous pericardium. Pick it for the outer layer of the heart wall.
Contracting to pump blood is the job of the myocardium, the cardiac muscle layer. Pick it for the layer that generates force.
Correct. The fibrous pericardium anchors the heart and limits overfilling.
questions.answerText: It anchors the heart and prevents overfilling

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What are the two layers of the serous pericardium?
options: The myocardium and endocardium
The fibrous and serous layers
The epicardium and endocardium
The parietal and visceral layers
questions.why: The serous pericardium is a thin double membrane. Its parietal layer lines the inside of the fibrous pericardium, and its visceral layer lies directly on the heart surface, where it is also called the epicardium. The pericardial cavity, a thin space filled with serous fluid, lies between these two layers.
notes: The myocardium and endocardium are the middle and inner layers of the heart wall. Pick them for the muscle layer and lining of the heart itself.
Fibrous and serous are the two main parts of the whole pericardium, not the two layers of the serous part. Pick this pair if the question asks for the two parts of the pericardial sac.
The epicardium is the visceral layer, but the endocardium lines the chambers and is not part of the pericardium. This choice mixes one correct layer with an unrelated one.
Correct. The serous pericardium has a parietal layer and a visceral layer.
questions.answerText: The parietal and visceral layers

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which layer of the serous pericardium lies directly on the heart surface?
options: The visceral layer
The endocardial layer
The fibrous layer
The parietal layer
questions.why: In any serous membrane, the visceral layer covers the organ itself and the parietal layer lines the cavity wall. The visceral layer of the serous pericardium clings to the heart surface and is the same membrane as the epicardium, the outer layer of the heart wall. Viscus means organ, which is a useful way to remember it.
notes: Correct. The visceral layer lies on the heart and is also called the epicardium.
The endocardium lines the inside of the heart chambers, not the outer surface. Pick it for the innermost layer of the heart wall.
The fibrous pericardium is the tough outer sac and is not part of the serous pericardium. Pick it for the layer that anchors the heart.
The parietal layer lines the inside of the fibrous pericardium, away from the heart surface. Pick it for the serous layer on the sac side of the pericardial cavity.
questions.answerText: The visceral layer

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which layer of the serous pericardium lines the inside of the fibrous pericardium?
options: The epicardium
The visceral layer
The myocardium
The parietal layer
questions.why: The parietal layer of the serous pericardium is fused to the inner surface of the fibrous pericardium. Parietal means wall, so this layer lines the wall of the sac. It faces the visceral layer across the pericardial cavity.
notes: The epicardium is another name for the visceral layer, which sits on the heart surface. Pick it for the outer layer of the heart wall.
The visceral layer lies on the heart surface, on the opposite side of the pericardial cavity. Pick it for the layer that clings to the heart.
The myocardium is the cardiac muscle layer of the heart wall, deep to the epicardium. Pick it for the layer that contracts.
Correct. The parietal layer lines the fibrous pericardium.
questions.answerText: The parietal layer

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Where is the pericardial cavity?
options: Between the parietal and visceral serous layers
Between the two pleural layers of each lung
Between the myocardium and the endocardium
Inside the four chambers of the heart
questions.why: The pericardial cavity is a thin space between the parietal layer, which lines the fibrous sac, and the visceral layer, which covers the heart. It holds a film of serous fluid that lets the two layers slide over each other as the heart beats. It is a potential space, so normally it holds only a small amount of fluid.
notes: Correct. The pericardial cavity lies between the parietal and visceral layers.
The space between the two pleural layers is the pleural cavity around a lung. Pick it for the fluid-filled space surrounding each lung.
The myocardium and endocardium are layers of the heart wall that are attached to each other with no cavity between. Pick them for the middle and inner layers of the wall.
The chambers are the hollow interior of the heart, where blood flows. They are separated from the pericardial cavity by the entire heart wall.
questions.answerText: Between the parietal and visceral serous layers

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What fluid reduces friction as the heart beats?
options: Cerebrospinal fluid
Synovial fluid
Lymph
Serous fluid
questions.why: The serous layers of the pericardium secrete a thin film of serous fluid into the pericardial cavity. This fluid lets the visceral layer on the heart slide smoothly against the parietal layer each time the heart contracts and relaxes. The same kind of fluid reduces friction around the lungs and abdominal organs.
notes: Cerebrospinal fluid surrounds and cushions the brain and spinal cord. Pick it for the fluid in the subarachnoid space and ventricles.
Synovial fluid lubricates freely movable joints such as the knee and shoulder. Pick it for the fluid inside a joint cavity.
Lymph is the fluid carried in lymphatic vessels back to the veins. Pick it for fluid collected from the tissues.
Correct. Serous fluid in the pericardial cavity reduces friction.
questions.answerText: Serous fluid

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which list gives the three layers of the heart wall in order from outside to inside?
options: Epicardium, endocardium, myocardium
Epicardium, myocardium, endocardium
Myocardium, epicardium, endocardium
Endocardium, myocardium, epicardium
questions.why: The epicardium (epi means upon) is the thin outer layer on the heart surface. The myocardium (myo means muscle) is the thick middle layer of cardiac muscle that contracts. The endocardium (endo means within) is the smooth inner lining of the chambers and valves.
notes: The endocardium is the innermost layer and cannot sit between the other two. This order puts the thick muscle layer on the inside where the lining should be.
Correct. Epicardium, then myocardium, then endocardium.
The myocardium is the middle layer, not the outer one. Students who think of the muscle as the main part of the heart may put it first.
This list runs from inside to outside, the reverse of what was asked. It would be correct if the question asked for the order from the chambers outward.
questions.answerText: Epicardium, myocardium, endocardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What is the outer layer of the heart wall?
options: The fibrous pericardium
The endocardium
The epicardium
The myocardium
questions.why: The epicardium is the thin serous membrane on the outer surface of the heart wall. It is the same membrane as the visceral layer of the serous pericardium, and fat and the coronary vessels run within it. The fibrous pericardium lies outside it but belongs to the sac, not the heart wall.
notes: The fibrous pericardium is the outer layer of the sac around the heart, not part of the heart wall. Pick it for the tough layer anchoring the heart in the mediastinum.
The endocardium is the inner lining of the chambers and valves. Pick it for the innermost layer.
Correct. The epicardium is the outer layer of the heart wall.
The myocardium is the thick middle muscle layer. Pick it for the layer that contracts.
questions.answerText: The epicardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What is the thick middle layer of the heart wall?
options: The epicardium
The myocardium
The endocardium
The pericardium
questions.why: The myocardium is the thick middle layer of the heart wall, built of cardiac muscle in spiraling bundles. It makes up about ninety five percent of the wall thickness and is the layer that contracts to pump blood. Its thickness varies by chamber, and it is thickest in the left ventricle.
notes: The epicardium is the thin outer layer on the heart surface. Pick it for the layer carrying the coronary vessels and fat.
Correct. The myocardium is the thick middle muscle layer.
The endocardium is the thin inner lining of the chambers. Pick it for the smooth surface that blood touches.
The pericardium is the sac around the heart, outside the heart wall. Pick it for the double-walled membrane that encloses the heart.
questions.answerText: The myocardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What is the inner layer of the heart wall?
options: The endocardium
The visceral pericardium
The myocardium
The epicardium
questions.why: The endocardium is a smooth endothelium (a thin sheet of flat cells) that lines the inside of all four chambers and covers the valves. It is continuous with the inner lining of the great vessels. Its smoothness lets blood flow across it without catching.
notes: Correct. The endocardium is the innermost layer of the heart wall.
The visceral pericardium is another name for the epicardium, the outer layer. Students sometimes pick it because visceral sounds like it means inner.
The myocardium is the thick middle layer of cardiac muscle. Pick it for the contracting layer.
The epicardium is the outer layer on the heart surface. Pick it for the outermost layer of the wall.
questions.answerText: The endocardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which layer of the heart wall is made of cardiac muscle?
options: The fibrous pericardium
The myocardium
The endocardium
The epicardium
questions.why: The myocardium is the layer of cardiac muscle in the heart wall. Its cells are short, branched, striated, and joined end to end by intercalated discs, which let the whole heart contract as a coordinated unit. The other layers are thin membranes or connective tissue.
notes: The fibrous pericardium is dense connective tissue forming the outer sac. Pick it for the tough layer that anchors the heart.
Correct. The myocardium is the cardiac muscle layer.
The endocardium is a thin endothelium lining the chambers and valves. Pick it for the smooth inner surface, not the muscle.
The epicardium is a thin serous membrane on the heart surface. Pick it for the outer layer where the coronary vessels run.
questions.answerText: The myocardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which layer of the heart wall lines the chambers?
options: The epicardium
The parietal pericardium
The endocardium
The myocardium
questions.why: The endocardium lines the inner surface of all four chambers. It is a smooth endothelium resting on a thin layer of connective tissue, and it gives blood a slick surface to flow across. It also covers the valves and continues into the lining of the great vessels.
notes: The epicardium covers the outer surface of the heart. Pick it for the outermost layer of the wall.
The parietal pericardium lines the fibrous sac outside the heart. Pick it for the serous layer facing the pericardial cavity from the sac side.
Correct. The endocardium lines the chambers.
The myocardium lies just outside the endocardium and forms the muscle of the chamber walls. Pick it for the layer that contracts.
questions.answerText: The endocardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which layer of the heart wall covers the surfaces of the valves?
options: The myocardium
The fibrous skeleton
The endocardium
The epicardium
questions.why: The valve cusps are folds of tissue covered on both surfaces by endocardium, the same smooth lining that covers the chambers. This smooth covering lets blood pass over the valves without catching. Because the valves are covered by endocardium, infection of the valves is a form of endocarditis.
notes: The myocardium is muscle and does not extend into the valve cusps. Valves open and close passively, so pick the myocardium only for the chamber walls that contract.
The fibrous skeleton is the set of dense connective tissue rings around the valve openings. It anchors the valves but does not cover their surfaces, so pick it for what holds the valves in place.
Correct. The endocardium covers the valves as well as lining the chambers.
The epicardium covers the outer surface of the heart, far from the valves inside. Pick it for the outer layer of the wall.
questions.answerText: The endocardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: The epicardium is the visceral layer of which membrane?
options: The serous pericardium
The peritoneum
The visceral pleura
The fibrous pericardium
questions.why: The epicardium and the visceral layer of the serous pericardium are the same membrane under two names. You call it the epicardium when describing the heart wall and the visceral serous pericardium when describing the sac. It faces the parietal layer across the pericardial cavity.
notes: Correct. The epicardium is the visceral layer of the serous pericardium.
The peritoneum is the serous membrane of the abdominopelvic cavity. Its visceral layer covers abdominal organs such as the stomach, not the heart.
The visceral pleura covers the surface of a lung, not the heart. Pick it for the membrane stuck to the lung surface.
The fibrous pericardium is a single tough layer of dense connective tissue with no visceral layer. Pick it for the outer sac that anchors the heart.
questions.answerText: The serous pericardium

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which two chambers are the receiving chambers of the heart?
options: The right atrium and right ventricle
The left atrium and left ventricle
The right and left atria
The right and left ventricles
questions.why: The two atria are the receiving chambers. The right atrium receives oxygen-poor blood returning from the body, and the left atrium receives oxygen-rich blood returning from the lungs. Their walls are thin because they only push blood a short distance into the ventricles below.
notes: These two chambers make up the right side of the heart, one receiving and one pumping. Pick this pair for the side that drives the pulmonary circuit.
These two chambers make up the left side of the heart, one receiving and one pumping. Pick this pair for the side that drives the systemic circuit.
Correct. The two atria receive blood returning to the heart.
The ventricles are the pumping chambers that send blood out of the heart. Pick them for the chambers that push blood into the pulmonary trunk and aorta.
questions.answerText: The right and left atria

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which two chambers are the pumping chambers of the heart?
options: The right and left atria
The right and left ventricles
The right atrium and right ventricle
The left atrium and left ventricle
questions.why: The two ventricles are the pumping chambers that send blood out of the heart. The right ventricle pumps into the pulmonary trunk toward the lungs, and the left ventricle pumps into the aorta toward the body. Their walls are much thicker than the atrial walls because they must push blood through an entire circuit.
notes: The atria are the receiving chambers. Pick them for the chambers that collect blood returning from the body and lungs.
Correct. The ventricles pump blood out of the heart.
This pair is the whole right side of the heart. Pick it for the side that drives the pulmonary circuit.
This pair is the whole left side of the heart. Pick it for the side that drives the systemic circuit.
questions.answerText: The right and left ventricles

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which chamber of the heart has the thickest wall?
options: The left ventricle
The left atrium
The right atrium
The right ventricle
questions.why: The left ventricle has the thickest myocardium of the four chambers because it pumps blood through the systemic circuit to the entire body. The right ventricle only pumps to the nearby lungs, so its wall is thinner. The atria have the thinnest walls because they push blood only into the ventricles below.
notes: Correct. The left ventricle has the thickest wall.
The left atrium is a thin-walled receiving chamber. Pick it for the chamber receiving blood from the pulmonary veins.
The right atrium is a thin-walled receiving chamber. Pick it for the chamber where the venae cavae and coronary sinus empty.
The right ventricle has a thicker wall than either atrium but a much thinner wall than the left ventricle. Pick it for the chamber that pumps to the lungs.
questions.answerText: The left ventricle

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which wall separates the two atria?
options: The coronary sulcus
The interatrial septum
The interventricular septum
The fibrous pericardium
questions.why: The interatrial septum is the thin wall between the right and left atria. Inter means between, so the name says it sits between the atria. It holds the fossa ovalis, the remnant of the fetal opening that once let blood pass from the right atrium to the left.
notes: The coronary sulcus is a groove on the outside of the heart that marks the boundary between the atria and the ventricles. Pick it for the external groove where the coronary sinus runs.
Correct. The interatrial septum separates the two atria.
The interventricular septum is the thick wall between the two ventricles. Pick it for the wall separating the pumping chambers.
The fibrous pericardium is the outer sac around the heart, not a wall inside it. Pick it for the tough layer anchoring the heart in the mediastinum.
questions.answerText: The interatrial septum

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which wall separates the two ventricles?
options: The coronary sulcus
The interatrial septum
The moderator band
The interventricular septum
questions.why: The interventricular septum is the thick muscular wall between the right and left ventricles. It keeps oxygen-poor blood on the right side from mixing with oxygen-rich blood on the left. On the surface of the heart, its position is marked by the anterior and posterior interventricular grooves.
notes: The coronary sulcus is an external groove marking the boundary between the atria and the ventricles. Pick it for the groove that encircles the heart.
The interatrial septum is the thin wall between the two atria. Pick it for the wall that holds the fossa ovalis.
The moderator band is a muscular band that crosses the right ventricle from the septum to the anterior papillary muscle. It attaches to the septum but does not separate the chambers.
Correct. The interventricular septum separates the ventricles.
questions.answerText: The interventricular septum

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What is the fossa ovalis?
options: An oval depression in the interatrial septum
A small wrinkled pouch on each atrium
A smooth outflow tract leading to the pulmonary valve
A muscular band crossing the right ventricle
questions.why: The fossa ovalis is a shallow oval depression in the interatrial septum, seen from inside the right atrium. Fossa means a shallow pit. It marks the site of the foramen ovale, an opening that let blood pass between the atria before birth and then sealed shut.
notes: Correct. The fossa ovalis is an oval depression in the interatrial septum.
A small wrinkled pouch on each atrium is an auricle. Pick it for the ear-shaped flap that slightly increases atrial capacity.
A smooth outflow tract leading to the pulmonary valve is the conus arteriosus of the right ventricle. Pick it for the smooth funnel below the pulmonary trunk.
A muscular band crossing the right ventricle is the moderator band. Pick it for the structure carrying conduction fibers to the anterior papillary muscle.
questions.answerText: An oval depression in the interatrial septum

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What is the small, wrinkled, ear-shaped pouch that projects from each atrium?
options: A fossa ovalis
A papillary muscle
A coronary sinus
An auricle
questions.why: Each atrium has an auricle, a small wrinkled pouch named for its resemblance to an ear (auricle means little ear). The auricles are visible on the anterior surface of the heart beside the great vessels. Their inner walls are lined with pectinate muscles, and they slightly increase how much blood each atrium can hold.
notes: The fossa ovalis is an oval depression in the interatrial septum, seen inside the right atrium. Pick it for the remnant of the foramen ovale.
A papillary muscle is a cone-shaped projection of the ventricle wall that anchors the chordae tendineae. Pick it for the muscle that holds the AV valves shut.
The coronary sinus is a large vein on the posterior heart that drains into the right atrium. Pick it for the vessel collecting the cardiac veins.
Correct. The auricle is the ear-shaped pouch on each atrium.
questions.answerText: An auricle

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What do the auricles do?
options: Anchor the chordae tendineae
Separate the atria from the ventricles
Drain blood from the heart wall
Slightly increase atrial capacity
questions.why: The auricles are small pouches that extend from the atria. They add a little extra room to each atrium, so the atria can hold slightly more blood before it passes into the ventricles. Their inner walls have the same parallel pectinate muscles found in the atria.
notes: Anchoring the chordae tendineae is the job of the papillary muscles in the ventricles. Pick papillary muscles for that role.
Separating the atria from the ventricles is the job of the fibrous skeleton and the AV valves. Pick the fibrous skeleton for the connective tissue that insulates atria from ventricles.
Draining blood from the heart wall is the job of the cardiac veins and coronary sinus. Pick the coronary sinus for the vessel emptying that blood into the right atrium.
Correct. The auricles slightly increase the capacity of the atria.
questions.answerText: Slightly increase atrial capacity

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which structures are parallel muscular ridges on the inner walls of the atria and auricles?
options: Papillary muscles
Chordae tendineae
Pectinate muscles
Trabeculae carneae
questions.why: Pectinate muscles are parallel ridges of muscle on the inner walls of the atria and auricles. Pectinate means comb-like, because the ridges line up like the teeth of a comb. In the right atrium, a ridge called the crista terminalis separates the rough pectinate wall from the smooth posterior wall.
notes: Papillary muscles are cone-shaped projections in the ventricles that anchor the chordae tendineae. Pick them for the muscles holding the AV valves shut.
Chordae tendineae are fibrous cords, not muscle ridges, linking AV valve cusps to papillary muscles. Pick them for the heart strings attached to the valves.
Correct. Pectinate muscles are the comb-like ridges in the atria and auricles.
Trabeculae carneae are irregular muscular ridges on the inner walls of the ventricles, not the atria. Pick them for the rough ridges inside a ventricle.
questions.answerText: Pectinate muscles

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which structures are irregular muscular ridges on the inner walls of the ventricles?
options: Pectinate muscles
Chordae tendineae
Crista terminalis
Trabeculae carneae
questions.why: Trabeculae carneae are irregular, crisscrossing ridges of muscle on the inner walls of both ventricles. The name means little beams of flesh. They give the ventricle walls a rough inner texture, unlike the parallel comb-like pectinate muscles of the atria.
notes: Pectinate muscles are parallel ridges in the atria and auricles. Pick them for the comb-like ridges of the receiving chambers.
Chordae tendineae are fibrous cords, not muscle ridges, that tie AV valve cusps to papillary muscles. Pick them for the heart strings.
The crista terminalis is a single ridge in the right atrium separating its smooth and rough walls. Pick it for that one atrial landmark.
Correct. Trabeculae carneae are the irregular ridges inside the ventricles.
questions.answerText: Trabeculae carneae

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which structure is a muscular band that crosses the right ventricle from the interventricular septum to the base of the anterior papillary muscle?
options: The moderator band
The chordae tendineae
The crista terminalis
The pectinate muscles
questions.why: The moderator band, also called the septomarginal trabecula, is a muscular band found in the right ventricle. It runs from the interventricular septum across the chamber to the base of the anterior papillary muscle. It carries part of the conduction system, which helps the papillary muscle contract on time.
notes: Correct. The moderator band crosses the right ventricle to the anterior papillary muscle.
Chordae tendineae are thin fibrous cords running from papillary muscles to the AV valve cusps. Pick them for the cords attached to the valves, not a muscle band from the septum.
The crista terminalis is a ridge in the right atrium, not the ventricle. Pick it for the ridge separating the smooth and rough parts of the right atrial wall.
Pectinate muscles are parallel ridges in the atria and auricles. Pick them for the comb-like ridges of the atrial walls.
questions.answerText: The moderator band

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the atria and the ventricles?
options: Atria and ventricles both pump blood out of the heart
Atria pump blood out, and ventricles receive returning blood
Atria have thicker walls because they hold more blood
Atria receive returning blood, and ventricles pump it out
questions.why: The atria are the receiving chambers: blood returning from the body or lungs enters them first. The ventricles are the pumping chambers that push blood out into the pulmonary trunk and aorta. This difference in job explains why the ventricles have much thicker walls than the atria.
notes: Only the ventricles push blood out of the heart into the great arteries. The atria push blood only a short distance into the ventricles.
This reverses the two roles. Blood enters the atria from veins and leaves the ventricles through arteries, so pick this only if you have the chambers flipped.
Atria have thinner walls, not thicker, because they do little pumping. Pick the ventricles, especially the left, for the thickest walls.
Correct. Atria receive blood, and ventricles pump it out of the heart.
questions.answerText: Atria receive returning blood, and ventricles pump it out

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Why is the wall of the left ventricle thicker than the wall of the right ventricle?
options: It receives more blood than the right ventricle
It pumps blood through the systemic circuit to the whole body
It must push blood up into the left atrium
It holds the coronary sinus within its wall
questions.why: The left ventricle pumps blood into the aorta and through the systemic circuit, which reaches every tissue of the body. Pushing blood through such a long, branching circuit takes much more force than pushing it to the nearby lungs. Thicker myocardium gives the left ventricle that extra force.
notes: Both ventricles pump about the same volume of blood with each beat. The difference is how hard each must push, not how much blood each receives.
Correct. The long systemic circuit requires a thicker, stronger wall.
Blood moves from the left atrium down into the left ventricle, not the other way. Pushing blood back into an atrium would be backflow, which the mitral valve prevents.
The coronary sinus lies in the groove on the posterior surface of the heart and empties into the right atrium. It does not explain wall thickness.
questions.answerText: It pumps blood through the systemic circuit to the whole body

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Why can the right ventricle have a thinner wall than the left ventricle?
options: It receives oxygen-rich blood that is easier to move
It pumps less blood with each beat
Its valves do most of the pumping work
It only pumps blood to the nearby lungs
questions.why: The right ventricle drives the pulmonary circuit, a short loop to the lungs right beside the heart. Moving blood through this short circuit takes less force than pushing it through the whole body. So the right ventricle needs a thinner wall, and in cross section it wraps around the thicker left ventricle in a crescent shape.
notes: The right ventricle carries oxygen-poor blood, not oxygen-rich. Oxygen content also does not change how hard blood is to move.
Both ventricles eject about the same volume with each beat. Choosing this confuses volume with the force needed to move it.
Valves only open and close to keep flow one-way. They do no pumping, so the myocardium does all the work.
Correct. The short pulmonary circuit needs less force.
questions.answerText: It only pumps blood to the nearby lungs

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the apex and the base of the heart?
options: The apex and the base are both formed by the right ventricle
The apex holds the great vessels, and the base rests on the diaphragm
The apex is the inferior tip, and the base is the superior surface
The apex is the superior surface, and the base is the inferior tip
questions.why: The apex is the pointed inferior tip of the heart, formed by the left ventricle and pointing down, forward, and to the left. The base is the broad superior surface, formed mostly by the left atrium, where the great vessels enter and leave. The names are opposite to what many students expect, since the base sits on top.
notes: The apex is formed by the left ventricle, and the base mostly by the left atrium. The right ventricle forms most of the anterior surface instead.
The great vessels attach at the base, not the apex. The surface resting on the diaphragm is the inferior surface, formed mostly by the left ventricle.
Correct. The apex is the inferior tip and the base is the superior surface.
This reverses the two. Students often assume the base must be at the bottom, but in the heart it is the top surface.
questions.answerText: The apex is the inferior tip, and the base is the superior surface

questions.topic: Heart: pericardium, wall, chambers and surface features
questions.q: What is the main job of the fluid-filled pericardial cavity?
options: It stores extra blood for the ventricles
It supplies oxygen to the heart wall
It lets the heart beat with little friction
It anchors the heart to the diaphragm
questions.why: The pericardial cavity holds a thin film of serous fluid between the parietal and visceral layers of the serous pericardium. As the heart contracts and relaxes, the two layers slide past each other on this fluid with very little friction. Without it, the beating heart would rub against its sac.
notes: The pericardial cavity holds only a thin film of fluid, never blood. Blood is stored in the chambers, and fluid or blood filling this space is a dangerous condition called cardiac tamponade.
Oxygen reaches the heart wall through the coronary arteries. Pick them for the heart's own blood supply.
Correct. The serous fluid lets the layers glide as the heart beats.
