notes: This pair mixes an atrioventricular valve, the mitral, with a semilunar valve, the aortic. It would fit a question about the two valves of the left ventricle.
The tricuspid and mitral valves are the atrioventricular valves, which do have chordae tendineae and papillary muscles. Pick this pair if the question asked which valves are held shut by cords.
This pair mixes an atrioventricular valve, the tricuspid, with a semilunar valve, the pulmonary. It would fit a question about the two valves of the right ventricle.
Correct. The semilunar valves have pocket-shaped cusps and no chordae tendineae.
questions.answerText: The pulmonary and aortic valves

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: The mitral valve is also known by which other name?
options: The tricuspid valve
The pulmonary semilunar valve
The aortic semilunar valve
The bicuspid valve
questions.why: The mitral valve is the left atrioventricular valve, and it has two cusps, so it is also called the bicuspid valve. The name mitral comes from its resemblance to a bishop's mitre, a two-pointed hat. It is the only heart valve with two cusps, which is a handy way to tell it apart from the other three.
notes: The tricuspid valve is the right atrioventricular valve, with three cusps. Pick it for the valve between the right atrium and right ventricle.
The pulmonary semilunar valve guards the exit of the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk. Pick it for the right ventricle's outflow.
The aortic semilunar valve guards the exit of the left ventricle into the aorta. It is on the same side of the heart as the mitral valve but at the outflow, so pick it for the left ventricle's exit.
Correct. The mitral valve is also called the bicuspid valve because it has two cusps.
questions.answerText: The bicuspid valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: When the right ventricle contracts, which valve closes to keep blood from flowing back into the right atrium?
options: The mitral valve
The tricuspid valve
The aortic valve
The pulmonary valve
questions.why: The tricuspid valve sits between the right atrium and right ventricle. When the right ventricle contracts, rising pressure pushes the three cusps together, and the chordae tendineae keep them from flipping back. This seals the opening so blood leaves through the pulmonary valve instead of returning to the right atrium.
notes: The mitral valve prevents backflow into the left atrium when the left ventricle contracts. Pick it for the left side.
Correct. The tricuspid valve closes to stop backflow into the right atrium.
The aortic valve guards the exit of the left ventricle. Pick it for backflow from the aorta into the left ventricle.

The pulmonary valve opens when the right ventricle contracts, letting blood into the pulmonary trunk. It closes afterward to prevent backflow into the right ventricle, so pick it for backflow from the pulmonary trunk.
questions.answerText: The tricuspid valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Starting in the right atrium, which three structures does blood pass through next, in order?
options: The tricuspid valve, the right ventricle, then the pulmonary valve
The tricuspid valve, the right ventricle, then the aortic valve
The pulmonary valve, the right ventricle, then the tricuspid valve
The mitral valve, the right ventricle, then the pulmonary valve
questions.why: From the right atrium, blood drops through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle. The right ventricle then contracts and pushes the blood up through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk. Each side of the heart follows the same pattern: atrium, atrioventricular valve, ventricle, semilunar valve.
notes: Correct. Blood passes the tricuspid valve, the right ventricle, and then the pulmonary valve.
The first two steps are right, but the aortic valve is on the left side, at the exit of the left ventricle. The right ventricle's exit valve is the pulmonary valve.
This order runs backward, putting the exit valve first and the entry valve last. Blood enters the right ventricle through the tricuspid valve and leaves through the pulmonary valve.
The mitral valve is the left atrioventricular valve, between the left atrium and left ventricle. The valve between the right atrium and right ventricle is the tricuspid.
questions.answerText: The tricuspid valve, the right ventricle, then the pulmonary valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: After blood leaves the lungs, which three heart structures does it pass through, in order, before reaching the aortic valve?
options: The left ventricle, the mitral valve, then the left atrium
The left atrium, the mitral valve, then the left ventricle
The right atrium, the tricuspid valve, then the right ventricle
The left atrium, the tricuspid valve, then the left ventricle
questions.why: Blood returning from the lungs through the pulmonary veins enters the left atrium. It then passes through the mitral valve into the left ventricle, which contracts and pushes it through the aortic valve into the aorta. This is the left-side version of the atrium, valve, ventricle pattern.
notes: This order runs backward. Blood fills the atrium first and then drops into the ventricle, so the left atrium must come before the left ventricle.
Correct. After the lungs, blood passes the left atrium, the mitral valve, and the left ventricle.
This is the sequence for blood returning from the body, on the right side of the heart. Pick it if the question started with blood arriving through the venae cavae.
The chambers are right, but the tricuspid valve is on the right side of the heart. The valve between the left atrium and left ventricle is the mitral valve.
questions.answerText: The left atrium, the mitral valve, then the left ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which sequence correctly traces blood from the right ventricle to the left atrium?
options: Aortic valve, aorta, lungs, pulmonary veins, left atrium
Pulmonary valve, pulmonary trunk, lungs, venae cavae, left atrium
Pulmonary valve, pulmonary trunk, lungs, pulmonary veins, left atrium
Tricuspid valve, pulmonary trunk, lungs, pulmonary veins, left atrium
questions.why: This route is the pulmonary circuit. Blood leaves the right ventricle through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk, travels in the pulmonary arteries to the lungs, picks up oxygen, and returns through the pulmonary veins to the left atrium. Everything in this loop carries the word pulmonary, which makes it easier to trace.
notes: The aortic valve and aorta carry blood out of the left ventricle to the body, not to the lungs. Pick this start for blood leaving the left ventricle on the systemic circuit.
The venae cavae return blood from the body to the right atrium, not from the lungs to the left atrium. Blood from the lungs returns through the pulmonary veins.
Correct. This is the pulmonary circuit from the right ventricle to the left atrium.
The tricuspid valve is the entrance to the right ventricle, not its exit. Blood leaves the right ventricle through the pulmonary valve.
questions.answerText: Pulmonary valve, pulmonary trunk, lungs, pulmonary veins, left atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which set correctly names the left ventricle's inflow valve, its outflow valve, and the great vessel it pumps into?
options: Mitral valve in, aortic valve out, into the aorta
Mitral valve in, pulmonary valve out, into the pulmonary trunk
Tricuspid valve in, pulmonary valve out, into the pulmonary trunk
Aortic valve in, mitral valve out, into the aorta
questions.why: Blood enters the left ventricle from the left atrium through the mitral valve. When the left ventricle contracts, the mitral valve closes and blood leaves through the aortic valve into the aorta. Pairing each ventricle with its inflow valve, outflow valve, and great vessel is a fast way to check any blood flow question.
notes: Correct. The left ventricle fills through the mitral valve and empties through the aortic valve into the aorta.
The inflow valve is right, but the pulmonary valve and pulmonary trunk belong to the right ventricle. The left ventricle's outflow is the aortic valve into the aorta.
This is the full set for the right ventricle. Pick it if the question asked about the right ventricle's inflow valve, outflow valve, and great vessel.
This set swaps the roles of the two valves. The mitral valve lets blood in from the left atrium, and the aortic valve lets blood out, so the order here runs backward.
questions.answerText: Mitral valve in, aortic valve out, into the aorta

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which set correctly names the right ventricle's inflow valve, its outflow valve, and the great vessel it pumps into?
options: Tricuspid valve in, pulmonary valve out, into the pulmonary trunk
Mitral valve in, aortic valve out, into the aorta
Pulmonary valve in, tricuspid valve out, into the pulmonary trunk
Tricuspid valve in, aortic valve out, into the aorta
questions.why: Blood enters the right ventricle from the right atrium through the tricuspid valve. When the right ventricle contracts, it pushes blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk, which carries it toward the lungs. Everything on the outflow side of the right ventricle is named pulmonary, which helps keep the sides apart.
notes: Correct. The right ventricle fills through the tricuspid valve and empties through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk.
This is the full set for the left ventricle. Pick it if the question asked about the left ventricle's inflow valve, outflow valve, and great vessel.
This set swaps the two valves. The tricuspid valve lets blood in from the right atrium, and the pulmonary valve lets blood out, so the order here runs backward.
The inflow valve is right, but the aortic valve and aorta belong to the left ventricle. The right ventricle sends blood to the lungs, not the body.
questions.answerText: Tricuspid valve in, pulmonary valve out, into the pulmonary trunk

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which heart valves have chordae tendineae attached to their cusps?
options: All four heart valves
Only the pulmonary and aortic valves
Only the mitral valve
Only the tricuspid and mitral valves
questions.why: Chordae tendineae belong only to the atrioventricular valves, the tricuspid and mitral. These valves face the full force of ventricular contraction and need cords and papillary muscles to keep their cusps from flipping into the atria. The semilunar valves have pocket-shaped cusps that fill with blood and close themselves, so they have no chordae.
notes: Only two of the four valves have chordae. The semilunar valves seal by filling their pocket-shaped cusps, so they need no cords.
The pulmonary and aortic valves are the semilunar valves, the two that lack chordae tendineae. Pick this pair if the question asked which valves close without cords.
The mitral valve does have chordae, but so does the tricuspid valve on the right side. Both atrioventricular valves are anchored the same way.
Correct. Only the atrioventricular valves, tricuspid and mitral, have chordae tendineae.
questions.answerText: Only the tricuspid and mitral valves

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which chamber pumps blood to the lungs through the pulmonary trunk?
options: The right ventricle
The left atrium
The right atrium
The left ventricle
questions.why: The right ventricle receives oxygen-poor blood from the right atrium and pumps it through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk. The trunk divides into the pulmonary arteries that carry the blood to the lungs. Because the lungs are close by and the pulmonary circuit is low-pressure, the right ventricle's wall is thinner than the left's.
notes: Correct. The right ventricle pumps blood into the pulmonary trunk toward the lungs.
The left atrium receives blood returning from the lungs through the pulmonary veins. Pick it for the chamber at the end of the pulmonary circuit.
The right atrium passes blood down into the right ventricle through the tricuspid valve. It is one step earlier, so pick it for the chamber that receives the venae cavae.
The left ventricle pumps blood into the aorta and out to the body. Pick it if the question asked which chamber drives the systemic circuit.
questions.answerText: The right ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which valve prevents blood in the aorta from flowing back into the left ventricle?
options: The mitral valve
The pulmonary valve
The aortic valve
The tricuspid valve
questions.why: The aortic valve is the semilunar valve between the left ventricle and the aorta. After the left ventricle contracts and relaxes, blood in the aorta tries to fall back, and that backflow fills the valve's pocket-shaped cusps and snaps them shut. Each valve guards against backflow into the chamber just behind it.
notes: The mitral valve prevents backflow from the left ventricle into the left atrium. Pick it if the question asked which valve protects the left atrium.
The pulmonary valve prevents backflow from the pulmonary trunk into the right ventricle. Pick it for the right ventricle's outflow.
Correct. The aortic valve stops backflow from the aorta into the left ventricle.
The tricuspid valve prevents backflow from the right ventricle into the right atrium. Pick it for the right atrioventricular opening.
questions.answerText: The aortic valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which circuit does the right side of the heart drive?
options: The systemic circuit
The pulmonary circuit
The coronary circulation
The hepatic portal system
questions.why: The right side of the heart receives oxygen-poor blood from the body and pumps it to the lungs and back, which is the pulmonary circuit. The left side pumps oxygen-rich blood out to the body and back, which is the systemic circuit. The two sides work side by side, so every drop of blood passes through both circuits in turn.
notes: The systemic circuit is driven by the left side of the heart, carrying blood to the body through the aorta. Pick it if the question asked about the left side.
Correct. The right side of the heart drives the pulmonary circuit to the lungs.
The coronary circulation is the heart wall's own blood supply, a branch of the systemic circuit fed by the aorta. Pick it for a question about the vessels that supply the myocardium.
The hepatic portal system carries blood from the digestive organs to the liver before it returns to the heart. Pick it for a question about blood flow through the liver.
questions.answerText: The pulmonary circuit

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: A drop of blood is being pumped out of the right ventricle. Which structure does it pass through next?
options: The tricuspid valve
The pulmonary valve
The aortic valve
The mitral valve
questions.why: When the right ventricle contracts, blood leaves through the pulmonary valve, the semilunar valve at the ventricle's exit, and enters the pulmonary trunk. From there it travels to the lungs. The pulmonary valve then closes so the blood cannot fall back into the right ventricle.
notes: The tricuspid valve is where the blood entered the right ventricle, one step earlier. It closes during contraction, so pick it for blood moving from the right atrium into the right ventricle.
Correct. Blood leaving the right ventricle passes through the pulmonary valve next.
The aortic valve is the exit of the left ventricle. The drop will reach it much later, after the lungs and the left side of the heart.
The mitral valve is between the left atrium and left ventricle. The drop reaches it after returning from the lungs, so pick it for the step after the left atrium.
questions.answerText: The pulmonary valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: A drop of blood has just returned from the lungs through the pulmonary veins. Which chamber does it enter?
options: The right atrium
The right ventricle
The left atrium
The left ventricle
questions.why: The four pulmonary veins carry oxygen-rich blood from the lungs into the left atrium. This is the end of the pulmonary circuit and the start of the left side of the heart. From the left atrium, the blood passes the mitral valve into the left ventricle.
notes: The right atrium receives oxygen-poor blood from the body through the venae cavae and the coronary sinus. Pick it for blood returning from the systemic circuit.
The right ventricle receives blood from the right atrium and pumps it toward the lungs. Pick it for the chamber that sends blood out in the pulmonary trunk.
Correct. The pulmonary veins empty into the left atrium.
The left ventricle is one step later, receiving blood from the left atrium through the mitral valve. Pick it for the chamber that pumps blood into the aorta.
questions.answerText: The left atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: A drop of blood in the right atrium moves down into the right ventricle. Which valve does it cross?
options: The mitral valve
The aortic valve
The tricuspid valve
The pulmonary valve
questions.why: Between the right atrium and right ventricle sits the tricuspid valve, the right atrioventricular valve. Blood passes through it as it drops from the atrium into the ventricle. When the ventricle then contracts, the tricuspid valve closes so the blood goes forward into the pulmonary trunk instead of back.
notes: The mitral valve is the atrioventricular valve on the left side, between the left atrium and left ventricle. Pick it for the same step on the left side of the heart.
The aortic valve is the exit of the left ventricle into the aorta. Pick it for blood leaving the left ventricle.
Correct. Blood moving from the right atrium to the right ventricle crosses the tricuspid valve.
The pulmonary valve is the exit of the right ventricle, one step later. Pick it for blood leaving the right ventricle.
questions.answerText: The tricuspid valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: The atrioventricular valves are tied to papillary muscles by chordae tendineae. Why are these cords needed when the ventricles contract forcefully?
options: They carry the electrical signal from the atria to the ventricles
They stop the cusps from flipping back into the atria
They anchor the semilunar valves to the walls of the great arteries
They pull the valve cusps open so blood can enter the ventricles
questions.why: When a ventricle contracts, the pressure inside it rises sharply and pushes the atrioventricular cusps upward toward the atrium. The chordae tendineae, held taut by the contracting papillary muscles, act like the strings of a parachute and stop the cusps from turning inside out. If a cord or papillary muscle fails, the valve leaks and blood flows back into the atrium.
notes: The signal from the atria to the ventricles travels through the conduction system, by way of the AV node and AV bundle. Pick the AV bundle for that pathway, since the chordae are passive fibrous cords.
Correct. The chordae keep the cusps from flipping into the atria under high ventricular pressure.
The semilunar valves have no chordae tendineae. Their pocket-shaped cusps close themselves when blood fills them, so this choice confuses the two kinds of valve.
The atrioventricular valves open on their own when pressure in the atrium is higher than in the ventricle. The cords hold the cusps back rather than pulling them open.
questions.answerText: They stop the cusps from flipping back into the atria

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Heart valves have no muscle of their own and are not moved by nerves. How do they still keep blood moving in only one direction?
options: Muscle within each cusp contracts to push blood forward
The valves stay open, and the order of chamber contraction sets the direction
Nerves open and close each valve in time with the heartbeat
Pressure differences push each valve open and then shut
questions.why: Valves are passive one-way gates moved by blood pressure. When pressure behind a valve is higher than pressure in front of it, blood pushes the cusps open and flows forward. When pressure reverses, the backflow catches the cusps and presses them shut, so blood cannot go the wrong way.
notes: Valve cusps are made of connective tissue covered by endocardium, with no muscle inside. The papillary muscles are in the ventricle wall and only hold the cords taut.
If the valves stayed open, blood would slosh back and forth with every contraction. Closing valves are what keep the flow one way, which is why a leaky valve causes backflow.
Nerves can change heart rate, but they do not open or close individual valves. Students who choose this are picturing valves as actively controlled doors.
Correct. Pressure differences open and close the valves, allowing only forward flow.
questions.answerText: Pressure differences push each valve open and then shut

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which circuit is driven by the right side of the heart?
options: The hepatic portal system
The pulmonary circuit
The coronary circuit
The systemic circuit
questions.why: The right side of the heart receives oxygen-poor blood from the body and pumps it through the pulmonary trunk to the lungs. That loop, from the heart to the lungs and back, is the pulmonary circuit. The left side drives the other loop, the systemic circuit to the body.
notes: The hepatic portal system carries blood from the digestive organs to the liver. Pick it for a question about blood draining the gut.
Correct. The right side pumps blood to the lungs in the pulmonary circuit.
The coronary circulation is the heart's own blood supply, which branches from the base of the aorta. Pick it for the vessels feeding the heart wall.
The systemic circuit is driven by the left side of the heart, which pumps blood into the aorta. Pick it for the left ventricle's job.
questions.answerText: The pulmonary circuit

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which circuit is driven by the left side of the heart?
options: The hepatic portal system
The systemic circuit
The pulmonary circuit
The coronary circulation
questions.why: The left side of the heart receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs and pumps it out through the aorta to every tissue of the body. That loop, from the heart to the body and back, is the systemic circuit. Because this circuit is so long, the left ventricle has the thickest wall of the four chambers.
notes: The hepatic portal system carries blood from the digestive organs to the liver before it returns to the heart. Pick it for blood draining the gut.
Correct. The left side pumps blood into the aorta for the systemic circuit.
The pulmonary circuit is driven by the right side, which pumps blood to the lungs. Pick it for the right ventricle's job.
The coronary circulation is the heart wall's own supply, running from the coronary arteries to the coronary sinus. Pick it for the vessels that feed the myocardium.
questions.answerText: The systemic circuit

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Where does the pulmonary circuit carry blood?
options: To the body tissues and back
To the heart wall and back
To the liver and back
To the lungs and back
questions.why: The pulmonary circuit carries oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle through the pulmonary trunk and pulmonary arteries to the lungs. There the blood picks up O2 and releases CO2, then returns through the pulmonary veins to the left atrium. Pulmo means lung, which is a quick way to remember this circuit.
notes: Carrying blood to the body tissues and back is the systemic circuit. Pick it for the loop that starts at the left ventricle and aorta.
Carrying blood to the heart wall and back is the coronary circulation. Pick it for the coronary arteries and cardiac veins.
Carrying blood from the gut to the liver is the hepatic portal system. Pick it for a question about nutrient-rich blood reaching the liver.
Correct. The pulmonary circuit is the loop to the lungs and back.
questions.answerText: To the lungs and back

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Where does the systemic circuit carry blood?
options: To the body tissues and back
To the lungs and back
To the atria and back
To the lymph nodes and back
questions.why: The systemic circuit begins when the left ventricle pumps oxygen-rich blood into the aorta. Branches of the aorta deliver that blood to tissues throughout the body, and oxygen-poor blood returns through the venae cavae to the right atrium. The word systemic refers to the whole body system.
notes: Correct. The systemic circuit carries blood to the body tissues and back.
Carrying blood to the lungs and back is the pulmonary circuit. Pick it for the loop driven by the right ventricle.
The atria are chambers inside the heart that receive blood from both circuits. They are not a destination of either circuit.
Lymph nodes filter lymph, not blood. Pick them for a question about where lymph is cleaned before it returns to the veins.
questions.answerText: To the body tissues and back

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which chamber receives oxygen-poor blood returning from the body?
options: The left ventricle
The right ventricle
The left atrium
The right atrium
questions.why: Oxygen-poor blood from the body returns through the superior and inferior venae cavae, and from the heart wall through the coronary sinus, into the right atrium. This is the first step of the pathway of blood through the heart. From the right atrium, blood passes through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle.
notes: The left ventricle receives blood from the left atrium and pumps it to the body. Pick it for the chamber that sends blood into the aorta.
The right ventricle receives blood from the right atrium, not directly from the body. Pick it for the chamber that pumps blood to the lungs.
The left atrium receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs through the pulmonary veins. Pick it for blood returning from the pulmonary circuit.
Correct. The right atrium receives systemic venous return.
questions.answerText: The right atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which chamber receives blood returning from the lungs?
options: The right ventricle
The right atrium
The left ventricle
The left atrium
questions.why: After picking up O2 in the lungs, blood returns through the four pulmonary veins into the left atrium. This oxygen-rich blood then passes through the mitral valve into the left ventricle. The left atrium is the receiving chamber at the end of the pulmonary circuit.
notes: The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs, not from them. Pick it for the chamber that sends blood into the pulmonary trunk.
The right atrium receives oxygen-poor blood from the body through the venae cavae. Pick it for blood returning from the systemic circuit.
The left ventricle receives blood from the left atrium, one step later. Pick it for the chamber that pumps blood into the aorta.
Correct. The left atrium receives oxygen-rich blood from the pulmonary veins.
questions.answerText: The left atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which chamber pumps blood to the lungs?
options: The left ventricle
The right atrium
The right ventricle
The left atrium
questions.why: The right ventricle contracts and pushes oxygen-poor blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk, which branches into the pulmonary arteries to the lungs. This starts the pulmonary circuit. The right ventricle receives that blood from the right atrium.
notes: The left ventricle pumps blood into the aorta for the body. Pick it for the systemic circuit.
The right atrium receives blood from the body and passes it to the right ventricle. It pushes blood only a short distance, so pick it for the chamber receiving venous return.
Correct. The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs.
The left atrium receives blood returning from the lungs. Pick it for the end of the pulmonary circuit, not its start.
questions.answerText: The right ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which chamber pumps blood to the body?
options: The right ventricle
The right atrium
The left atrium
The left ventricle
questions.why: The left ventricle contracts with force and pushes oxygen-rich blood through the aortic valve into the aorta, which carries it to the whole body. This starts the systemic circuit. Because this circuit is long, the left ventricle has the thickest wall of the four chambers.
notes: The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs through the pulmonary trunk. Pick it for the pulmonary circuit.
The right atrium receives oxygen-poor blood from the body. Pick it for the chamber where the venae cavae empty.
The left atrium receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs and passes it to the left ventricle. Pick it for the chamber receiving pulmonary venous return.
Correct. The left ventricle pumps blood to the body through the aorta.
questions.answerText: The left ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the right and left sides of the heart?
options: The right side drives the pulmonary circuit, and the left drives the systemic
Both sides pump blood into the aorta at the same time
The right side carries oxygen-rich blood, and the left carries oxygen-poor blood
The right side drives the systemic circuit, and the left drives the pulmonary
questions.why: The right side of the heart receives oxygen-poor blood from the body and pumps it to the lungs, so it drives the pulmonary circuit. The left side receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs and pumps it to the body, so it drives the systemic circuit. The heart is really two pumps side by side.
notes: Correct. Right side to lungs, left side to body.
Only the left ventricle pumps into the aorta. The right ventricle pumps into the pulmonary trunk, so the two sides send blood to different circuits.
This reverses the oxygen content. The right side carries oxygen-poor blood from the body, and the left side carries oxygen-rich blood from the lungs.
This reverses the circuits. The right ventricle feeds the pulmonary trunk, and the left ventricle feeds the aorta.
questions.answerText: The right side drives the pulmonary circuit, and the left drives the systemic

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the pulmonary and systemic circuits?
options: Pulmonary runs heart to lungs to heart, and systemic runs heart to body to heart
Pulmonary runs heart to body to heart, and systemic runs heart to lungs to heart
Pulmonary carries oxygen-rich blood away from the heart, and systemic carries oxygen-poor blood
Both circuits begin in the left ventricle and end in the right atrium
questions.why: The pulmonary circuit carries oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle to the lungs and returns oxygen-rich blood to the left atrium. The systemic circuit carries oxygen-rich blood from the left ventricle to the body and returns oxygen-poor blood to the right atrium. Blood passes through both circuits in a figure eight, with the heart at the crossing point.
notes: Correct. Pulmonary is heart to lungs to heart, and systemic is heart to body to heart.
This swaps the destinations. Pulmo means lung, so the pulmonary circuit is the loop to the lungs.
This reverses the oxygen content. Blood leaving in the pulmonary trunk is oxygen-poor, and blood leaving in the aorta is oxygen-rich.
Only the systemic circuit begins in the left ventricle and ends in the right atrium. The pulmonary circuit begins in the right ventricle and ends in the left atrium.
questions.answerText: Pulmonary runs heart to lungs to heart, and systemic runs heart to body to heart

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Blood returning from the lungs must reach the pump for the systemic circuit. Which chambers does it pass through, in order?
options: The left ventricle, then the left atrium
The left atrium, then the left ventricle
The right ventricle, then the left atrium
The right atrium, then the right ventricle
questions.why: The pulmonary veins deliver oxygen-rich blood to the left atrium. From there it passes through the mitral valve into the left ventricle, which pumps it into the aorta for the systemic circuit. The left side of the heart is the link between pulmonary venous return and systemic pumping.
notes: These are the right chambers in the wrong order. Blood always enters an atrium first and then flows down into the ventricle below it.
Correct. Left atrium first, then left ventricle.
The right ventricle and left atrium are not directly connected. Blood leaving the right ventricle must travel through the lungs before reaching the left atrium.
The right atrium and right ventricle handle blood returning from the body and pump it to the lungs. Pick this pair for the link between systemic return and pulmonary pumping.
questions.answerText: The left atrium, then the left ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Blood returning from the body must reach the pump for the pulmonary circuit. Which chambers does it pass through, in order?
options: The right ventricle, then the right atrium
The left atrium, then the left ventricle
The right atrium, then the left atrium
The right atrium, then the right ventricle
questions.why: The venae cavae and coronary sinus deliver oxygen-poor blood to the right atrium. It passes through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, which pumps it into the pulmonary trunk toward the lungs. The right side of the heart links systemic venous return to pulmonary pumping.
notes: These are the right chambers in the wrong order. Blood always fills an atrium first and then flows down into its ventricle.
The left atrium and left ventricle handle blood returning from the lungs and pump it to the body. Pick this pair for the link between pulmonary return and systemic pumping.
In the adult heart there is no opening between the atria. Blood crossed from the right atrium to the left only before birth, through the foramen ovale.
Correct. Right atrium first, then right ventricle.
questions.answerText: The right atrium, then the right ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Why does the aorta arise from the left ventricle rather than the right?
options: The left ventricle receives blood straight from the venae cavae
The left ventricle is the chamber nearest the lungs
The left ventricle holds oxygen-poor blood bound for the lungs
The left ventricle holds oxygen-rich blood bound for the body
questions.why: Blood reaching the left ventricle has just returned from the lungs through the left atrium, so it is rich in O2. The aorta carries blood to the tissues of the body, which need that oxygen. Connecting the aorta to the left ventricle sends freshly oxygenated blood into the systemic circuit.
notes: The venae cavae empty into the right atrium, not the left ventricle. Pick the right atrium for that venous return.
Both ventricles sit beside the lungs, so nearness does not explain the connection. What matters is that the left ventricle holds blood that has already been to the lungs.
Oxygen-poor blood bound for the lungs is held in the right ventricle. Pick it for the chamber connected to the pulmonary trunk.
Correct. The left ventricle sends oxygen-rich blood to the body through the aorta.
questions.answerText: The left ventricle holds oxygen-rich blood bound for the body

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Why does the pulmonary trunk arise from the right ventricle?
options: The right ventricle receives blood from the pulmonary veins
The right ventricle has the thickest wall of the four chambers
The right ventricle holds oxygen-poor blood that must go to the lungs
The right ventricle holds oxygen-rich blood bound for the body
questions.why: The right ventricle receives oxygen-poor blood that has just returned from the body. That blood needs to pick up O2, so the right ventricle pumps it into the pulmonary trunk and on to the lungs. Linking the right ventricle to the pulmonary trunk sends used blood straight to be refreshed.
notes: The pulmonary veins empty into the left atrium. Pick the left atrium for the chamber receiving blood from the lungs.
The left ventricle, not the right, has the thickest wall. Pick the left ventricle for the strongest pump.
Correct. Oxygen-poor blood in the right ventricle goes to the lungs through the pulmonary trunk.
Oxygen-rich blood bound for the body is held in the left ventricle. Pick it for the chamber connected to the aorta.
questions.answerText: The right ventricle holds oxygen-poor blood that must go to the lungs

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which sequence correctly traces blood from the right atrium to the left ventricle?
options: Right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, left ventricle
Right atrium, right ventricle, lungs, left atrium, left ventricle
Right atrium, left atrium, lungs, right ventricle, left ventricle
Right atrium, lungs, right ventricle, left atrium, left ventricle
questions.why: Blood entering the right atrium passes to the right ventricle, which pumps it through the pulmonary trunk to the lungs. It returns through the pulmonary veins to the left atrium and then flows into the left ventricle. The right and left sides are not directly connected in the adult heart, so the lungs must sit between them in the sequence.
notes: This skips the lungs. In the adult heart, blood cannot go straight from the right ventricle to the left atrium; it must pass through the pulmonary circuit first.
Correct. Blood must pass through the lungs between the right and left sides.
Blood does not cross from the right atrium to the left atrium after birth. That shortcut existed only in the fetus through the foramen ovale.
The right atrium sends blood to the right ventricle first, and only the ventricle pumps it to the lungs. An atrium cannot send blood out of the heart.
questions.answerText: Right atrium, right ventricle, lungs, left atrium, left ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: A student writes: the left atrium pumps blood to the body. Which statement corrects this?
options: The left atrium sends blood to the left ventricle, which pumps it to the body
The right atrium pumps blood to the body through the aorta
The left atrium sends blood to the right ventricle, which pumps it to the body
The left atrium sends blood to the lungs, which return it to the body
questions.why: Atria are receiving chambers that pass blood down to the ventricle on the same side. The left atrium sends oxygen-rich blood through the mitral valve into the left ventricle. Only the left ventricle pumps blood into the aorta and out to the body.
notes: Correct. The left atrium fills the left ventricle, which pumps to the body.
The right atrium receives blood from the body and does not pump into the aorta. Only the left ventricle connects to the aorta.
The left atrium and right ventricle are not connected. Each atrium empties into the ventricle on its own side.
The left atrium receives blood from the lungs; it does not send blood to them. The right ventricle is the chamber that sends blood to the lungs.
questions.answerText: The left atrium sends blood to the left ventricle, which pumps it to the body

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: A student writes: the right atrium pumps blood to the lungs. Which statement corrects this?
options: The left atrium pumps blood to the lungs through the pulmonary veins
The right atrium sends blood to the left atrium, which pumps it to the lungs
The right atrium sends blood to the left ventricle, which pumps it to the lungs
The right atrium sends blood to the right ventricle, which pumps it to the lungs
questions.why: The right atrium receives oxygen-poor blood from the body and passes it through the tricuspid valve to the right ventricle. The right ventricle then pumps that blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk and on to the lungs. Atria pass blood down; ventricles pump it out.
notes: The pulmonary veins carry blood toward the left atrium, not away from it. The left atrium receives blood from the lungs instead of sending it there.
The atria are not connected in the adult heart. Blood crossed between the atria only before birth, through the foramen ovale.
The right atrium does not connect to the left ventricle, and the left ventricle pumps to the body. Each atrium empties into the ventricle on its own side.
Correct. The right atrium fills the right ventricle, which pumps to the lungs.
questions.answerText: The right atrium sends blood to the right ventricle, which pumps it to the lungs

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Why is the heart described as a double pump?
options: It beats twice for every breath
It pumps blood and lymph through separate chambers
The atria and the ventricles each pump blood to the body
The right side pumps to the lungs, and the left side pumps to the body
questions.why: The heart is two pumps working side by side. The right side receives blood from the body and pumps it to the lungs in the pulmonary circuit, and the left side receives blood from the lungs and pumps it to the body in the systemic circuit. Both sides contract at the same time with each heartbeat.
notes: Heart rate and breathing rate are not linked in a fixed two to one ratio. The word double refers to the two circuits, not to timing.
The heart pumps only blood. Lymph moves through lymphatic vessels without any heart chamber.
Only the left ventricle pumps blood to the body. The atria push blood only into the ventricles below them.
Correct. The two sides pump to two separate circuits.
questions.answerText: The right side pumps to the lungs, and the left side pumps to the body

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: If the pulmonary veins are blocked, which chamber receives less blood?
options: The right ventricle
The left atrium
The left ventricle
The right atrium
questions.why: The four pulmonary veins carry oxygen-rich blood from the lungs into the left atrium. If they are blocked, the left atrium is the first chamber to receive less blood. The left ventricle would then fill less too, but only as a downstream effect.
notes: The right ventricle receives blood from the right atrium and pumps toward the lungs. A pulmonary vein blockage lies downstream of it, so it does not receive less blood first.
Correct. The pulmonary veins drain directly into the left atrium.
The left ventricle would eventually fill less, but it receives blood from the left atrium, not directly from the pulmonary veins. Pick it for a blocked mitral valve.
The right atrium receives the venae cavae and coronary sinus, not the pulmonary veins. Pick it for a blockage of systemic venous return.
questions.answerText: The left atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: If the pulmonary trunk is blocked, which chamber struggles to empty?
options: The right ventricle
The left ventricle
The left atrium
The right atrium
questions.why: The right ventricle pumps blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk. A blockage in the trunk means the right ventricle is pushing against resistance and cannot empty normally. The chamber that pumps directly into a blocked vessel is the one that struggles first.
notes: Correct. The right ventricle pumps directly into the pulmonary trunk.
The left ventricle pumps into the aorta. Pick it for a blockage at the start of the aorta.
The left atrium receives blood from the lungs, downstream of the blockage. It would receive less blood, but it does not pump into the pulmonary trunk.
The right atrium empties into the right ventricle, not into the pulmonary trunk. It would be affected only later, as blood backs up.
questions.answerText: The right ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: If the aorta is narrowed near its origin, which chamber has to work against increased resistance?
options: The left atrium
The right atrium
The left ventricle
The right ventricle
questions.why: The left ventricle pumps blood through the aortic valve directly into the aorta. A narrowing near the start of the aorta forces the left ventricle to push harder to move the same blood. Over time, this extra work can thicken the left ventricular wall.
notes: The left atrium sends blood to the left ventricle, not into the aorta. It is one step upstream of the chamber that faces the resistance.
The right atrium receives blood from the body. Pick it for a blockage in the venae cavae.
Correct. The left ventricle pumps directly into the aorta.
The right ventricle pumps into the pulmonary trunk. Pick it for a narrowing at the start of the pulmonary circuit.
questions.answerText: The left ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Why would failure of the left ventricle reduce blood flow to the body's tissues?
options: It pumps blood into the aorta
It receives blood from the venae cavae
It pumps blood into the pulmonary trunk
It drains blood from the heart wall
questions.why: The left ventricle is the pump for the systemic circuit. It pushes oxygen-rich blood into the aorta, whose branches deliver it to every tissue. If the left ventricle fails, less blood enters the aorta, so the body's tissues receive less blood.
notes: Correct. The left ventricle supplies the aorta and the whole systemic circuit.
The venae cavae empty into the right atrium. Pick the right atrium for the chamber receiving blood from the body.
The pulmonary trunk is fed by the right ventricle. Pick the right ventricle for the pump to the lungs.
Draining the heart wall is the job of the cardiac veins and the coronary sinus. Pick the coronary sinus for that drainage.
questions.answerText: It pumps blood into the aorta

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Why would failure of the right ventricle reduce blood flow to the lungs?
options: It pumps blood into the aorta
It holds the mitral valve
It receives blood from the pulmonary veins
It pumps blood into the pulmonary trunk
questions.why: The right ventricle is the pump for the pulmonary circuit. It pushes oxygen-poor blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk, which branches to the lungs. If it fails, less blood reaches the lungs to pick up oxygen.
notes: The aorta is fed by the left ventricle. Pick the left ventricle for the pump to the body.
The mitral valve sits between the left atrium and left ventricle. The right ventricle receives blood through the tricuspid valve instead.
The pulmonary veins empty into the left atrium. Pick the left atrium for blood returning from the lungs.
Correct. The right ventricle supplies the pulmonary trunk and the lungs.
questions.answerText: It pumps blood into the pulmonary trunk

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: A student says oxygen-rich blood enters the right atrium. Which statement corrects the mistake?
options: The right atrium receives oxygen-poor blood from the lungs
The right atrium receives no blood directly from vessels
The right atrium receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs
The right atrium receives oxygen-poor blood from the body
questions.why: The right atrium is the receiving chamber for systemic venous return. The venae cavae and coronary sinus bring it blood that has already delivered its oxygen to the body's tissues, so that blood is oxygen-poor. Oxygen-rich blood from the lungs enters the left atrium instead.
notes: The oxygen level is right, but blood from the lungs is oxygen-rich and enters the left atrium. This choice mixes up where the right atrium's blood comes from.
The right atrium receives blood directly from three large veins, the superior vena cava, inferior vena cava, and coronary sinus, plus a few small anterior cardiac veins.
Oxygen-rich blood from the lungs enters the left atrium through the pulmonary veins. This choice describes the left atrium.
Correct. The right atrium receives oxygen-poor blood from the body.
questions.answerText: The right atrium receives oxygen-poor blood from the body

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: A student says oxygen-poor blood enters the left atrium. Which statement corrects the mistake?
options: The left atrium receives blood from the right ventricle
The left atrium receives oxygen-rich blood from the venae cavae
The left atrium receives oxygen-rich blood from the pulmonary veins
The left atrium receives oxygen-poor blood from the pulmonary veins
questions.why: Blood reaching the left atrium has just passed through the lungs, where it picked up O2 and released CO2. It arrives through the four pulmonary veins and is oxygen-rich. The left atrium then passes it to the left ventricle for delivery to the body.
notes: The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs, not into the left atrium. The lungs sit between these two chambers in the pathway.
The venae cavae carry oxygen-poor blood and empty into the right atrium. Pick them for the right atrium, not the left.
Correct. The pulmonary veins bring oxygen-rich blood to the left atrium.
The vessels are right, but the pulmonary veins carry blood that has just picked up oxygen in the lungs. This choice keeps the student's original mistake.
questions.answerText: The left atrium receives oxygen-rich blood from the pulmonary veins

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: How many valves are found in the heart?
options: Six
Three
Two
Four
questions.why: The heart has four valves: two atrioventricular (AV) valves between the atria and ventricles, and two semilunar valves where the ventricles meet their great arteries. The tricuspid and mitral valves are the AV valves, and the pulmonary and aortic valves are the semilunar valves. Together they keep blood moving in one direction.
notes: Six is not a valve count for the heart. Students may reach it by mixing up valves with cusps or with the vessels that attach at the base.
Three may come from the tricuspid valve's three cusps. Cusps are the flaps of a single valve, not separate valves.
Two would count only one type, such as the two AV valves. Students sometimes forget that the ventricles have exit valves as well as entry valves.
Correct. The heart has four valves.
questions.answerText: Four

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which list names the four heart valves?
options: Tricuspid, bicuspid, mitral, and aortic
Tricuspid, mitral, pulmonary, and aortic
Tricuspid, mitral, pulmonary, and coronary
Tricuspid, mitral, aortic, and sinoatrial
questions.why: The four valves are the tricuspid valve (right atrium to right ventricle), the mitral or bicuspid valve (left atrium to left ventricle), the pulmonary valve (right ventricle to pulmonary trunk), and the aortic valve (left ventricle to aorta). The first two are AV valves and the last two are semilunar valves. Learning them in the order blood meets them helps: tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, aortic.
notes: Bicuspid and mitral are two names for the same valve, so this list counts one valve twice and leaves out the pulmonary valve.
Correct. Tricuspid, mitral, pulmonary, and aortic are the four heart valves.
There is no coronary valve. The coronary arteries leave the aorta just above the aortic valve, which may cause this mix-up.
The sinoatrial (SA) node is the pacemaker of the conduction system, not a valve. Pick it for where each heartbeat starts.
questions.answerText: Tricuspid, mitral, pulmonary, and aortic

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which valve lies between the right ventricle and the pulmonary trunk?
options: The mitral valve
The pulmonary valve
The tricuspid valve
The aortic valve
questions.why: The pulmonary valve is a semilunar valve with three pocket-shaped cusps. It opens when the right ventricle contracts, letting blood into the pulmonary trunk, and closes as the ventricle relaxes to stop blood falling back. It sits at the top of the conus arteriosus, the smooth outflow tract of the right ventricle.
notes: The mitral valve sits between the left atrium and left ventricle. Pick it for the left AV valve.
Correct. The pulmonary valve guards the exit from the right ventricle.
The tricuspid valve is the entrance to the right ventricle, from the right atrium. Pick it for the valve one step earlier.
The aortic valve guards the exit from the left ventricle into the aorta. Pick it for the left side's semilunar valve.
questions.answerText: The pulmonary valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which valve lies between the left ventricle and the aorta?
options: The tricuspid valve
The mitral valve
The pulmonary valve
The aortic valve
questions.why: The aortic valve is a semilunar valve with three pocket-shaped cusps. It opens when the left ventricle contracts, sending oxygen-rich blood into the aorta, and closes to keep that blood from falling back into the ventricle. The coronary arteries branch from the aorta just above it.
notes: The tricuspid valve sits between the right atrium and right ventricle. Pick it for the right AV valve.
The mitral valve is the entrance to the left ventricle, from the left atrium. Pick it for the valve one step earlier.
The pulmonary valve guards the exit of the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk. Pick it for the right side's semilunar valve.
Correct. The aortic valve is between the left ventricle and aorta.
questions.answerText: The aortic valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which two valves are the atrioventricular (AV) valves?
options: The mitral and aortic valves
The tricuspid and pulmonary valves
The pulmonary and aortic valves
The tricuspid and mitral valves
questions.why: Atrioventricular valves sit between an atrium and a ventricle. The tricuspid valve is the right AV valve and the mitral valve is the left AV valve. Both are anchored by chordae tendineae and papillary muscles, which hold them shut when the ventricles contract.
notes: This pairs the left AV valve with the left semilunar valve. Pick it for the two valves on the left side of the heart.
This pairs the right AV valve with the right semilunar valve. Pick it for the two valves on the right side of the heart.
The pulmonary and aortic valves are the semilunar valves at the exits of the ventricles. Pick this pair for the valves leading into the great arteries.
Correct. The tricuspid and mitral valves are the AV valves.
questions.answerText: The tricuspid and mitral valves

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which two valves are the semilunar valves?
options: The tricuspid and mitral valves
The pulmonary and aortic valves
The tricuspid and aortic valves
The mitral and pulmonary valves
questions.why: Semilunar means half-moon, describing the shape of the three pocket-like cusps in each of these valves. The pulmonary valve guards the exit of the right ventricle and the aortic valve guards the exit of the left ventricle. They have no chordae tendineae, because their cusps close by filling with blood.
notes: The tricuspid and mitral valves are the AV valves between atria and ventricles. Pick this pair for the valves anchored by chordae tendineae.
Correct. The pulmonary and aortic valves are the semilunar valves.
This mixes one AV valve with one semilunar valve. Pick it only for a question pairing the first and last valves blood passes through.
This mixes the left AV valve with the right semilunar valve. It does not match any single valve type.
questions.answerText: The pulmonary and aortic valves

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: How many cusps does the mitral valve have?
options: Two
Three
One
Four
questions.why: The mitral valve has two cusps, which is why it is also called the bicuspid valve. The other three heart valves each have three cusps: the tricuspid valve and both semilunar valves. The mitral valve is the only valve with two.
notes: Correct. The mitral valve has two cusps.
Three cusps belong to the tricuspid valve and to the pulmonary and aortic valves. Pick three for any heart valve except the mitral.
No heart valve has a single cusp. One flap could not seal an opening the way two or three meeting flaps do.
No heart valve has four cusps. This number may come from the four valves or four chambers.
questions.answerText: Two

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which valve is also called the bicuspid valve?
options: The aortic valve
The tricuspid valve
The mitral valve
The pulmonary valve
questions.why: The mitral valve, the left AV valve, is also called the bicuspid valve because it has two cusps. Its other name comes from its resemblance to a bishop's miter, a tall two-pointed hat. Your lab list calls it the left atrioventricular (bicuspid or mitral) valve.
notes: The aortic valve is a semilunar valve with three cusps. Pick it for the exit of the left ventricle.
The tricuspid valve is the right AV valve with three cusps. Pick it for the valve whose name says three.
Correct. The mitral valve is the bicuspid valve.
The pulmonary valve is a semilunar valve with three cusps. Pick it for the exit of the right ventricle.
questions.answerText: The mitral valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which valve prevents backflow into the right atrium?
options: The aortic valve
The pulmonary valve
The mitral valve
The tricuspid valve
questions.why: A valve prevents backflow into the chamber blood has just left. Blood leaves the right atrium through the tricuspid valve, so when the right ventricle contracts, the tricuspid valve closes and keeps blood from being pushed back into the right atrium.
notes: The aortic valve stops backflow into the left ventricle from the aorta. Pick it for the exit of the left ventricle.
The pulmonary valve stops backflow into the right ventricle from the pulmonary trunk. Pick it for the chamber one step later.
The mitral valve stops backflow into the left atrium. Pick it for the left side's AV valve.
Correct. The tricuspid valve stops backflow into the right atrium.
questions.answerText: The tricuspid valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which valve prevents backflow into the left atrium?
options: The mitral valve
The tricuspid valve
The aortic valve
The pulmonary valve
questions.why: Blood leaves the left atrium through the mitral valve into the left ventricle. When the left ventricle contracts, the mitral valve closes so that blood is pushed out through the aorta rather than back into the left atrium. The chordae tendineae and papillary muscles keep the mitral cusps from flipping backward.
notes: Correct. The mitral valve stops backflow into the left atrium.
The tricuspid valve stops backflow into the right atrium. Pick it for the right side's AV valve.
The aortic valve stops backflow into the left ventricle. Pick it for the exit of the left ventricle.
The pulmonary valve stops backflow into the right ventricle. Pick it for the exit of the right ventricle.
questions.answerText: The mitral valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which valve prevents backflow into the right ventricle?
options: The aortic valve
The tricuspid valve
The pulmonary valve
The mitral valve
questions.why: Blood leaves the right ventricle through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk. When the right ventricle relaxes, blood in the trunk tends to fall back, filling the pocket-shaped cusps and snapping the pulmonary valve shut. This keeps blood from returning to the right ventricle.
notes: The aortic valve prevents backflow into the left ventricle. Pick it for the left side's semilunar valve.
The tricuspid valve is the entrance to the right ventricle and prevents backflow into the right atrium. Pick it for the chamber one step earlier.
Correct. The pulmonary valve stops backflow into the right ventricle.
The mitral valve prevents backflow into the left atrium. Pick it for the left AV valve.
questions.answerText: The pulmonary valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which valve prevents backflow into the left ventricle?
options: The aortic valve
The mitral valve
The pulmonary valve
The tricuspid valve
questions.why: Blood leaves the left ventricle through the aortic valve into the aorta. When the left ventricle relaxes, blood in the aorta fills the three pocket-shaped cusps and closes the valve, keeping blood from falling back into the ventricle. The mitral valve, the entrance to the left ventricle, guards the left atrium instead.
notes: Correct. The aortic valve stops backflow into the left ventricle.
The mitral valve is the entrance to the left ventricle and prevents backflow into the left atrium. Students pick it because it touches the left ventricle too.
The pulmonary valve prevents backflow into the right ventricle. Pick it for the right side's semilunar valve.
The tricuspid valve prevents backflow into the right atrium. Pick it for the right AV valve.
questions.answerText: The aortic valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: What are the chordae tendineae?
options: Muscular ridges on the inner walls of the ventricles
Pocket-shaped cusps of the semilunar valves
Fibrous cords tying AV valve cusps to papillary muscles
Connective tissue rings around the valve openings
questions.why: The chordae tendineae, sometimes called heart strings, are strong fibrous cords. They run from the edges of the tricuspid and mitral valve cusps down to the papillary muscles in the ventricle wall. When the ventricle contracts, they keep the cusps from being pushed back into the atria.
notes: Muscular ridges on the ventricle walls are the trabeculae carneae. Pick them for the rough inner texture of the ventricles.
Pocket-shaped cusps belong to the pulmonary and aortic valves, which have no chordae. Pick them for the semilunar valves.
Correct. Chordae tendineae tie AV valve cusps to papillary muscles.
The connective tissue rings around the valves form the fibrous skeleton. Pick it for what anchors the valves and insulates the atria from the ventricles.
questions.answerText: Fibrous cords tying AV valve cusps to papillary muscles

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: What do the papillary muscles anchor?
options: The coronary arteries
The pectinate muscles
The chordae tendineae
The semilunar valve cusps
questions.why: Papillary muscles are cone-shaped projections of the ventricle wall. The chordae tendineae attach to their tips and run up to the cusps of the AV valves. When the ventricle contracts, the papillary muscles contract too, keeping the chordae taut so the cusps stay shut.
notes: The coronary arteries run in the grooves on the outer surface of the heart. Pick them for the vessels supplying the myocardium.
The pectinate muscles are ridges in the atrial walls, not attached to the papillary muscles. Pick them for the comb-like ridges of the atria and auricles.
Correct. The papillary muscles anchor the chordae tendineae.
The semilunar valve cusps have no anchoring cords or muscles; they close by filling with blood. Pick them for the pulmonary and aortic valves.
questions.answerText: The chordae tendineae

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the AV valves with the semilunar valves?
options: AV valves lie between atria and ventricles, and semilunar valves lie between ventricles and arteries
AV valves lie between ventricles and arteries, and semilunar valves lie between atria and ventricles
Both types lie between the two atria
Both types are anchored by chordae tendineae and papillary muscles
questions.why: The AV valves (tricuspid and mitral) are the entrances to the ventricles, between each atrium and its ventricle. The semilunar valves (pulmonary and aortic) are the exits, between each ventricle and the great artery it pumps into. Only the AV valves have chordae tendineae and papillary muscles.
notes: Correct. AV valves are ventricle entrances, and semilunar valves are ventricle exits.
This swaps the two types. Use the name atrioventricular as a clue: it joins an atrium to a ventricle.
No valve lies between the two atria; they are separated by the interatrial septum. Pick the septum for the wall between the atria.
Only the AV valves have chordae and papillary muscles. Semilunar cusps fill with blood and close on their own.
questions.answerText: AV valves lie between atria and ventricles, and semilunar valves lie between ventricles and arteries

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the tricuspid and mitral valves?
options: The tricuspid is on the left, and the mitral is on the right
Both are semilunar valves at the exits of the ventricles
The tricuspid has three cusps on the right, and the mitral has two cusps on the left
The tricuspid has two cusps on the left, and the mitral has three cusps on the right
questions.why: Both valves are atrioventricular valves anchored by chordae tendineae and papillary muscles. The tricuspid valve sits on the right, between the right atrium and right ventricle, and has three cusps. The mitral valve sits on the left, between the left atrium and left ventricle, and has two cusps.
notes: This swaps the sides. Blood meets the tricuspid valve first, on the right, and the mitral (bicuspid) valve later, on the left.
Both are AV valves, not semilunar valves. The semilunar valves are the pulmonary and aortic valves at the ventricle exits.
Correct. Tricuspid is right with three cusps, and mitral is left with two.
This swaps both the sides and the cusp counts. Remember that tri means three, and the tricuspid is on the right.
questions.answerText: The tricuspid has three cusps on the right, and the mitral has two cusps on the left

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the pulmonary and aortic valves?
options: The pulmonary guards the left ventricle exit, and the aortic the right
Both are semilunar; pulmonary guards the right ventricle exit, aortic the left
The pulmonary has two cusps, and the aortic has three
Both are AV valves held by chordae tendineae
questions.why: The pulmonary and aortic valves are both semilunar valves with three pocket-shaped cusps. The pulmonary valve sits where the right ventricle opens into the pulmonary trunk, and the aortic valve sits where the left ventricle opens into the aorta. Neither has chordae tendineae.
notes: This swaps the sides. The pulmonary trunk leaves the right ventricle and the aorta leaves the left.
Correct. Both are semilunar valves, one at each ventricle exit.
Both semilunar valves have three cusps. The only two-cusped valve is the mitral valve.
Neither is an AV valve, and neither has chordae tendineae. Pick this description for the tricuspid and mitral valves.
questions.answerText: Both are semilunar; pulmonary guards the right ventricle exit, aortic the left

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Why don't the semilunar valves need chordae tendineae?
options: Their cusps are made of muscle that contracts shut
They are anchored by the papillary muscles instead
They only open once per minute
Their pocket-shaped cusps fill with blood and close themselves
questions.why: Each semilunar valve has three pocket-shaped cusps, like small cups facing up into the artery. When the ventricle relaxes and blood starts to fall back, it fills these pockets, which press together and seal the opening. The design closes itself, so no cords or muscles are needed.
notes: Valve cusps contain no muscle; they are folds of endocardium over connective tissue. Pick the myocardium for the muscle that contracts.
Papillary muscles are found only with the AV valves. Pick them for the muscles anchoring the tricuspid and mitral chordae.
The semilunar valves open with every heartbeat, many times a minute. This choice misreads how often they work.
Correct. Blood filling the pocket-shaped cusps closes the valve.
questions.answerText: Their pocket-shaped cusps fill with blood and close themselves

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Papillary muscles are projections of which structure?
options: The valve cusps
The interatrial septum
The atrial wall
The ventricle wall
questions.why: Papillary muscles are cone-shaped projections of the myocardium of the ventricle wall. They rise from the floor and walls of each ventricle, and the chordae tendineae run from their tips to the AV valve cusps. Because they are part of the ventricle wall, they contract when the ventricle does.
notes: The valve cusps contain no muscle. They are the flaps that the chordae attach to, at the other end from the papillary muscles.
The interatrial septum separates the atria and holds the fossa ovalis. Pick it for the wall between the receiving chambers.
The atrial wall has pectinate muscles, not papillary muscles. Pick the atrial wall for the comb-like ridges.
Correct. Papillary muscles project from the ventricle wall.
questions.answerText: The ventricle wall

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: What job do all four heart valves share?
options: They keep blood flowing in one direction
They pump blood out of the ventricles
They start each heartbeat
They mix blood between the two sides
questions.why: Each valve opens to let blood pass forward and closes to stop it from flowing back into the chamber it just left. With four valves in a row, blood can only move one way: atrium to ventricle to artery on each side. This one-way flow is what makes the heart an effective pump.
notes: Correct. All four valves enforce one-way flow.
Valves do no pumping. The myocardium of the ventricles generates the force, and valves only open and close.
Each heartbeat starts at the sinoatrial (SA) node in the right atrium wall. Pick the SA node for the heart's pacemaker.
The two sides of the adult heart are kept separate, and no valve connects them. Mixing between sides happens only through a defect, such as a septal hole.
questions.answerText: They keep blood flowing in one direction

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: A valve that does not close cleanly lets blood slip backward. What does a clinician hear through a stethoscope because of the turbulent flow?
options: A crackle in the lungs
A heart murmur
A gurgling bowel sound
A wheeze
questions.why: When a valve leaks or is narrowed, blood no longer flows smoothly through it. The turbulence makes an extra sound, heard through a stethoscope as a murmur. One-way flow through four well-sealed valves is what keeps the normal heart sounds clean.
notes: Crackles are heard over the lungs when the alveoli contain fluid. Pick them for a problem in the respiratory zone, not the heart.
Correct. Turbulent flow through a faulty valve is heard as a murmur.
Bowel sounds come from the movement of gas and contents through the intestines. Pick them for a question about the digestive tract.
A wheeze is a whistling sound from air forced through narrowed airways, as in asthma. Pick it for a problem in the bronchial tree.
questions.answerText: A heart murmur

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: If the tricuspid valve fails to close, blood leaks backward into which chamber when the right ventricle contracts?
options: The right ventricle
The pulmonary trunk
The right atrium
The left atrium
questions.why: The tricuspid valve sits between the right atrium and right ventricle and normally closes when the right ventricle contracts. If it fails, some of the blood being pushed by the right ventricle leaks back into the right atrium. This backward leak is called regurgitation.
notes: The right ventricle is the chamber doing the pushing, so blood leaks out of it, not into it. Pick it for a failing pulmonary valve.
The pulmonary trunk is where blood should go forward. A tricuspid leak sends blood backward, away from the trunk.
Correct. A leaky tricuspid valve lets blood flow back into the right atrium.
The left atrium sits behind the mitral valve on the other side of the heart. Pick it for a failing mitral valve.
questions.answerText: The right atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: If the mitral valve fails to close, blood leaks backward into which chamber when the left ventricle contracts?
options: The left ventricle
The left atrium
The aorta
The right atrium
questions.why: The mitral valve sits between the left atrium and left ventricle. When the left ventricle contracts, the mitral valve should close so all the blood goes out through the aorta. If it fails, some blood is pushed back into the left atrium, which is called mitral regurgitation.
notes: The left ventricle is the chamber doing the pushing, so blood leaks out of it, not into it. Pick it for a failing aortic valve.
Correct. A leaky mitral valve sends blood back into the left atrium.
The aorta is where blood should go forward. A mitral leak sends blood backward, away from the aorta.
The right atrium sits behind the tricuspid valve. Pick it for a failing tricuspid valve.
questions.answerText: The left atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: If the pulmonary valve fails to close, blood leaks backward into which chamber as the right ventricle relaxes?
options: The right ventricle
The right atrium
The left atrium
The left ventricle
questions.why: The pulmonary valve guards the exit from the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk. When the ventricle relaxes, the valve should snap shut so blood stays in the trunk. If it fails, blood falls back from the pulmonary trunk into the right ventricle.
notes: Correct. A leaky pulmonary valve lets blood fall back into the right ventricle.
The right atrium is protected by the tricuspid valve, not the pulmonary valve. Pick it for a failing tricuspid valve.
The left atrium is protected by the mitral valve. Pick it for a failing mitral valve.
The left ventricle is protected by the aortic valve. Pick it for a failing aortic valve.
questions.answerText: The right ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: If the aortic valve fails to close, blood leaks backward into which chamber as the left ventricle relaxes?
options: The right atrium
The right ventricle
The left atrium
The left ventricle
questions.why: The aortic valve guards the exit from the left ventricle into the aorta. As the ventricle relaxes, the valve should close so blood stays in the aorta. If it fails, blood falls back from the aorta into the left ventricle, so the ventricle must pump some of the same blood again.
notes: The right atrium is protected by the tricuspid valve. Pick it for a failing tricuspid valve.
The right ventricle is protected by the pulmonary valve. Pick it for a failing pulmonary valve.
The left atrium is protected by the mitral valve. Pick it for a failing mitral valve.
Correct. A leaky aortic valve lets blood fall back into the left ventricle.
questions.answerText: The left ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: A patient has ruptured chordae tendineae. Which valves are most directly affected?
options: All four valves equally
The semilunar valves
The AV valves
The pulmonary valve only
questions.why: Chordae tendineae attach only to the cusps of the AV valves, the tricuspid and mitral. When they rupture, the cusps lose their anchor and can be pushed back into the atrium when the ventricle contracts. The semilunar valves have no chordae and are not directly affected.
notes: Only two valves have chordae. The pulmonary and aortic valves would be unaffected.
The semilunar valves have no chordae tendineae, so ruptured chordae do not touch them. Pick them for problems with pocket-shaped cusps.
Correct. Chordae tendineae belong only to the AV valves.
The pulmonary valve is a semilunar valve with no chordae. Pick it for a problem at the exit of the right ventricle.
questions.answerText: The AV valves

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: A heart attack kills a papillary muscle in the left ventricle. Which valve is most at risk of failing?
options: The mitral valve
The aortic valve
The tricuspid valve
The pulmonary valve
questions.why: The papillary muscles of the left ventricle anchor the chordae tendineae of the mitral valve. If one dies, its chordae go slack and the mitral cusps can be pushed back into the left atrium. The aortic valve also opens from the left ventricle, but it has no papillary muscles.
notes: Correct. Left ventricular papillary muscles hold the mitral valve.
The aortic valve sits at the exit of the left ventricle, but semilunar valves have no papillary muscles or chordae. Pick it for a problem with the left ventricle's outflow.
The tricuspid valve is anchored by papillary muscles in the right ventricle. Pick it for a right ventricular papillary muscle injury.
The pulmonary valve is a semilunar valve with no papillary muscles. Pick it for the exit of the right ventricle.
questions.answerText: The mitral valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which sequence traces the anchoring chain that holds an AV valve shut, from the ventricle wall to the valve?
options: Papillary muscle, chordae tendineae, valve cusp
Chordae tendineae, papillary muscle, valve cusp
Trabeculae carneae, pectinate muscle, valve cusp
Papillary muscle, valve cusp, chordae tendineae
questions.why: The papillary muscles rise from the ventricle wall. Chordae tendineae run from their tips up to the edges of the AV valve cusps. When the ventricle contracts, this chain stays taut and keeps the cusps from being pushed back into the atrium, which is why damage anywhere along it can make the valve fail.
notes: Correct. Papillary muscle, then chordae tendineae, then the valve cusp.
This puts the chordae next to the wall. In fact the papillary muscle projects from the wall, and the chordae connect it to the cusp.
Trabeculae carneae are ridges on the ventricle walls and pectinate muscles are in the atria. Neither is part of the chain holding a valve shut.
This puts the cusp in the middle. The chordae are what link the papillary muscle to the cusp, so they must sit between them.
questions.answerText: Papillary muscle, chordae tendineae, valve cusp
