questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Blood leaks from the aorta back into the left ventricle each time the ventricle relaxes. Which valve is failing?
options: The mitral valve
The tricuspid valve
The aortic valve
The pulmonary valve
questions.why: The aortic valve is the only valve between the aorta and the left ventricle. Its job is to close as the ventricle relaxes, so blood stays in the aorta. A leak in that exact direction points to aortic valve failure, called aortic regurgitation.
notes: The mitral valve separates the left atrium from the left ventricle. Pick it for blood leaking back into the left atrium.
The tricuspid valve separates the right atrium from the right ventricle. Pick it for blood leaking back into the right atrium.
Correct. The aortic valve separates the aorta from the left ventricle.
The pulmonary valve separates the pulmonary trunk from the right ventricle. Pick it for a leak on the right side.
questions.answerText: The aortic valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Blood leaks from the pulmonary trunk back into the right ventricle each time the ventricle relaxes. Which valve is failing?
options: The pulmonary valve
The aortic valve
The tricuspid valve
The mitral valve
questions.why: The pulmonary valve sits between the right ventricle and the pulmonary trunk. It should close as the right ventricle relaxes so blood stays in the trunk. When it is incompetent (unable to close fully), blood falls back into the right ventricle.
notes: Correct. The pulmonary valve separates the pulmonary trunk from the right ventricle.
The aortic valve separates the aorta from the left ventricle. Pick it for a leak on the left side.
The tricuspid valve separates the right atrium from the right ventricle. Pick it for a leak back into the right atrium.
The mitral valve separates the left atrium from the left ventricle. Pick it for a leak back into the left atrium.
questions.answerText: The pulmonary valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In mitral valve prolapse, the mitral cusps bulge back into the left atrium when the ventricle contracts. Which structures normally prevent this?
options: The trabeculae carneae
The pectinate muscles
The chordae tendineae
The moderator band
questions.why: The chordae tendineae tie the mitral cusps to the papillary muscles of the left ventricle. When the ventricle contracts, they hold the cusps in place so they meet and seal instead of bulging into the atrium. If the chordae are stretched or weak, the cusps prolapse, meaning they slip backward.
notes: The trabeculae carneae are muscular ridges on the ventricle walls and do not attach to the cusps. Pick them for the rough inner surface of the ventricles.
The pectinate muscles are ridges in the atrial walls. Pick them for the comb-like ridges of the atria and auricles.
Correct. The chordae tendineae hold the mitral cusps in place.
The moderator band is in the right ventricle and carries conduction fibers. It has no connection to the mitral valve on the left side.
questions.answerText: The chordae tendineae

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: What do the papillary muscles do as the ventricles contract?
options: They relax so the AV cusps can swing into the atria
They contract and keep the chordae taut so the AV cusps stay shut
They push the semilunar cusps open
They squeeze blood forward out of the atria
questions.why: The papillary muscles are part of the ventricle wall, so they contract along with it. As they contract, they pull on the chordae tendineae and keep them taut. This holds the tricuspid and mitral cusps together against the pressure of the contracting ventricle, so the cusps do not flip into the atria.
notes: If the papillary muscles relaxed, the cusps would be free to flip into the atria, which is exactly the failure they prevent. This choice describes what happens when a papillary muscle is damaged.
Correct. Contracting papillary muscles keep the chordae taut.
The semilunar valves open because blood pressure in the ventricle rises above the pressure in the artery. They have no connection to the papillary muscles.
Atrial contraction comes from the thin atrial walls themselves, just before the ventricles contract. Papillary muscles sit inside the ventricles.
questions.answerText: They contract and keep the chordae taut so the AV cusps stay shut

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In pulmonary valve stenosis, the pulmonary valve is narrowed. Which chamber must work harder first?
options: The right ventricle
The right atrium
The left ventricle
The left atrium
questions.why: Stenosis means narrowing. The pulmonary valve is the exit of the right ventricle, so a narrowed pulmonary valve forces the right ventricle to push harder to move blood into the pulmonary trunk. The chamber directly behind a narrowed exit valve is the first to feel the strain.
notes: Correct. The right ventricle pumps through the pulmonary valve.
The right atrium empties through the tricuspid valve. Pick it for tricuspid stenosis.
The left ventricle pumps through the aortic valve. Pick it for aortic stenosis.
The left atrium empties through the mitral valve. Pick it for mitral stenosis.
questions.answerText: The right ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In aortic stenosis, the aortic valve is narrowed. Which chamber must work harder first?
options: The left atrium
The left ventricle
The right ventricle
The right atrium
questions.why: The aortic valve is the exit of the left ventricle. When it is narrowed, the left ventricle must push harder to force blood into the aorta. Over time, this extra work can thicken the left ventricular wall.
notes: The left atrium empties through the mitral valve, one step upstream. Pick it for mitral stenosis.
Correct. The left ventricle pumps through the aortic valve.
The right ventricle pumps through the pulmonary valve. Pick it for pulmonary stenosis.
The right atrium empties through the tricuspid valve. Pick it for tricuspid stenosis.
questions.answerText: The left ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Why does blood normally not flow from the ventricles back into the atria?
options: The AV valves close when the ventricles contract
The semilunar valves close when the ventricles contract
The interventricular septum blocks the path
The atria contract at the same moment as the ventricles
questions.why: The AV valves, tricuspid and mitral, sit between each atrium and its ventricle. When the ventricles contract, rising pressure pushes the cusps together and the chordae tendineae hold them shut. With the AV valves sealed, blood can only leave the ventricles through the semilunar valves into the arteries.
notes: Correct. Closed AV valves block the way back into the atria.
The semilunar valves open, not close, when the ventricles contract, so blood can leave into the arteries. They close when the ventricles relax, protecting the ventricles from backflow.
The interventricular septum separates the two ventricles from each other, not the ventricles from the atria. Pick it for a ventricular septal defect.
The atria contract first and then relax while the ventricles contract. Their timing alone would not stop backflow.
questions.answerText: The AV valves close when the ventricles contract

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which narrowed valve would most directly restrict blood leaving the left ventricle into the aorta?
options: The mitral valve
The aortic valve
The pulmonary valve
The tricuspid valve
questions.why: Blood leaving the left ventricle must pass through the aortic valve to enter the aorta. If that valve is narrowed, a condition called aortic stenosis, less blood gets through with each beat. The other valves sit elsewhere in the pathway and would affect different steps.
notes: A narrowed mitral valve restricts blood entering the left ventricle from the left atrium, one step earlier. Pick it for reduced filling of the left ventricle.
Correct. The aortic valve is the gateway from the left ventricle into the aorta.
A narrowed pulmonary valve restricts blood leaving the right ventricle. Pick it for reduced flow into the pulmonary trunk.
A narrowed tricuspid valve restricts blood entering the right ventricle. Pick it for reduced filling on the right side.
questions.answerText: The aortic valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which narrowed valve would most directly restrict blood leaving the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk?
options: The mitral valve
The pulmonary valve
The tricuspid valve
The aortic valve
questions.why: Blood leaving the right ventricle must pass through the pulmonary valve to enter the pulmonary trunk. If that valve is narrowed, called pulmonary stenosis, less blood reaches the lungs with each beat. The right ventricle has to push harder to overcome it.
notes: A narrowed mitral valve restricts blood entering the left ventricle. Pick it for reduced left ventricular filling.
Correct. The pulmonary valve is the gateway from the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk.
A narrowed tricuspid valve restricts blood entering the right ventricle, one step earlier. Pick it for reduced right ventricular filling.
A narrowed aortic valve restricts blood leaving the left ventricle. Pick it for reduced flow into the aorta.
questions.answerText: The pulmonary valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which statement explains why the AV valves need chordae tendineae and papillary muscles but the semilunar valves do not?
options: Semilunar valves are made of muscle and close themselves by contracting
Semilunar valves face stronger pressure and need thicker cusps instead
AV cusps would be pushed into the atria, while semilunar cusps close by filling
AV valves open only once per minute and need extra support
questions.why: When a ventricle contracts, high pressure pushes up against the AV cusps from below. Without the chordae tendineae, held taut by the papillary muscles, the cusps would turn inside out into the atria. Semilunar cusps are shaped like pockets that fill with falling blood and press together, so they seal without any anchors.
notes: No valve contains muscle. All valves open and close passively as blood pressure changes on either side.
Cusp thickness is not the explanation. The key difference is the shape of the cusps and the direction of the pressure they face.
Correct. AV cusps need anchors against ventricular pressure, while semilunar cusps seal by filling.
The AV valves open with every heartbeat, many times a minute. Their support is needed against pressure, not because of how often they open.
questions.answerText: AV cusps would be pushed into the atria, while semilunar cusps close by filling

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Blood that passes through the pulmonary valve enters which circuit?
options: The pulmonary circuit
The hepatic portal system
The coronary circulation
The systemic circuit
questions.why: The pulmonary valve opens into the pulmonary trunk, which divides into the pulmonary arteries to the lungs. Blood that passes through it has entered the pulmonary circuit, where it will pick up O2 before returning to the left atrium. A problem with this valve therefore affects flow to the lungs first.
notes: Correct. The pulmonary valve opens into the pulmonary circuit.
The hepatic portal system carries blood from the digestive organs to the liver. Pick it for blood draining the gut.
The coronary circulation begins with the coronary arteries just above the aortic valve. Pick it for the heart's own blood supply.
Blood enters the systemic circuit through the aortic valve. Pick it for the valve at the exit of the left ventricle.
questions.answerText: The pulmonary circuit

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In mitral stenosis, the mitral valve is narrowed. Which chamber would not fill normally?
options: The left atrium
The left ventricle
The right ventricle
The right atrium
questions.why: The mitral valve is the entrance to the left ventricle, the doorway blood uses to move down from the left atrium. When it is narrowed, less blood can get through, so the left ventricle does not fill normally. Blood instead backs up in the left atrium behind the narrowed valve.
notes: The left atrium sits behind the narrowed valve, so it overfills rather than underfills. Pick it for the chamber where blood backs up.
Correct. A narrowed mitral valve limits filling of the left ventricle.
The right ventricle fills through the tricuspid valve. Pick it for tricuspid stenosis.
The right atrium fills from the venae cavae and coronary sinus, with no valve in the way. Pick it for blocked systemic venous return.
questions.answerText: The left ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: If the tricuspid valve could not close at all, blood pushed backward by the right ventricle would enter the right atrium and back up toward which vessels?
options: The pulmonary veins
The aorta
The coronary arteries
The venae cavae
questions.why: With no working tricuspid valve, each right ventricular contraction sends blood back into the right atrium. The right atrium is fed by the superior and inferior venae cavae, so blood backs up into those veins and the veins of the body. Tracing backward from a failed valve tells you where the congestion builds.
notes: The pulmonary veins feed the left atrium. Pick them for backup caused by a failed mitral valve.
The aorta carries blood away from the left ventricle and is not upstream of the right atrium. Pick it for a problem with the aortic valve.
The coronary arteries leave the aorta to supply the heart wall. They are not part of the backward path from the right atrium.
Correct. Blood backs up from the right atrium into the venae cavae.
questions.answerText: The venae cavae

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: If the mitral valve could not close at all, blood pushed backward by the left ventricle would enter the left atrium and back up toward which organs?
options: The body tissues, through the venae cavae
The heart wall, through the coronary sinus
The lungs, through the pulmonary veins
The body tissues, through the aorta
questions.why: With no working mitral valve, each left ventricular contraction sends blood back into the left atrium. The left atrium is fed by the pulmonary veins from the lungs, so blood backs up into those veins and the lungs. This is why severe mitral valve failure can cause fluid to build up in the lungs.
notes: The venae cavae feed the right atrium. Pick them for backup caused by a failed tricuspid valve.
The coronary sinus drains into the right atrium, not the left. Pick it for the vessel draining the heart wall.
Correct. Blood backs up from the left atrium into the pulmonary veins and lungs.
The aorta carries blood forward from the left ventricle, not backward from the left atrium. Pick it for normal flow to the body.
questions.answerText: The lungs, through the pulmonary veins

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: What opens and closes the heart valves?
options: Nerve signals sent directly to each valve
Pressure differences in the blood on either side
Contraction of muscle inside each cusp
The papillary muscles pulling the cusps open
questions.why: Heart valves are passive flaps of endocardium over connective tissue, with no muscle of their own. When blood pressure behind a valve is higher than in front of it, the valve is pushed open; when pressure in front becomes higher, blood pushes the cusps shut. The chambers create these pressure changes as they contract and relax.
notes: No nerves open or close the valves. Nerves to the heart act on the SA node and the myocardium, which change heart rate and force.
Correct. Pressure differences push the valves open and shut.
Valve cusps contain no muscle. Pick the myocardium for heart tissue that contracts.
Papillary muscles hold the AV cusps shut against ventricular pressure; they do not pull them open. The valves open when atrial pressure rises above ventricular pressure.
questions.answerText: Pressure differences in the blood on either side

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Blood passing through which valve leaves the heart and enters the systemic arteries?
options: The mitral valve
The pulmonary valve
The tricuspid valve
The aortic valve
questions.why: The aortic valve opens from the left ventricle into the aorta, the first artery of the systemic circuit. Blood passing through it is on its way to the body's tissues. The pulmonary valve is the matching exit on the right side, but it leads into the pulmonary circuit instead.
notes: The mitral valve lets blood move from the left atrium into the left ventricle, so blood passing through it is still inside the heart.
The pulmonary valve also lets blood leave the heart, but into the pulmonary trunk toward the lungs. Pick it for entry into the pulmonary circuit.
The tricuspid valve lets blood move from the right atrium into the right ventricle, still inside the heart. Pick it for the entrance to the right ventricle.
Correct. The aortic valve opens into the aorta and the systemic arteries.
questions.answerText: The aortic valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Where does oxygen-poor blood returning from the body first enter the heart?
options: Right atrium
Left ventricle
Left atrium
Right ventricle
questions.why: Oxygen-poor blood returns from the body through the superior and inferior venae cavae, and both empty into the right atrium. The coronary sinus also delivers blood from the heart wall to this chamber. The right atrium then passes the blood through the tricuspid valve to the right ventricle.
notes: Correct. Both venae cavae empty into the right atrium.
The left ventricle pumps oxygen-rich blood into the aorta. It would be the answer for the chamber that sends blood out to the body.
The left atrium receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs through the four pulmonary veins. Choose it for where blood first enters the heart after the lungs.
The right ventricle is the next chamber, receiving blood from the right atrium through the tricuspid valve. It would be the answer for which chamber pumps blood to the lungs.
questions.answerText: Right atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Blood leaves the right atrium through which valve?
options: Aortic valve
Mitral valve
Tricuspid valve
Pulmonary valve
questions.why: The tricuspid valve is the right atrioventricular valve, with three cusps, sitting between the right atrium and the right ventricle. Blood passes through it from the atrium down into the ventricle, and the valve closes when the ventricle contracts so blood cannot flow back into the atrium.
notes: The aortic valve is the semilunar valve between the left ventricle and the aorta. It is the answer for the last valve blood crosses before leaving the heart for the body.
The mitral (bicuspid) valve is the left atrioventricular valve, between the left atrium and the left ventricle. It would be the answer for blood leaving the left atrium.
Correct. The tricuspid valve connects the right atrium to the right ventricle.
The pulmonary valve is the semilunar valve between the right ventricle and the pulmonary trunk. Choose it for blood leaving the right ventricle, one step later in the pathway.
questions.answerText: Tricuspid valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which chamber pumps blood through the pulmonary valve?
options: Left atrium
Right atrium
Right ventricle
Left ventricle
questions.why: The pulmonary valve guards the exit of the right ventricle, where it opens into the pulmonary trunk. When the right ventricle contracts, it pushes oxygen-poor blood through this semilunar valve and on toward the lungs. This is the start of the pulmonary circuit.
notes: The left atrium passes oxygen-rich blood through the mitral valve to the left ventricle. Pick it for the chamber that receives the pulmonary veins.
The right atrium sends blood to the right ventricle through the tricuspid valve, not the pulmonary valve. Choose it for the chamber that receives blood from the venae cavae.
Correct. The right ventricle pumps blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk.
The left ventricle pumps blood through the aortic valve into the aorta. It is the left-side mirror of this answer and would be right for a question about the valve leading to the body.
questions.answerText: Right ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: After passing through the pulmonary valve, blood enters which vessel?
options: Pulmonary trunk
Superior vena cava
Pulmonary veins
Aorta
questions.why: The pulmonary valve sits at the exit of the right ventricle, and on the far side of it is the pulmonary trunk. This large vessel carries oxygen-poor blood upward and then splits into the right and left pulmonary arteries, which take the blood to the lungs.
notes: Correct. The pulmonary trunk lies just beyond the pulmonary valve.
The superior vena cava returns oxygen-poor blood from the head, neck, and upper limbs into the right atrium. Choose it for a vessel that brings blood into the heart, not one that carries blood out.

The pulmonary veins carry oxygen-rich blood from the lungs back to the left atrium. They are the answer for the vessels that return blood to the heart after the lungs, not the vessel that leaves the right ventricle.
The aorta receives blood from the left ventricle through the aortic valve. It would be the answer for the vessel just past the aortic valve, the left-side mirror of this question.
questions.answerText: Pulmonary trunk

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Along the pathway of blood through the heart and lungs, where does blood pick up oxygen?
options: Right ventricle
Left atrium
Lungs
Pulmonary trunk
questions.why: Blood picks up oxygen in the lungs, where the capillaries surrounding the alveoli (tiny air sacs) exchange gases with inhaled air. Blood arrives there oxygen-poor through the pulmonary arteries, picks up O2 and releases CO2, and returns to the left atrium through the pulmonary veins.
notes: The right ventricle holds oxygen-poor blood and pumps it toward the lungs. Choose it for the chamber that sends blood into the pulmonary circuit, not where oxygen is added.
The left atrium receives blood that is already oxygen-rich, delivered by the pulmonary veins. It would be the answer for the first chamber to receive oxygenated blood.
Correct. Gas exchange in the lung capillaries oxygenates the blood.
The pulmonary trunk carries oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle toward the lungs. Its thick wall does not allow gas exchange; pick it for the vessel just past the pulmonary valve.
questions.answerText: Lungs

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which chamber of the heart receives oxygen-rich blood returning from the lungs?
options: Right ventricle
Right atrium
Left atrium
Left ventricle
questions.why: Oxygen-rich blood leaves the lungs in the four pulmonary veins, and these empty into the left atrium. The left atrium then passes the blood through the mitral valve into the left ventricle, which pumps it out to the body.
notes: The right ventricle holds oxygen-poor blood and pumps it to the lungs. Pick it for the chamber that starts the pulmonary circuit.
The right atrium receives oxygen-poor blood from the body through the venae cavae and from the heart wall through the coronary sinus. Choose it for where returning systemic blood enters the heart.
Correct. The pulmonary veins empty into the left atrium.
The left ventricle does hold oxygen-rich blood, but it receives it from the left atrium, not directly from the lungs. It is the answer for the chamber that pumps blood into the aorta.
questions.answerText: Left atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Blood enters the left ventricle through which valve?
options: Pulmonary valve
Mitral valve
Aortic valve
Tricuspid valve
questions.why: The mitral valve, also called the bicuspid valve because it has two cusps, is the left atrioventricular valve. It lies between the left atrium and the left ventricle, so blood passes through it to fill the left ventricle. When the ventricle contracts, the mitral valve closes to keep blood from flowing back into the left atrium.
notes: The pulmonary valve lets blood leave the right ventricle for the pulmonary trunk. Pick it for the exit valve on the right side of the heart.
Correct. The mitral valve opens from the left atrium into the left ventricle.
The aortic valve is how blood leaves the left ventricle, not how it enters. Choose it for the valve between the left ventricle and the aorta.

The tricuspid valve is the right atrioventricular valve, letting blood into the right ventricle. It is the mirror image of the mitral valve and would be right for the same question about the right ventricle.
questions.answerText: Mitral valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which valve must blood pass through just before entering the aorta?
options: Aortic valve
Tricuspid valve
Mitral valve
Pulmonary valve
questions.why: The aortic valve is the semilunar valve between the left ventricle and the aorta. When the left ventricle contracts, the valve's three pocket-shaped cusps open and blood flows into the aorta. When the ventricle relaxes, the cusps fill with blood and close, keeping blood from falling back into the ventricle.
notes: Correct. The aortic valve opens from the left ventricle into the aorta.
The tricuspid valve lies between the right atrium and the right ventricle. Choose it for the first valve blood crosses after entering the heart from the venae cavae.
The mitral valve lies between the left atrium and the left ventricle, one step earlier in the pathway. It is the answer for the valve blood crosses to enter the left ventricle.
The pulmonary valve sits between the right ventricle and the pulmonary trunk. It is the right-side counterpart and would be correct for the valve just before the pulmonary trunk.
questions.answerText: Aortic valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Through which vessel does blood leave the heart to begin the systemic circuit?
options: Pulmonary trunk
Aorta
Superior vena cava
Pulmonary veins
questions.why: The systemic circuit is the loop that carries blood from the left side of the heart out to the body and back. It begins when the left ventricle pumps oxygen-rich blood through the aortic valve into the aorta, the largest artery, whose branches reach every region of the body.
notes: The pulmonary trunk is where blood leaves the heart to begin the pulmonary circuit to the lungs. Choose it for the outflow vessel of the right ventricle.
Correct. The aorta carries blood out of the left ventricle to the body.
The superior vena cava brings blood back into the right atrium at the end of the systemic circuit. It would be the answer for where blood from the upper body returns, not where it leaves.
The pulmonary veins bring oxygen-rich blood into the left atrium at the end of the pulmonary circuit. They carry blood toward the heart, not out to the body.
questions.answerText: Aorta

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Blood returning from the body enters the heart. Which sequence lists the first three structures it meets, in order?
options: Right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle
Right atrium, mitral valve, right ventricle
Right ventricle, tricuspid valve, right atrium
Left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle
questions.why: Blood from the body arrives in the venae cavae, which empty into the right atrium. From there it passes through the tricuspid valve, the right atrioventricular valve, and fills the right ventricle. The right ventricle then pumps it toward the lungs.
notes: Correct. Right atrium, then tricuspid valve, then right ventricle.
The mitral valve is on the left side, between the left atrium and left ventricle. This sequence puts a left-side valve on the right side, a common mix-up between the two atrioventricular valves.
This lists the right structures in reverse order. Blood always moves from atrium to ventricle, so the atrium comes first; this order would mean blood flowing backward.
This is the correct sequence for oxygen-rich blood returning from the lungs through the pulmonary veins. It would be right if the question started on the left side of the heart.
questions.answerText: Right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Blood has left the pulmonary trunk through the pulmonary arteries. Which sequence does it follow next?
options: Lungs, pulmonary veins, right atrium
Aorta, lungs, left atrium
Lungs, pulmonary veins, left atrium
Lungs, venae cavae, right atrium
questions.why: The pulmonary arteries carry oxygen-poor blood into the lungs, where it picks up oxygen in the capillaries around the alveoli. The now oxygen-rich blood drains into the pulmonary veins, and the four pulmonary veins empty into the left atrium. This completes the pulmonary circuit.
notes: The pulmonary veins do drain the lungs, but they empty into the left atrium. The right atrium receives the venae cavae and the coronary sinus, so this sequence ends in the wrong chamber.
The aorta carries blood from the left ventricle to the body and is not part of the pulmonary circuit. It comes later, after the left atrium and left ventricle.
Correct. Lungs, then pulmonary veins, then left atrium.
The venae cavae return oxygen-poor blood from the body to the right atrium at the end of the systemic circuit. This sequence would fit blood coming back from the body, not from the lungs.
questions.answerText: Lungs, pulmonary veins, left atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Starting in the left atrium, which sequence does blood follow next?
options: Mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve
Aortic valve, left ventricle, mitral valve
Mitral valve, left ventricle, pulmonary valve
Tricuspid valve, left ventricle, aortic valve
questions.why: From the left atrium, blood passes through the mitral valve, the left atrioventricular valve, into the left ventricle. The left ventricle, the thickest-walled chamber, then contracts and pushes the blood through the aortic valve into the aorta. Each valve opens only in the forward direction, so the order is fixed.
notes: Correct. Mitral valve, then left ventricle, then aortic valve.
These are the right valves listed backward. Blood enters the left ventricle through the mitral valve and leaves through the aortic valve, never the reverse.
The pulmonary valve is the exit of the right ventricle, not the left. This sequence would need to be on the right side, leading to the pulmonary trunk, for that valve to appear.
The tricuspid valve is the right atrioventricular valve, between the right atrium and right ventricle. It would start the sequence if the question began in the right atrium.
questions.answerText: Mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: The pulmonary valve sits between which two structures?
options: Right atrium and right ventricle
Pulmonary trunk and pulmonary arteries
Left ventricle and aorta
Right ventricle and pulmonary trunk
questions.why: The pulmonary valve is a semilunar valve with three pocket-shaped cusps at the exit of the right ventricle. Blood pushed out of the right ventricle passes through it into the pulmonary trunk, and when the ventricle relaxes the cusps fill and close so blood cannot fall back into the ventricle.
notes: The tricuspid valve sits between the right atrium and right ventricle. Choose this pair for the right atrioventricular valve.

The pulmonary trunk simply divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries, with no valve at the split. This pair would be the answer for where the pulmonary trunk branches, not where a valve sits.
The aortic valve sits between the left ventricle and the aorta. It is the left-side twin of the pulmonary valve and would be right for the same question about the aortic valve.
Correct. The pulmonary valve guards the opening from the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk.
questions.answerText: Right ventricle and pulmonary trunk

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which structure lies immediately before the mitral valve in the pathway of blood?
options: Left ventricle
Right atrium
Left atrium
Pulmonary trunk
questions.why: The mitral valve is the left atrioventricular valve, so it connects the left atrium above to the left ventricle below. Blood collects in the left atrium from the pulmonary veins and then passes through the mitral valve into the left ventricle, which makes the left atrium the structure just before it.
notes: The left ventricle comes immediately after the mitral valve, not before it. It would be the answer for the chamber that the mitral valve opens into.
The right atrium sits immediately before the tricuspid valve, the right atrioventricular valve. Choose it if the question asked about the tricuspid valve instead.
Correct. The left atrium empties through the mitral valve.
The pulmonary trunk is the vessel just past the pulmonary valve, carrying blood to the lungs. It is several steps earlier in the pathway and has no direct connection to the mitral valve.
questions.answerText: Left atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: The aortic valve sits between which two structures?
options: Right ventricle and pulmonary trunk
Left atrium and left ventricle
Left ventricle and aorta
Aorta and brachiocephalic trunk
questions.why: The aortic valve is a semilunar valve with three cusps that guards the exit of the left ventricle. Blood forced out of the left ventricle passes through it into the ascending aorta. When the ventricle relaxes, the cusps fill and close so blood cannot leak back into the left ventricle.
notes: The pulmonary valve sits between the right ventricle and the pulmonary trunk. It is the right-side twin of the aortic valve.
The mitral valve sits between the left atrium and the left ventricle. Choose this pair for the left atrioventricular valve, one step earlier in the pathway.
Correct. The aortic valve opens from the left ventricle into the aorta.

The brachiocephalic trunk is the first branch off the aortic arch, and there is no valve where it leaves the aorta. This pair would describe where the aortic arch first branches, not where a heart valve sits.
questions.answerText: Left ventricle and aorta

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: When the right ventricle contracts, which valve opens to let blood leave it?
options: Mitral valve
Aortic valve
Tricuspid valve
Pulmonary valve
questions.why: When the right ventricle contracts, the pressure inside it pushes the pulmonary valve open and blood flows into the pulmonary trunk. At the same moment the tricuspid valve is forced shut, so blood cannot return to the right atrium. Each ventricle has an inlet valve that closes and an outlet valve that opens when it contracts.
notes: The mitral valve is the inlet of the left ventricle and closes when that ventricle contracts. It would be right for the valve that stops backflow into the left atrium.
The aortic valve opens when the left ventricle contracts, letting blood into the aorta. Choose it for the outlet valve of the left ventricle.

The tricuspid valve is the inlet of the right ventricle, and it closes, not opens, when the ventricle contracts. It would be the answer for the valve that stops blood from flowing back into the right atrium.
Correct. The pulmonary valve is the outlet of the right ventricle.
questions.answerText: Pulmonary valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which chamber contracts to push blood into the aorta?
options: Left ventricle
Left atrium
Right ventricle
Right atrium
questions.why: The left ventricle is the last chamber blood passes through before leaving for the body. When it contracts, it forces oxygen-rich blood through the aortic valve into the aorta. Because it has to push blood through the entire systemic circuit, it has the thickest wall of the four chambers.
notes: Correct. The left ventricle pumps blood through the aortic valve into the aorta.
The left atrium contracts to top off the left ventricle through the mitral valve. It sits one step earlier and never connects directly to the aorta.
The right ventricle pushes blood into the pulmonary trunk, not the aorta. It would be the answer for the chamber that sends blood to the lungs.
The right atrium pushes blood into the right ventricle through the tricuspid valve. Choose it for the chamber that receives the venae cavae.
questions.answerText: Left ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Why is the left ventricle the last chamber blood passes through before entering the systemic circuit?
options: It pumps blood straight into the aorta through the aortic valve
It empties into the right atrium through the coronary sinus
It receives blood directly from both venae cavae
It sends blood to the lungs through the pulmonary trunk
questions.why: The systemic circuit begins at the aorta, and the left ventricle is the only chamber that opens into it. Blood passes from the left atrium through the mitral valve into the left ventricle, and when the ventricle contracts it pushes the blood through the aortic valve into the aorta. No other chamber lies between the left ventricle and the body.
notes: Correct. The left ventricle opens directly into the aorta, the start of the systemic circuit.
The coronary sinus collects blood from the heart wall and empties into the right atrium. Chambers do not drain into it; it would be the answer for how venous blood from the myocardium returns.
The venae cavae empty into the right atrium, the first chamber of the pathway, not the last. This statement describes the right atrium.
The pulmonary trunk leaves the right ventricle and carries blood to the lungs. This describes the right ventricle, the last chamber before the pulmonary circuit.
questions.answerText: It pumps blood straight into the aorta through the aortic valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Trace blood from the venae cavae to the pulmonary trunk. Which sequence is correct?
options: Right ventricle, tricuspid valve, right atrium, pulmonary valve
Right atrium, pulmonary valve, right ventricle, tricuspid valve
Right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve
Right atrium, mitral valve, right ventricle, aortic valve
questions.why: The venae cavae empty into the right atrium. Blood passes through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, and when the right ventricle contracts it pushes the blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk. Each side of the heart follows the same pattern: atrium, atrioventricular valve, ventricle, semilunar valve.
notes: This puts the right ventricle before the right atrium, which would mean blood flowing backward. The atrium always receives blood first and then fills the ventricle.

This swaps the two right-side valves. The tricuspid valve lies between the right atrium and right ventricle and the pulmonary valve guards the exit of the right ventricle, so the tricuspid comes first.
Correct. Right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, then the pulmonary trunk.
This uses the left-side valves on the right side. The mitral and aortic valves belong to the left heart; this pattern would fit a trace from the left atrium to the aorta.
questions.answerText: Right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Trace blood from the pulmonary veins to the aorta. Which sequence is correct?
options: Left atrium, aortic valve, left ventricle, mitral valve
Left ventricle, mitral valve, left atrium, aortic valve
Left atrium, tricuspid valve, left ventricle, pulmonary valve
Left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve
questions.why: The pulmonary veins empty into the left atrium. Blood passes through the mitral valve into the left ventricle, and when the left ventricle contracts it forces the blood through the aortic valve into the aorta. This mirrors the right side, with the mitral valve as the atrioventricular valve and the aortic valve as the semilunar valve.
notes: This swaps the two left-side valves. The mitral valve is the inlet of the left ventricle and the aortic valve is its outlet, so the mitral valve comes first.
This places the left ventricle before the left atrium, which would mean blood flowing backward. The pulmonary veins enter the left atrium, so the atrium has to come first.
The tricuspid and pulmonary valves are on the right side of the heart. This sequence would fit a trace through the right heart from the venae cavae to the pulmonary trunk.
Correct. Left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, then the aorta.
questions.answerText: Left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Blood returning from the body passes through the pulmonary circuit before the left ventricle sends it back out. Why does this order matter?
options: Blood must pick up oxygen in the lungs before reaching the tissues
Blood must lose its pressure in the lungs before entering the aorta
The lungs add nutrients absorbed from the digestive tract
The lungs remove worn-out red blood cells from circulation
questions.why: Blood returning from the body is oxygen-poor because the tissues have used its O2. The right side of the heart sends this blood to the lungs, where it picks up oxygen and gives off CO2, and only then does it return to the left side to be pumped out through the aorta. Running the lung loop first means the body always receives freshly oxygenated blood.
notes: Correct. The pulmonary circuit oxygenates blood before the systemic circuit delivers it.

Blood does lose pressure as it passes through the lung capillaries, but that is not the reason for the order. The left ventricle has to rebuild the pressure to drive blood through the body; the purpose of the lung loop is oxygenation.
Nutrients from digestion enter the blood in the intestines and travel to the liver through the hepatic portal system. The lungs exchange gases, not nutrients.
Removing worn-out red blood cells is a job of the spleen and liver, not the lungs. Choose the spleen for a question about where old red blood cells are broken down.
questions.answerText: Blood must pick up oxygen in the lungs before reaching the tissues

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In the normal pathway of blood through the heart, oxygen-poor blood leaving the superior vena cava enters which chamber next?
options: Left ventricle
Right atrium
Left atrium
Right ventricle
questions.why: The superior vena cava returns oxygen-poor blood from the head, neck, and upper limbs and empties straight into the right atrium. The right atrium is the receiving chamber for blood coming back from the body, so it is always the first chamber blood enters after either vena cava. From there the blood moves on through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle.
notes: The left ventricle receives blood from the left atrium through the mitral valve and pumps it into the aorta. It would be the answer if the question started at the mitral valve.
Correct. The superior vena cava empties directly into the right atrium.
The left atrium receives oxygen-rich blood from the four pulmonary veins, not blood from the venae cavae. Pick it if the question started at the pulmonary veins.
The right ventricle is one step later. Blood reaches it only after leaving the right atrium and crossing the tricuspid valve. It would be the answer if the question started at the tricuspid valve.
questions.answerText: Right atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Blood returning from the legs travels up the inferior vena cava. Which chamber of the heart does it enter next?
options: Left ventricle
Left atrium
Right atrium
Right ventricle
questions.why: The inferior vena cava carries oxygen-poor blood from the trunk and lower limbs and opens into the right atrium, just as the superior vena cava does from above. Both venae cavae deliver blood from the body to the right atrium, which starts the trip toward the lungs. Next the blood passes through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle.
notes: The left ventricle pumps oxygen-rich blood into the aorta and never receives blood straight from the venae cavae. It would be right if the question started at the mitral valve.
The left atrium receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs through the pulmonary veins. It would be the answer if the blood were returning from the lungs instead of the legs.
Correct. The inferior vena cava empties into the right atrium.
The right ventricle is the chamber after the right atrium, reached by crossing the tricuspid valve. Pick it if the question started at the tricuspid valve.
questions.answerText: Right atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In the normal pathway of blood through the heart, blood leaving the right atrium passes through which valve next?
options: Mitral valve
Pulmonary valve
Tricuspid valve
Aortic valve
questions.why: The tricuspid valve is the atrioventricular valve between the right atrium and the right ventricle. An atrioventricular valve sits between an atrium and the ventricle below it. Blood in the right atrium flows down through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, and the valve closes to keep it from flowing back.
notes: The mitral valve is the atrioventricular valve on the left side, between the left atrium and the left ventricle. It would be the answer if the blood were leaving the left atrium.
The pulmonary valve sits between the right ventricle and the pulmonary trunk, one chamber later. Pick it if the question asked which valve blood crosses as it leaves the right ventricle.
Correct. The tricuspid valve guards the opening from the right atrium into the right ventricle.
The aortic valve sits between the left ventricle and the aorta, on the opposite side of the heart. It would be right if the question asked which valve blood crosses as it leaves the left ventricle.
questions.answerText: Tricuspid valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In the normal pathway of blood through the heart, blood that has just crossed the tricuspid valve enters which chamber?
options: Left ventricle
Right atrium
Left atrium
Right ventricle
questions.why: The tricuspid valve lies between the right atrium and the right ventricle, so blood that crosses it lands in the right ventricle. The right ventricle then contracts and pumps the blood upward through the pulmonary valve toward the lungs. Its chordae tendineae and papillary muscles hold the tricuspid cusps shut during that contraction.
notes: The left ventricle sits below the mitral valve, not the tricuspid valve. Pick it if the blood had just crossed the mitral valve.
The right atrium is the chamber blood came from before the tricuspid valve, not the one it enters after. It would be the answer if the question started at the venae cavae.
The left atrium receives blood from the pulmonary veins and sits above the mitral valve. It would be the answer if the question started at the pulmonary veins.
Correct. Blood that crosses the tricuspid valve enters the right ventricle.
questions.answerText: Right ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In the normal pathway of blood through the heart, the right ventricle pumps blood out through which valve?
options: Aortic valve
Pulmonary valve
Tricuspid valve
Mitral valve
questions.why: The pulmonary valve is a semilunar valve between the right ventricle and the pulmonary trunk. Semilunar valves have pocket-shaped cusps and guard the exits from the ventricles into the great arteries. When the right ventricle contracts, the pulmonary valve opens and blood moves into the pulmonary trunk on its way to the lungs.
notes: The aortic valve is the exit valve of the left ventricle, leading into the aorta. It would be the answer if the question asked how the left ventricle sends blood to the body.
Correct. The pulmonary valve is the exit from the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk.

The tricuspid valve is the entrance to the right ventricle from the right atrium, so it closes when the ventricle contracts. Pick it if the question asked which valve blood crosses to get into the right ventricle.
The mitral valve is the entrance to the left ventricle from the left atrium. It would be right if the question asked which valve blood crosses on its way out of the left atrium.
questions.answerText: Pulmonary valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In the normal pathway of blood through the heart, blood that has just passed the pulmonary valve enters which vessel?
options: Aorta
Pulmonary veins
Right and left pulmonary arteries
Pulmonary trunk
questions.why: The pulmonary valve opens directly into the pulmonary trunk, the single large artery that leaves the right ventricle. A short distance above the heart, the pulmonary trunk divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries, which carry the oxygen-poor blood to the two lungs.
notes: The aorta leaves the left ventricle through the aortic valve and carries oxygen-rich blood to the body. Pick it if the blood had just crossed the aortic valve.

The pulmonary veins carry oxygen-rich blood from the lungs back to the left atrium, so they are at the far end of the pulmonary circuit. They would be the answer if the question asked which vessels leave the lungs.
The right and left pulmonary arteries come one step later, where the pulmonary trunk branches. They would be the answer if the question started at the pulmonary trunk.
Correct. The pulmonary valve opens into the pulmonary trunk.
questions.answerText: Pulmonary trunk

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In the adult pathway of blood, the pulmonary trunk divides into which vessels?
options: Four pulmonary veins
Right and left pulmonary arteries
Right and left brachiocephalic veins
Right and left coronary arteries
questions.why: The pulmonary trunk is a short, wide artery that leaves the right ventricle and splits into the right and left pulmonary arteries. Each pulmonary artery enters a lung at its hilum and carries oxygen-poor blood to the lung capillaries. These are arteries because they carry blood away from the heart, even though the blood in them is low in oxygen.
notes: The four pulmonary veins return oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium. Pick them if the question asked which vessels blood takes after the lungs.
Correct. The pulmonary trunk divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries.
The brachiocephalic veins drain the head and upper limbs and join to form the superior vena cava. They would fit a question about venous return from the head and arms, not the pulmonary circuit.

The right and left coronary arteries branch from the base of the aorta, not the pulmonary trunk, and supply the heart wall itself. They would be the answer if the question asked what branches from the base of the aorta.
questions.answerText: Right and left pulmonary arteries

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In the pulmonary circuit, blood that has picked up oxygen in the lung capillaries leaves the lungs through which vessels?
options: Pulmonary veins
Pulmonary arteries
Pulmonary trunk
Venae cavae
questions.why: After gas exchange in the lung capillaries, oxygen-rich blood collects into the pulmonary veins. There are four of them, two from each lung, and they carry the blood back to the left atrium. They are veins because they carry blood toward the heart, even though their blood is rich in oxygen.
notes: Correct. Oxygen-rich blood leaves the lungs in the pulmonary veins.
The pulmonary arteries carry oxygen-poor blood into the lungs, the step just before the capillaries. They would be the answer if the question asked which vessels deliver blood to the lungs.
The pulmonary trunk is the large artery leaving the right ventricle, two steps before the lungs. It would be the answer if the question started at the pulmonary valve.
The venae cavae return oxygen-poor blood from the body to the right atrium. Pick them if the question asked how blood from the systemic circuit returns to the heart.
questions.answerText: Pulmonary veins

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In the normal pathway of blood through the heart, oxygen-rich blood in the pulmonary veins empties into which chamber?
options: Right atrium
Left atrium
Right ventricle
Left ventricle
questions.why: The four pulmonary veins open into the left atrium, which receives the oxygen-rich blood returning from the lungs. The left atrium makes up most of the base of the heart, on its posterior side. From there blood passes through the mitral valve into the left ventricle.
notes: The right atrium receives oxygen-poor blood from the venae cavae and the coronary sinus. It would be the answer if the question started at either vena cava.
Correct. The pulmonary veins empty into the left atrium.
The right ventricle receives blood from the right atrium and pumps it to the lungs. It would be the answer if the question started at the tricuspid valve.
The left ventricle comes one step later, after the mitral valve. Pick it if the question started at the mitral valve.
questions.answerText: Left atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In the normal pathway of blood through the heart, blood leaving the left atrium passes through which valve next?
options: Aortic valve
Tricuspid valve
Pulmonary valve
Mitral valve
questions.why: The mitral valve, also called the bicuspid valve because it has two cusps, is the atrioventricular valve between the left atrium and the left ventricle. Blood flows down through it into the left ventricle. Chordae tendineae and papillary muscles hold its cusps shut when the left ventricle contracts.
notes: The aortic valve is the exit from the left ventricle into the aorta, one chamber later. It would be the answer if the question asked which valve blood crosses as it leaves the left ventricle.
The tricuspid valve is the atrioventricular valve on the right side, between the right atrium and the right ventricle. Pick it if the blood were leaving the right atrium.
The pulmonary valve is the exit from the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk. It would be right if the question asked how blood leaves the right ventricle.
Correct. The mitral valve separates the left atrium from the left ventricle.
questions.answerText: Mitral valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In the normal pathway of blood through the heart, blood that has just crossed the mitral valve enters which chamber?
options: Left ventricle
Right atrium
Left atrium
Right ventricle
questions.why: The mitral valve lies between the left atrium and the left ventricle, so blood that crosses it enters the left ventricle. The left ventricle has the thickest wall of the four chambers because it pumps blood out through the aortic valve to the entire body.
notes: Correct. Blood that crosses the mitral valve enters the left ventricle.
The right atrium receives blood from the venae cavae and never receives blood through the mitral valve. It would be the answer if the question started at the superior or inferior vena cava.
The left atrium is where the blood was before it crossed the mitral valve. It would be the answer if the question started at the pulmonary veins.
The right ventricle sits below the tricuspid valve, on the right side of the heart. Pick it if the blood had just crossed the tricuspid valve.
questions.answerText: Left ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In the normal pathway of blood through the heart, the left ventricle pumps blood out through which valve?
options: Mitral valve
Pulmonary valve
Tricuspid valve
Aortic valve
questions.why: The aortic valve is the semilunar valve between the left ventricle and the aorta. When the left ventricle contracts, the aortic valve opens and oxygen-rich blood flows into the aorta for delivery to the body. When the ventricle relaxes, the cusps fill and close so blood cannot slip back into the ventricle.
notes: The mitral valve is the entrance to the left ventricle from the left atrium, and it closes when the ventricle contracts. It would be the answer if the question asked which valve blood crosses to get into the left ventricle.
The pulmonary valve is the exit from the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk. Pick it if the question asked how the right ventricle sends blood to the lungs.
The tricuspid valve is the entrance to the right ventricle from the right atrium. It would fit a question about blood leaving the right atrium.
Correct. The aortic valve is the exit from the left ventricle into the aorta.
questions.answerText: Aortic valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In the normal pathway of blood through the heart, blood that has just passed the aortic valve enters which vessel?
options: Pulmonary veins
Inferior vena cava
Pulmonary trunk
Aorta
questions.why: The aortic valve opens directly into the aorta, the largest artery in the body. The aorta carries oxygen-rich blood from the left ventricle out to the systemic circuit. Passing the aortic valve is the last step of blood's trip through the heart before it heads to the body.
notes: The pulmonary veins bring oxygen-rich blood from the lungs into the left atrium, well before the aortic valve. Pick them if the question asked which vessels leave the lungs.

The inferior vena cava returns oxygen-poor blood from the trunk and legs to the right atrium. It would be the answer if the question asked which vessel brings blood from the lower body back to the heart.
The pulmonary trunk receives blood through the pulmonary valve from the right ventricle. It would be the answer if the blood had just passed the pulmonary valve.
Correct. The aortic valve opens into the aorta.
questions.answerText: Aorta

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which sequence correctly traces blood from the superior vena cava to the pulmonary trunk?
options: Superior vena cava, right ventricle, tricuspid valve, right atrium, pulmonary valve, pulmonary trunk
Superior vena cava, right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, pulmonary trunk
Superior vena cava, right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, aortic valve, pulmonary trunk
Superior vena cava, right atrium, mitral valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, pulmonary trunk
questions.why: The superior vena cava empties into the right atrium. Blood then crosses the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, which pumps it through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk. Every structure on this route belongs to the right side of the heart, which drives the pulmonary circuit.
notes: This sequence reverses the right atrium and right ventricle. The atrium is the receiving chamber, so blood from a vena cava must enter the right atrium first. The ventricle is the pumping chamber that comes after the tricuspid valve.
Correct. This is the full right-side route from the superior vena cava to the pulmonary trunk.

This sequence uses the aortic valve as the exit from the right ventricle. The aortic valve guards the exit from the left ventricle into the aorta, so it would belong in a trace that ends at the aorta.

This sequence puts the mitral valve between the right atrium and right ventricle. The mitral valve is on the left side, between the left atrium and left ventricle, so it would belong in a trace from the pulmonary veins to the aorta.
questions.answerText: Superior vena cava, right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, pulmonary trunk

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Blood travels from the inferior vena cava to the lungs. Which two heart valves does it cross, in order?
options: Pulmonary valve, then tricuspid valve
Tricuspid valve, then pulmonary valve
Mitral valve, then aortic valve
Tricuspid valve, then aortic valve
questions.why: Blood from the inferior vena cava enters the right atrium and crosses the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle. The right ventricle then pumps it through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk, which branches to the lungs. On each side of the heart, blood crosses the atrioventricular valve first and the semilunar valve second.
notes: These are the right valves in the wrong order. Blood must enter the right ventricle through the tricuspid valve before the ventricle can pump it out through the pulmonary valve.
Correct. The tricuspid valve comes first, then the pulmonary valve.

The mitral and aortic valves are the two left-side valves. Blood crosses them, in that order, on the way from the lungs to the body, so they would be the answer for a trace from the pulmonary veins to the aorta.
The tricuspid valve is right, but the aortic valve is the exit from the left ventricle, not the right. It would fit only if the question were about blood leaving the left ventricle for the body.
questions.answerText: Tricuspid valve, then pulmonary valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which sequence correctly traces oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the aorta?
options: Pulmonary veins, left atrium, tricuspid valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, aorta
Pulmonary veins, left ventricle, mitral valve, left atrium, aortic valve, aorta
Pulmonary arteries, left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, aorta
Pulmonary veins, left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, aorta
questions.why: Oxygen-rich blood leaves the lungs in the pulmonary veins, which empty into the left atrium. It crosses the mitral valve into the left ventricle, and the left ventricle pumps it through the aortic valve into the aorta. This is the left side of the heart, which drives the systemic circuit.
notes: This sequence uses the tricuspid valve on the left side. The tricuspid valve sits between the right atrium and right ventricle, so it belongs in a trace from the venae cavae to the lungs.
This sequence swaps the left atrium and left ventricle. The pulmonary veins empty into the left atrium, the receiving chamber, and the left ventricle comes after the mitral valve.

This sequence starts with the pulmonary arteries. Those carry oxygen-poor blood into the lungs from the pulmonary trunk, so they belong in a trace from the right ventricle to the lungs, not out of the lungs.
Correct. This is the full left-side route from the lungs to the aorta.
questions.answerText: Pulmonary veins, left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, aorta

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Which chamber pumps blood into the pulmonary circuit, and which chamber receives it when it returns?
options: Leaves from the left ventricle, returns to the right atrium
Leaves from the right ventricle, returns to the left atrium
Leaves from the right atrium, returns to the left ventricle
Leaves from the left atrium, returns to the right ventricle
questions.why: The pulmonary circuit is the loop to the lungs and back. The right ventricle pumps oxygen-poor blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk and pulmonary arteries. After gas exchange in the lungs, the pulmonary veins return oxygen-rich blood to the left atrium, which ends the circuit.
notes: This describes the systemic circuit, which leaves the left ventricle through the aorta and returns through the venae cavae to the right atrium. It would be the answer if the question asked about the systemic circuit.
Correct. The right ventricle sends blood to the lungs and the left atrium receives it back.

Atria are receiving chambers, so the right atrium does not pump blood into a circuit, and the left ventricle does not receive blood from the lungs. This pairing mixes up which chambers receive and which pump.
This reverses the true flow. The left atrium receives blood from the lungs rather than sending it out, and the right ventricle never receives blood straight from the lungs.
questions.answerText: Leaves from the right ventricle, returns to the left atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: In the systemic circuit, which vessel carries blood out of the heart, and which vessels bring it back?
options: Pulmonary trunk carries it out, venae cavae bring it back
Aorta carries it out, pulmonary veins bring it back
Aorta carries it out, venae cavae bring it back
Pulmonary trunk carries it out, pulmonary veins bring it back
questions.why: The systemic circuit is the loop from the left side of the heart out to the body and back to the right side. The left ventricle pumps oxygen-rich blood into the aorta, which branches into arteries, arterioles, and capillaries throughout the body. The blood then returns through venules and veins to the superior and inferior venae cavae, which empty into the right atrium.
notes: The venae cavae are the right returning vessels, but the pulmonary trunk carries blood to the lungs, not the body. It is the outgoing vessel of the pulmonary circuit.
The aorta is the right outgoing vessel, but the pulmonary veins return blood from the lungs, not from the body. They belong to the pulmonary circuit.
Correct. The aorta begins the systemic circuit and the venae cavae end it.
The pulmonary trunk and pulmonary veins are the outgoing and returning vessels of the pulmonary circuit. They would be the answer if the question asked about the loop to the lungs.
questions.answerText: Aorta carries it out, venae cavae bring it back

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Tracing blood backward through the heart, which chamber does blood occupy just before it crosses the tricuspid valve?
options: Right atrium
Left ventricle
Right ventricle
Left atrium
questions.why: The tricuspid valve separates the right atrium above from the right ventricle below. Blood in the right atrium flows down through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, so the right atrium is the chamber just before it. Reading the pathway backward like this checks that you know what each valve separates.
notes: Correct. Blood is in the right atrium just before it crosses the tricuspid valve.
The left ventricle sits below the mitral valve and above the aortic valve. It would be the answer if the question asked which chamber comes just before the aortic valve.

The right ventricle is where blood arrives after crossing the tricuspid valve, not where it comes from. It would be the answer if the question asked which chamber comes just before the pulmonary valve.
The left atrium sits above the mitral valve, not the tricuspid valve. It would be the answer if the question asked which chamber comes just before the mitral valve.
questions.answerText: Right atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Tracing blood backward through the heart, blood that has just passed the pulmonary valve was pumped out by which chamber?
options: Right ventricle
Left ventricle
Left atrium
Right atrium
questions.why: The pulmonary valve sits between the right ventricle and the pulmonary trunk. When the right ventricle contracts, the pulmonary valve opens and blood moves into the pulmonary trunk. So any blood that has just passed the pulmonary valve came from the right ventricle.
notes: Correct. The right ventricle pumps blood out through the pulmonary valve.
The left ventricle pumps blood through the aortic valve into the aorta, not through the pulmonary valve. It would be the answer if the blood had just passed the aortic valve.
The left atrium empties through the mitral valve into the left ventricle. It would be the answer if the blood had just crossed the mitral valve.
The right atrium empties through the tricuspid valve, not the pulmonary valve. It would be the answer if the blood had just crossed the tricuspid valve.
questions.answerText: Right ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Tracing blood backward through the heart, blood that has just crossed the mitral valve came from which chamber?
options: Right ventricle
Right atrium
Left ventricle
Left atrium
questions.why: The mitral valve is the atrioventricular valve between the left atrium and the left ventricle. Blood from the pulmonary veins collects in the left atrium and then flows down through the mitral valve into the left ventricle. So blood that has just crossed the mitral valve came from the left atrium.
notes: The right ventricle pumps blood through the pulmonary valve, not the mitral valve. It would be the answer if the blood had just passed the pulmonary valve.
The right atrium empties through the tricuspid valve on the right side. It would be the answer if the blood had just crossed the tricuspid valve.
The left ventricle is where blood ends up after crossing the mitral valve, not where it comes from. It would be the answer if the blood had just passed the aortic valve.
Correct. Blood crosses the mitral valve on its way from the left atrium to the left ventricle.
questions.answerText: Left atrium

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: Tracing blood backward through the heart, blood that has just passed the aortic valve was pumped out by which chamber?
options: Left ventricle
Right ventricle
Left atrium
Right atrium
questions.why: The aortic valve sits between the left ventricle and the aorta. The left ventricle, the chamber with the thickest wall, contracts and forces blood through the aortic valve into the aorta for delivery to the body. Blood that has just passed the aortic valve therefore came from the left ventricle.
notes: Correct. The left ventricle pumps blood out through the aortic valve.
The right ventricle pumps blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk. It would be the answer if the blood had just passed the pulmonary valve.
The left atrium empties through the mitral valve into the left ventricle, one step earlier. It would be the answer if the blood had just crossed the mitral valve.
The right atrium empties through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle. It would be the answer if the blood had just crossed the tricuspid valve.
questions.answerText: Left ventricle

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: A clot from a calf vein has traveled up to the right atrium. Which valve will it cross next?
options: Tricuspid valve
Aortic valve
Mitral valve
Pulmonary valve
questions.why: A clot in a vein follows normal venous return. From the right atrium, blood flows down through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, so the tricuspid valve is the next valve the clot meets. In a normal adult heart there is no opening in the interatrial septum, so the clot cannot cross to the left side.
notes: Correct. From the right atrium the clot crosses the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle.

The aortic valve is the exit from the left ventricle into the aorta. It would be the answer if the clot had somehow reached the left ventricle, which a venous clot cannot do without crossing the lungs.

The mitral valve is on the left side, between the left atrium and left ventricle. A clot could only reach it by first passing through the lungs, so it would be the answer for blood leaving the left atrium.
The pulmonary valve is the exit from the right ventricle, one chamber later. The clot will cross it after it has passed the tricuspid valve and entered the right ventricle.
questions.answerText: Tricuspid valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: A clot is being pumped out of the right ventricle. Which valve does it cross as it leaves?
options: Mitral valve
Pulmonary valve
Aortic valve
Tricuspid valve
questions.why: The right ventricle pumps blood out through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk. A clot riding in that blood crosses the pulmonary valve and heads for the lungs. This is why a clot from the venous side lodges in a pulmonary artery rather than going out to the body.
notes: The mitral valve lets blood from the left atrium into the left ventricle. It would be the answer for a clot moving from the left atrium into the left ventricle.
Correct. Blood and anything in it leave the right ventricle through the pulmonary valve.
The aortic valve is the exit from the left ventricle. It would be the answer for a clot leaving the left ventricle, which would travel out to the body instead of the lungs.
The tricuspid valve is the entrance to the right ventricle, and it closes when the ventricle contracts. The clot already crossed it on the way in from the right atrium.
questions.answerText: Pulmonary valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: A clot has just passed through the pulmonary valve. Which vessel does it enter?
options: Pulmonary veins
Aorta
Pulmonary trunk
Superior vena cava
questions.why: The pulmonary valve opens into the pulmonary trunk, so a clot that passes the valve enters the pulmonary trunk. The trunk then splits into the right and left pulmonary arteries, which carry the clot toward the lungs. As those arteries branch and narrow, the clot lodges and blocks flow, which is a pulmonary embolism.
notes: The pulmonary veins carry blood out of the lungs to the left atrium, beyond the lungs. A clot would only reach them after somehow passing through the lung capillaries.
The aorta receives blood from the left ventricle through the aortic valve. It would be the answer if the clot had just passed the aortic valve.
Correct. The pulmonary valve opens into the pulmonary trunk.
The superior vena cava brings blood from the upper body into the right atrium, much earlier in the route. It would be the answer if the question asked where a clot from an arm vein enters the heart.
questions.answerText: Pulmonary trunk

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: An echocardiogram shows blood leaking backward from the right ventricle into the right atrium each time the ventricle contracts. Which valve is failing to close?
options: Mitral valve
Aortic valve
Pulmonary valve
Tricuspid valve
questions.why: Regurgitation means blood leaking backward through a valve that does not close fully. The tricuspid valve sits between the right atrium and right ventricle and normally closes when the right ventricle contracts. If blood leaks from the right ventricle back into the right atrium, the tricuspid valve is the one failing.
notes: The mitral valve separates the left atrium and left ventricle. It would be the answer if blood leaked from the left ventricle into the left atrium.
The aortic valve separates the left ventricle and aorta. It would be the answer if blood leaked from the aorta back into the left ventricle.
The pulmonary valve sits between the right ventricle and pulmonary trunk. If it failed, blood would leak from the pulmonary trunk back into the right ventricle, not into the right atrium.
Correct. The tricuspid valve separates the right atrium from the right ventricle.
questions.answerText: Tricuspid valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: An echocardiogram shows blood leaking backward from the left ventricle into the left atrium each time the ventricle contracts. Which valve is failing to close?
options: Tricuspid valve
Mitral valve
Pulmonary valve
Aortic valve
questions.why: The mitral valve is the atrioventricular valve between the left atrium and the left ventricle. Its chordae tendineae and papillary muscles hold it shut when the left ventricle contracts. If blood leaks from the left ventricle back into the left atrium, the mitral valve is not closing properly.
notes: The tricuspid valve is the matching valve on the right side. It would be the answer if blood leaked from the right ventricle into the right atrium.
Correct. The mitral valve separates the left ventricle from the left atrium.
The pulmonary valve sits between the right ventricle and pulmonary trunk. It would be the answer if blood leaked from the pulmonary trunk back into the right ventricle.
The aortic valve sits between the left ventricle and the aorta. A leaking aortic valve lets blood fall back from the aorta into the left ventricle, not from the ventricle into the atrium.
questions.answerText: Mitral valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: An echocardiogram shows blood falling back from the aorta into the left ventricle each time the ventricle relaxes. Which valve is failing to close?
options: Pulmonary valve
Tricuspid valve
Aortic valve
Mitral valve
questions.why: The aortic valve is the semilunar valve between the left ventricle and the aorta. When the ventricle relaxes, its pocket-shaped cusps fill with blood and snap shut so blood cannot return to the ventricle. Blood falling from the aorta back into the left ventricle means the aortic valve is not sealing.
notes: The pulmonary valve is the semilunar valve on the right side. It would be the answer if blood fell back from the pulmonary trunk into the right ventricle.
The tricuspid valve separates the right atrium and right ventricle. It would be the answer if blood leaked from the right ventricle back into the right atrium.
Correct. The aortic valve separates the aorta from the left ventricle.
The mitral valve separates the left atrium and left ventricle. It would be the answer if blood leaked from the left ventricle back into the left atrium.
questions.answerText: Aortic valve

questions.topic: Heart valves and blood flow through the heart
questions.q: An echocardiogram shows blood falling back from the pulmonary trunk into the right ventricle each time the ventricle relaxes. Which valve is failing to close?
options: Tricuspid valve
Pulmonary valve
Mitral valve
Aortic valve
questions.why: The pulmonary valve is the semilunar valve between the right ventricle and the pulmonary trunk. When the right ventricle relaxes, the valve should close so blood in the pulmonary trunk cannot return. Backflow from the pulmonary trunk into the right ventricle points to a pulmonary valve that is not sealing.
