notes: The bundle branches conduct quickly down the septum and do not hold the signal. They would be the answer if the question asked which structures carry the signal toward the apex.

The Purkinje fibers conduct the signal rapidly through the ventricle walls so the ventricles contract together. Choose them if the question asked which structures deliver the signal to the ventricular muscle.
The SA node starts the signal rather than holding it. Pick it if the question asked which structure fires first and sets the pace.
Correct. The AV node holds the signal briefly so the atria can finish emptying.
questions.answerText: The atrioventricular node

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Two named structures of the conduction system sit within the right atrium. Which pair is it?
options: The bundle branches and the Purkinje fibers
The AV node and the Purkinje fibers
The SA node and the AV node
The AV bundle and the bundle branches
questions.why: Both nodes sit in the right atrium. The SA node is in the upper right atrial wall near the opening of the superior vena cava, and the AV node is in the floor of the right atrium near the interatrial septum. Everything after the AV node, from the AV bundle to the Purkinje fibers, lies in the interventricular septum or the ventricle walls.
notes: These are the two structures farthest down the pathway, running toward the apex and through the ventricle walls. They would fit a question about which structures carry the signal within the ventricles.

Only half of this pair is right. The AV node is in the right atrium, but the Purkinje fibers are spread through both ventricle walls, so students pick it when they remember one node but not the other.
Correct. Both the SA node and the AV node are in the right atrium.
These two lie in the interventricular septum, not the right atrium. Pick this pair if the question asked which conduction structures are found within the septum.
questions.answerText: The SA node and the AV node

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Which two conduction structures both lie within the interventricular septum?
options: The AV bundle and the bundle branches
The SA node and the bundle branches
The SA node and the AV node
The AV node and the Purkinje fibers
questions.why: The AV bundle enters the superior part of the interventricular septum and splits into the right and left bundle branches, which run down either side of the septum toward the apex. So both of these structures sit within the septum. The two nodes are above, in the right atrium, and the Purkinje fibers spread out into the ventricle walls.
notes: Correct. The AV bundle and its two branches are the septal part of the pathway.
Only the bundle branches are in the septum. The SA node is high in the right atrial wall near the superior vena cava, at the opposite end of the pathway.
Both nodes are in the right atrium, not the septum between the ventricles. Pick this pair if the question asked which conduction structures lie in the right atrium.

Neither belongs here. The AV node sits in the floor of the right atrium and the Purkinje fibers spread through the ventricle walls; students pick this pair when they mix up the AV node with the AV bundle, whose names are nearly identical.
questions.answerText: The AV bundle and the bundle branches

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: What conduction event does the P wave of an ECG show?
options: The signal spreading across the atria
The signal spreading across the ventricles
The atria electrically recovering
The ventricles electrically recovering
questions.why: The P wave is the first small bump of each heartbeat on an ECG, and it lines up with the signal spreading across both atria right after the SA node fires. The atria contract just after the P wave. The larger QRS complex comes next, showing the signal spreading through the ventricles.
notes: Correct. The P wave shows the signal crossing the atria.
The signal spreading across the ventricles produces the QRS complex, the tall spike after the P wave. Pick it if the question asked what the QRS complex shows.

The atria do recover electrically, but this happens at the same time as the much larger QRS complex, so it is hidden and has no wave of its own. Students choose it by assuming every chamber event must have its own visible wave.
Ventricular recovery shows up as the T wave, the last deflection of the heartbeat. It would be correct if the question asked what the T wave represents.
questions.answerText: The signal spreading across the atria

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: On an ECG, which part of the tracing corresponds to the signal spreading across the ventricles?
options: The flat line after the P wave
The P wave
The T wave
The QRS complex
questions.why: The QRS complex is the tall, sharp spike of each heartbeat, and it lines up with the signal spreading through the ventricles by way of the bundle branches and Purkinje fibers. It is larger than the P wave because the ventricles have far more muscle than the atria. The ventricles contract just after the QRS complex.
notes: The flat line between the P wave and the QRS complex mostly reflects the brief pause at the AV node, when the signal is held before it enters the ventricles. Choose it if the question asked where the AV node delay appears on an ECG.
The P wave is the small first bump, showing the signal spreading across the atria. Pick it if the question asked about the atria.
The T wave comes after the QRS complex and shows the ventricles electrically recovering before they relax. It would be correct if the question asked about ventricular recovery.
Correct. The QRS complex shows the signal sweeping through the ventricles.
questions.answerText: The QRS complex

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Which nerves reach the heart through the cardiac plexus and speed up the heart rate?
options: The parasympathetic nerves
The somatic motor nerves
The phrenic nerves
The sympathetic nerves
questions.why: Sympathetic nerves belong to the part of the autonomic nervous system that prepares the body for activity. Their fibers reach the heart through the cardiac plexus and end on the SA and AV nodes, where they raise the heart rate. They speed up the beat that the SA node already makes; they do not create it.
notes: Parasympathetic fibers also pass through the cardiac plexus, but they slow the heart rate. Pick them if the question asked which autonomic fibers, carried in the vagus nerve, slow the heart.

Somatic motor nerves control skeletal muscle, the voluntary muscle you move on purpose, and they do not supply the heart. They would be the answer if the question asked which nerves stimulate voluntary muscle.

The phrenic nerves run down through the thorax past the heart to reach the diaphragm, and they do not adjust heart rate. Choose them if the question asked which nerves from the cervical plexus travel to the diaphragm.
Correct. Sympathetic fibers speed the rate set by the SA node.
questions.answerText: The sympathetic nerves

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Which term is the umbrella name for any deviation from the normal heart rhythm?
options: Ectopic pacemaker
Tachycardia
Arrhythmia
Heart block
questions.why: Arrhythmia means any deviation from the normal heart rhythm, so it is the umbrella term that covers all the specific conduction disorders. A rhythm that is too fast, too slow, irregular, or started from the wrong place all count as arrhythmias. The other terms each name one particular kind.
notes: An ectopic pacemaker is one specific arrhythmia, in which a site outside the SA node takes over the rhythm. Choose it if the question described the beat starting in the wrong place.
Tachycardia is one specific arrhythmia, an abnormally fast resting heart rate. It would be correct if the question described a heart beating too fast at rest.
Correct. Arrhythmia is the general term that includes all the others.
Heart block is one specific arrhythmia, in which the signal is delayed or stopped at the AV node. Pick it if the question described the atria and ventricles beating out of step.
questions.answerText: Arrhythmia

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Where in the heart does heart block delay or stop the signal?
options: The atrioventricular node
The cardiac plexus
The Purkinje fibers
The sinoatrial node
questions.why: In heart block, the signal from the atria is delayed or stopped at the AV node, so it reaches the ventricles late or not at all. Because the AV node and AV bundle form the only route through the insulating fibrous skeleton, a block here can leave the atria and ventricles beating out of step. An artificial pacemaker can carry the signal past the block.
notes: Correct. Heart block happens at the AV node, between the atria and the ventricles.

The cardiac plexus is a network of autonomic nerves near the base of the heart, not part of the conduction pathway, so the heartbeat signal does not travel through it. Pick it if the question asked how autonomic nerves reach the nodes.
The Purkinje fibers deliver the signal within the ventricle walls. They would be the answer if the question asked which structure hands the signal to the ventricular muscle.
The SA node starts the signal. A failing SA node causes a slow or missing pacemaker signal, which would fit a question about what an artificial pacemaker replaces when the natural pacemaker fails.
questions.answerText: The atrioventricular node

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: If the atrioventricular bundle were destroyed, which two parts of the heart would lose their only electrical connection?
options: The SA node and the AV node
The right ventricle and the left ventricle
The right atrium and the left atrium
The atria and the ventricles
questions.why: The fibrous skeleton is a layer of dense connective tissue between the atria and the ventricles that does not carry electrical signals. The AV bundle is the one strand of conducting tissue that crosses it, so it is the only electrical bridge from the upper chambers to the lower chambers. If it were destroyed, the atria could still beat from the SA node, but their signal could not reach the ventricles.
notes: The SA node and AV node are connected through the atrial muscle, upstream of the AV bundle, so damage to the bundle would not cut them apart. This pair would fit a question about which two structures sit in the right atrium.

Both ventricles receive the signal below the AV bundle, through the right and left bundle branches, so the bundle does not connect them to each other. Students choose this pair because the bundle splits toward the two ventricles, but it links the upper chambers to the lower ones.

The two atria are joined by atrial muscle, and the SA node signal spreads across both of them without using the AV bundle. Pick this pair if the question asked which chambers the signal reaches right after the SA node fires.
Correct. The AV bundle is the only conducting bridge from the atria to the ventricles.
questions.answerText: The atria and the ventricles

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: A conduction structure sits in the right atrial wall near the opening of the superior vena cava and fires first. Which structure is it?
options: The sinoatrial node
The bundle branches
The atrioventricular node
The atrioventricular bundle
questions.why: Two clues point to the SA node: its location in the right atrial wall near the opening of the superior vena cava, and the fact that it fires first. Because it fires faster than any other part of the conduction system, it sets the pace for the whole heart, which is why it is called the natural pacemaker.
notes: Correct. Its location and its role as the first to fire both identify the SA node.
The bundle branches run down both sides of the interventricular septum toward the apex. Choose them if the description mentioned a right and a left portion in the septum.

The AV node is also in the right atrium, but in the floor near the interatrial septum, and it receives the signal after it crosses the atria. Pick it if the description mentioned the floor of the right atrium and a brief delay.
The AV bundle lies in the superior interventricular septum, below the atria. It would be correct for a description of the only electrical bridge between the atria and the ventricles.
questions.answerText: The sinoatrial node

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: A conduction structure lies in the floor of the right atrium near the interatrial septum, where it briefly delays the signal. Which structure is it?
options: The atrioventricular bundle
The Purkinje fibers
The atrioventricular node
The sinoatrial node
questions.why: The floor of the right atrium near the interatrial septum is the home of the AV node, and the brief delay is its signature job. Holding the signal for a moment lets the atria finish emptying into the ventricles before the ventricles contract. After the delay, the AV node passes the signal into the AV bundle.
notes: The AV bundle comes right after the AV node and sits in the superior interventricular septum. Choose it for a description of the only electrical bridge from the atria to the ventricles.

The Purkinje fibers spread through the ventricle walls and conduct quickly rather than holding the signal. They would match a description of a fine network handing the signal to the ventricular muscle.
Correct. The location in the right atrial floor and the delay both identify the AV node.

The SA node is also in the right atrium, but high in the wall near the superior vena cava, and it starts the signal rather than delaying it. Pick it for a description of the structure that fires first.
questions.answerText: The atrioventricular node

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: A conduction structure divides into a right portion and a left portion that run down opposite sides of the interventricular septum. Which step of the pathway is this?
options: The AV bundle dividing into the bundle branches
The AV node passing the signal into the AV bundle
The bundle branches passing the signal to the Purkinje fibers
The SA node passing the signal across the atria
questions.why: The AV bundle enters the top of the interventricular septum and then splits into the right and left bundle branches. These run down opposite sides of the septum toward the apex, one branch for each ventricle. A single structure becoming two portions that travel down the septum fits only this step.
notes: Correct. The AV bundle splits into the right and left bundle branches.
The AV node passes the signal into a single AV bundle; nothing splits into right and left parts at this step. Pick it if the question asked what follows the AV node.

The bundle branches do hand the signal to the Purkinje fibers near the apex, but that step fans out through the ventricle walls rather than splitting into two portions in the septum. Choose it if the question asked what happens at the end of the bundle branches.
The SA node's signal spreads outward across both atria, not down the septum. This would fit a question about the first step after the pacemaker fires.
questions.answerText: The AV bundle dividing into the bundle branches

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: A conduction structure forms a fine network spread throughout both ventricle walls and hands the signal to the working muscle cells. Which structure is it?
options: The Purkinje fibers
The bundle branches
The atrioventricular node
The atrioventricular bundle
questions.why: A fine network spread through both ventricle walls is the Purkinje fibers. They are the last part of the conduction pathway, passing the signal to the contractile cells so the ventricles contract. Because they spread upward from the apex, contraction starts at the bottom of the ventricles and moves toward the top.
notes: Correct. The Purkinje fibers are the network that reaches the ventricular muscle.
The bundle branches are two tracts that run down the interventricular septum, not a network through the walls. Pick them for a description of a right and a left portion in the septum.
The AV node is a compact cluster in the floor of the right atrium that delays the signal. It would fit a description of where the signal pauses.
The AV bundle is a short single strand in the superior interventricular septum. Choose it for a description of the only electrical link between the atria and the ventricles.
questions.answerText: The Purkinje fibers

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: On a normal ECG, which part of the tracing lines up with the ventricles electrically recovering?
options: The QRS complex
The flat line after the P wave
The P wave
The T wave
questions.why: The T wave is the last deflection of each heartbeat, following the QRS complex. It lines up with the ventricles electrically recovering so they are ready for the next signal, and the ventricles relax after it. So the order within one beat is P wave, QRS complex, then T wave.
notes: The QRS complex shows the signal spreading across the ventricles, just before they contract. It would be correct if the question asked about ventricular spread rather than recovery.
The flat line between the P wave and the QRS complex mostly reflects the pause at the AV node. Choose it if the question asked where the AV node delay appears on an ECG.
The P wave is the first small bump, showing the signal spreading across the atria. Pick it if the question asked which deflection comes just before the atria contract.
Correct. The T wave shows the ventricles recovering.
questions.answerText: The T wave

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: On an ECG, which mechanical event follows the P wave?
options: The ventricles relax
The atria contract
The ventricles contract
The SA node fires
questions.why: The P wave shows the signal spreading across both atria, and the atrial muscle contracts right after it. Each deflection works the same way: the electrical event comes first and the mechanical event follows. So the P wave is followed by atrial contraction, the QRS complex by ventricular contraction, and the T wave by ventricular relaxation.
notes: The ventricles relax after the T wave, which shows them electrically recovering. It would be correct if the question asked what follows the T wave.
Correct. The atria contract right after the P wave.
The ventricles contract after the QRS complex, which shows the signal spreading across the ventricles. Pick it if the question asked what follows the QRS complex.

The SA node fires just before the P wave, starting the signal that the P wave then shows spreading across the atria. Students pick it because the SA node starts the beat, but its firing comes before the P wave, not after it.
questions.answerText: The atria contract

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: A conduction disorder is described as a site outside the sinoatrial node taking over the heart's rhythm. Which disorder is it?
options: Heart block
Bradycardia
An ectopic pacemaker
Atrial fibrillation
questions.why: Ectopic means out of place, so an ectopic pacemaker is a site outside the SA node that starts firing and takes over the rhythm. When this happens, the normal pacing order of the heart is lost because the beat no longer starts at the top of the right atrium. The SA node is supposed to be the only pacemaker in a normal heartbeat.
notes: Heart block is a delay or stop of the signal at the AV node, so the problem is a blocked route rather than a new starting point. It would be the answer if the question described the atria and ventricles beating out of step.
Bradycardia is an abnormally slow resting heart rate, which can happen even when the SA node is still in charge. Pick it if the question described a heart rate that is too slow.
Correct. An ectopic pacemaker is a site outside the SA node that takes over.

Atrial fibrillation is rapid, disorganized signaling across the atria so they quiver, not one organized site taking over. Choose it if the question described the atria quivering instead of contracting.
questions.answerText: An ectopic pacemaker

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: A conduction disorder is described as rapid, disorganized signals in the atria, so the atria quiver instead of contracting. Which disorder is it?
options: Atrial fibrillation
Heart block
Ventricular fibrillation
Tachycardia
questions.why: Fibrillation means quivering, and in atrial fibrillation rapid, disorganized signals in the atria make them quiver instead of giving one coordinated squeeze. The ventricles still pump, so the condition is common and treatable rather than immediately fatal. The location in the name tells you which chambers are affected.
notes: Correct. Rapid, disorganized atrial signals make the atria quiver.
Heart block is a delay or stop at the AV node, not chaotic signaling in the atria. Choose it if the question described the signal failing to pass from the atria to the ventricles.

Ventricular fibrillation is the same kind of chaotic signaling, but in the ventricles, so they cannot pump at all. Pick it if the question described the ventricles quivering, a life-threatening emergency.
Tachycardia is an abnormally fast resting heart rate in which the beats are still organized. It would be correct if the question described a heart beating too fast at rest.
questions.answerText: Atrial fibrillation

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: A conduction disorder is described as rapid, disorganized signals in the ventricles, so the ventricles cannot pump. Which disorder is it?
options: Ventricular fibrillation
Atrial fibrillation
Bradycardia
Ectopic pacemaker
questions.why: In ventricular fibrillation, chaotic signals make the ventricles quiver instead of contracting, so they move no blood out to the lungs or body. Because the ventricles are the main pumping chambers, this is a life-threatening emergency. It is treated with a defibrillator, which delivers a shock that stops all the chaotic signals at once.
notes: Correct. Disorganized ventricular signals stop the ventricles from pumping.
Atrial fibrillation is the same chaotic quivering, but in the atria, so the ventricles keep pumping. Pick it if the question described the atria quivering in a common, treatable condition.
Bradycardia is an abnormally slow but organized heart rate, so the ventricles still pump. It would be the answer if the question described a resting heart rate that is too slow.

An ectopic pacemaker is a single site outside the SA node taking over the rhythm, not chaotic signaling throughout the ventricles. Choose it if the question described the beat starting from the wrong place.
questions.answerText: Ventricular fibrillation

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: A conduction disorder is described as an abnormally slow resting heart rate. Which disorder is it?
options: Bradycardia
Atrial fibrillation
Heart block
Tachycardia
questions.why: Bradycardia is an abnormally slow resting heart rate. The prefix brady means slow and cardia refers to the heart. The concern is that a heart beating too slowly may not deliver enough blood flow to the body.
notes: Correct. Brady means slow, so bradycardia is a slow resting heart rate.
Atrial fibrillation is rapid, disorganized signaling in the atria that makes them quiver. It would be the answer if the question described the atria quivering instead of contracting.

Heart block is a delay or stop of the signal at the AV node. It can slow the ventricles, but the disorder is defined by the blocked route, so choose it if the question described the atria and ventricles beating out of step.
Tachycardia is the opposite, an abnormally fast resting heart rate (tachy means fast). Pick it if the question described a heart beating too fast at rest.
questions.answerText: Bradycardia

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Which sequence lists the conduction structures in the order the signal travels, starting at the pacemaker?
options: SA node, AV node, bundle branches, AV bundle, Purkinje fibers
SA node, AV node, AV bundle, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
SA node, AV bundle, AV node, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
AV node, SA node, bundle branches, AV bundle, Purkinje fibers
questions.why: The signal starts at the SA node in the right atrial wall, crosses both atria, and pauses at the AV node in the right atrial floor. It then passes through the AV bundle into the interventricular septum, splits into the right and left bundle branches, and finally spreads through the ventricle walls in the Purkinje fibers. The order runs from the top of the heart down to the apex and then out through the ventricles.
notes: This sequence puts the bundle branches before the AV bundle. The branches are what the bundle divides into, so the AV bundle has to come first.
Correct. This is the full pathway from the SA node to the Purkinje fibers.
This sequence swaps the AV node and the AV bundle. The node must come first because it receives the signal from the atria and delays it before the bundle carries it into the septum.
This sequence starts at the AV node, but the SA node is the pacemaker and always fires first. It also places the bundle branches before the AV bundle that they branch from.
questions.answerText: SA node, AV node, AV bundle, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Moving from the right atrium toward the apex of the heart, in what order do you meet these structures: bundle branches, SA node, AV bundle, AV node?
options: SA node, AV node, AV bundle, bundle branches
SA node, AV bundle, AV node, bundle branches
AV bundle, SA node, AV node, bundle branches
AV node, SA node, AV bundle, bundle branches
questions.why: The SA node is highest, in the upper right atrial wall near the superior vena cava. The AV node is lower, in the floor of the right atrium near the interatrial septum. Below that, the AV bundle sits in the superior interventricular septum, and the bundle branches run down the septum toward the apex, so location and signal order match.
notes: Correct. This order runs from the top of the right atrium down the septum toward the apex.
This order places the AV bundle above the AV node. The AV node is still in the right atrium, while the AV bundle has already crossed into the interventricular septum.
This order starts with the AV bundle, which actually lies below both nodes in the septum. Students who confuse the AV bundle with the AV node tend to place it too high.
This order puts the AV node above the SA node. The SA node sits higher, near the opening of the superior vena cava, while the AV node is down in the atrial floor.
questions.answerText: SA node, AV node, AV bundle, bundle branches

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Which choice correctly matches the three normal ECG deflections to their conduction events, in the order they occur during one heartbeat?
options: QRS complex for atrial spread, P wave for ventricular spread, T wave for ventricular recovery
P wave for ventricular spread, QRS complex for atrial spread, T wave for atrial recovery
P wave for atrial spread, QRS complex for ventricular spread, T wave for ventricular recovery
T wave for atrial spread, P wave for ventricular spread, QRS complex for ventricular recovery
questions.why: Each heartbeat on an ECG shows three deflections in order. The small P wave shows the signal spreading across the atria, the tall QRS complex shows it spreading across the ventricles, and the T wave shows the ventricles electrically recovering. The order of the waves follows the order of the conduction pathway, from the atria down to the ventricles.
notes: This match swaps the P wave and the QRS complex. The P wave comes first because the atria receive the signal first, and the larger QRS complex reflects the bigger muscle mass of the ventricles.
This match reverses the atria and ventricles for the first two waves and assigns the T wave to the atria. Atrial recovery is hidden inside the QRS complex, so the T wave belongs to the ventricles.
Correct. P is atrial spread, QRS is ventricular spread, and T is ventricular recovery.
This match shifts every label by one position. The heartbeat starts with the P wave for the atria, not the T wave, which is always the last deflection.
questions.answerText: P wave for atrial spread, QRS complex for ventricular spread, T wave for ventricular recovery

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Which statement correctly places the AV node in the conduction pathway?
options: After the signal crosses the atria and before the AV bundle
After the SA node fires and before the signal crosses the atria
After the AV bundle and before the bundle branches
After the bundle branches and before the Purkinje fibers
questions.why: The SA node fires first and the signal spreads across both atria. It then reaches the AV node, which holds it briefly, and passes it on to the AV bundle in the interventricular septum. The AV node is therefore the link between the atrial part of the pathway and the septal part.
notes: Correct. The AV node receives the signal after it crosses the atria and passes it to the AV bundle.

The signal goes straight from the SA node across the atrial muscle, so the AV node cannot come before that spread. Students pick this when they think the two nodes connect directly, but the atria are between them.
Nothing sits between the AV bundle and the bundle branches, because the bundle simply divides into them. This placement would be right for a question about where the AV bundle splits.

The bundle branches pass the signal straight to the Purkinje fibers near the apex, with no node between them. This placement mixes up the AV node, which is in the right atrium, with the lower parts of the pathway.
questions.answerText: After the signal crosses the atria and before the AV bundle

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Which choice gives the order of the conduction structures within the interventricular septum and then the structure the signal reaches right after leaving the septum?
options: Bundle branches then AV bundle in the septum, then the Purkinje fibers in the ventricle walls
AV bundle then Purkinje fibers in the septum, then the bundle branches in the ventricle walls
AV bundle then bundle branches in the septum, then the Purkinje fibers in the ventricle walls
AV node then AV bundle in the septum, then the bundle branches in the ventricle walls
questions.why: Inside the interventricular septum, the AV bundle comes first and then divides into the right and left bundle branches, which run down toward the apex. From there the signal passes to the Purkinje fibers, which spread through the walls of both ventricles. This is the lower half of the conduction pathway, after the AV node.
notes: This order reverses the septal structures. The AV bundle is the single trunk that splits into the branches, so it must come before them.
This order swaps the bundle branches and the Purkinje fibers. The Purkinje fibers are the last structures, spread through the ventricle walls, while the bundle branches stay in the septum.
Correct. The AV bundle and then the bundle branches lie in the septum, and the Purkinje fibers come next.
The AV node is not in the interventricular septum; it sits in the floor of the right atrium. The bundle branches also run in the septum, not out in the ventricle walls.
questions.answerText: AV bundle then bundle branches in the septum, then the Purkinje fibers in the ventricle walls

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: What is the heart's built-in ability to generate its own rhythm called?
options: Autorhythmicity
Excitability
Conductivity
Contractility
questions.why: Autorhythmicity is the heart's ability to generate its own rhythm without a signal from the nervous system. The word breaks down as auto (self) plus rhythm, so it means self-rhythm. This property belongs to the conduction system, especially the SA node, which is why a transplanted heart with its nerves cut still beats.
notes: Correct. Autorhythmicity means the heart sets its own rhythm.

Excitability is the ability of a cell to respond to a stimulus. It would be the answer if the question asked about a cell's ability to react when a signal arrives, rather than to start the rhythm on its own.
Conductivity is the ability to pass a signal along from cell to cell. Choose it if the question asked about spreading the signal rather than generating it.
Contractility is the ability of muscle to shorten and produce force. Pick it if the question asked what lets the heart muscle squeeze once it receives a signal.
questions.answerText: Autorhythmicity

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: A textbook refers to the bundle of His. Which conduction structure does this name identify?
options: The atrioventricular node
The Purkinje fibers
The bundle branches
The atrioventricular bundle
questions.why: The bundle of His is another name for the atrioventricular (AV) bundle. It is the short strand of conducting cells that carries the signal from the AV node into the superior interventricular septum. It is the only electrical link between the atria and the ventricles, and just below it the pathway splits into the right and left bundle branches.
notes: The AV node is the structure just before the bundle of His, in the floor of the right atrium. Students mix them up because both names start with atrioventricular, but the node delays the signal while the bundle carries it into the septum.
The Purkinje fibers are the last part of the pathway, spread through the ventricle walls. Pick them if the question asked which fibers deliver the signal to the ventricular muscle.
The bundle branches are the right and left divisions that the bundle of His splits into. They would be correct if the question asked what comes right after the bundle of His.
Correct. The bundle of His and the AV bundle are the same structure.
questions.answerText: The atrioventricular bundle

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: What does an electrocardiogram (ECG) record?
options: The oxygen level in the blood
The heart's electrical activity
The volume pumped with each beat
The pressure inside the chambers
questions.why: An electrocardiogram, also called an ECG or EKG, is a tracing of the heart's electrical activity recorded through electrodes on the skin. Each deflection of a heartbeat lines up with an event in the conduction system, such as the signal spreading across the atria or the ventricles. A clinician reads it to judge whether the heart's rhythm and timing are normal.
notes: Blood oxygen is measured with a pulse oximeter on a fingertip or with a blood sample. It would be the answer if the question asked what a pulse oximeter checks.
Correct. An ECG records electrical activity through electrodes on the skin.

The volume pumped per beat is called the stroke volume, and it is estimated with imaging or other tests rather than read off an ECG. Students confuse the two because both describe the heartbeat, but the ECG shows only electrical events.
Chamber pressure is measured with a catheter placed inside the heart, not with skin electrodes. Pick it if the question asked what a cardiac catheter measures.
questions.answerText: The heart's electrical activity

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Which ECG deflection lines up with the signal spreading across the atria?
options: The flat line after the P wave
The T wave
The P wave
The QRS complex
questions.why: The P wave is the first small bump of each heartbeat. It lines up with the signal spreading across both atria right after the SA node fires, and the atria contract just after it. It is small because the atria have relatively little muscle compared with the ventricles.
notes: The flat line after the P wave mostly reflects the brief pause at the AV node, after the atria have already received the signal. Choose it if the question asked where the AV node delay appears.
The T wave is the last deflection and shows the ventricles electrically recovering. It would be correct if the question asked which deflection comes before the ventricles relax.
Correct. The P wave shows the signal crossing the atria.
The QRS complex is the tall spike that shows the signal spreading across the ventricles. Pick it if the question asked about the ventricles rather than the atria.
questions.answerText: The P wave

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: On an ECG, the QRS complex is much taller than the P wave. Why?
options: The ventricles contain much more muscle than the atria
The AV node strengthens the signal before passing it on
The SA node fires a second, stronger signal for the ventricles
The Purkinje fibers add an extra beat of their own
questions.why: The QRS complex shows the signal spreading across the ventricles, and the P wave shows it spreading across the atria. The ventricles have far thicker, more muscular walls than the atria because they pump blood out of the heart, so far more cells carry the signal at once. More muscle produces a larger electrical signal at the skin, which is why the QRS complex is taller.
notes: Correct. The larger muscle mass of the ventricles produces the larger deflection.
The AV node does not strengthen the signal; it delays it briefly so the atria can finish emptying. Students pick this when they confuse the node's timing role with boosting the signal.

The SA node fires once per heartbeat, and that single signal travels through the whole pathway. This choice comes from imagining separate signals for the atria and ventricles, which the conduction system does not use.
The Purkinje fibers spread the same signal through the ventricle walls rather than creating an extra beat. Pick them if the question asked which structures hand the signal to the ventricular muscle.
questions.answerText: The ventricles contain much more muscle than the atria

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: On an ECG, which conduction event does the T wave mark?
options: The ventricles electrically recovering
The signal spreading across the atria
The atria contracting
The signal pausing at the AV node
questions.why: The T wave is the last deflection of each heartbeat, after the QRS complex. It marks the ventricles electrically recovering, resetting so they can respond to the next signal. The ventricles relax right after the T wave.
notes: Correct. The T wave marks ventricular recovery.
The signal spreading across the atria is shown by the P wave, the first small bump. It would be correct if the question asked what the P wave shows.
The atria contract after the P wave, at the start of the heartbeat, not at the end. Pick this event if the question asked what follows the P wave.
The pause at the AV node appears as the flat line between the P wave and the QRS complex, not as a wave. Choose it if the question asked where the AV node delay shows on an ECG.
questions.answerText: The ventricles electrically recovering

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: What is an arrhythmia?
options: Any deviation from the normal heart rhythm
A blocked coronary artery
A leaking heart valve
Fluid collecting in the pericardial cavity
questions.why: An arrhythmia is any deviation from the normal heart rhythm. It is the umbrella term for the conduction disorders, including tachycardia, bradycardia, heart block, fibrillation and an ectopic pacemaker. The word itself means without rhythm, which points to a problem with the heart's electrical timing rather than its plumbing.
notes: Correct. Arrhythmia covers any abnormal heart rhythm.
A blocked coronary artery cuts off blood to part of the heart wall, which can cause a heart attack. Pick it if the question asked about a disease of the vessels that feed the heart muscle.
A leaking heart valve lets blood flow backward and is a valve problem, not a rhythm problem. It would be the answer if the question asked about valve disease or a heart murmur.
Fluid in the pericardial cavity is a problem of the sac around the heart. Choose it if the question asked about a buildup of fluid between the layers of the pericardium.
questions.answerText: Any deviation from the normal heart rhythm

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: What is tachycardia?
options: An abnormally fast resting heart rate
An abnormally slow resting heart rate
A signal delayed or stopped at the AV node
A site outside the SA node taking over the rhythm
questions.why: Tachycardia is an abnormally fast resting heart rate; tachy means fast. The concern is that when the heart beats too fast, the chambers may not have enough time to fill with blood between beats. It is one of the specific arrhythmias.
notes: Correct. Tachy means fast, so tachycardia is a fast resting heart rate.
An abnormally slow resting heart rate is bradycardia, the opposite of tachycardia. Pick it if the question asked what bradycardia means.
A signal delayed or stopped at the AV node is heart block. It would be the answer if the question asked about the atria and ventricles beating out of step.
A site outside the SA node taking over is an ectopic pacemaker. Choose it if the question asked about the beat starting from the wrong place.
questions.answerText: An abnormally fast resting heart rate

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: What is bradycardia?
options: Rapid, disorganized signals in the atria
An abnormally slow resting heart rate
Rapid, disorganized signals in the ventricles
An abnormally fast resting heart rate
questions.why: Bradycardia is an abnormally slow resting heart rate; brady means slow. The concern is that a heart beating too slowly may not send enough blood to the body. If the SA node is failing, an artificial pacemaker can take over its job.
notes: Rapid, disorganized signals in the atria describe atrial fibrillation, where the atria quiver. It would be the answer if the question asked about atrial fibrillation.
Correct. Brady means slow, so bradycardia is a slow resting heart rate.
Rapid, disorganized signals in the ventricles describe ventricular fibrillation, a life-threatening emergency. Choose it if the question asked about the ventricles quivering and failing to pump.
An abnormally fast resting heart rate is tachycardia. Pick it if the question asked what tachycardia means.
questions.answerText: An abnormally slow resting heart rate

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: After the SA node fires, the signal spreads across the atria. Which conduction structure does it reach next?
options: The Purkinje fibers
The bundle branches
The AV node
The AV bundle
questions.why: Once the signal has spread across both atria, it collects at the AV node in the floor of the right atrium. The AV node holds the signal briefly so the atria can finish emptying, then passes it on. The pathway continues from there to the AV bundle, the bundle branches, and the Purkinje fibers.
notes: The Purkinje fibers are the last stop, in the ventricle walls, several steps later. They would be correct if the question asked which structure follows the bundle branches.
The bundle branches run down the interventricular septum, two steps after the AV node. Choose them if the question asked what the AV bundle divides into.
Correct. The AV node is the next stop after the atria.
The AV bundle comes right after the AV node, in the superior interventricular septum. Pick it if the question asked where the signal goes after it leaves the AV node.
questions.answerText: The AV node

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Why does the signal pause briefly at the AV node?
options: To give the ventricles time to empty before the atria contract
To let the ventricles recover electrically before the next beat
To give the atria time to finish emptying into the ventricles
To let the atria and ventricles contract at the same moment
questions.why: The atria contract first and push their last portion of blood down into the ventricles. The brief hold at the AV node keeps the ventricles from being signaled until that filling is finished. Without the delay, the ventricles would contract before they were fully loaded with blood.
notes: This reverses the real order. The atria contract first and the ventricles second, so the delay protects ventricular filling, not ventricular emptying.
Ventricular recovery happens later in the beat and appears as the T wave. Pick it if the question asked what the T wave represents.
Correct. The delay lets the atria finish filling the ventricles before the ventricles contract.
The pause does the opposite, separating atrial and ventricular contraction in time. Students pick this when they assume the whole heart squeezes at once, but the chambers contract in sequence.
questions.answerText: To give the atria time to finish emptying into the ventricles

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: From the AV bundle, the signal travels down both sides of the interventricular septum. Which structures carry it?
options: The Purkinje fibers
The chordae tendineae
The bundle branches
The cardiac plexus
questions.why: The AV bundle splits into the right and left bundle branches at the top of the interventricular septum. They run down either side of the septum toward the apex, carrying the signal to both ventricles. At the apex they pass the signal to the Purkinje fibers.
notes: The Purkinje fibers come next, spreading through the ventricle walls rather than running down the septum. Pick them if the question asked which structures reach the contractile cells.

The chordae tendineae are tendon-like cords that tie the AV valve cusps to the papillary muscles. Students confuse them with conduction fibers because both are cord-like structures inside the ventricles, but the chordae keep the valves from flipping into the atria.
Correct. The right and left bundle branches carry the signal down the septum.

The cardiac plexus is a network of autonomic nerve fibers near the base of the heart, not part of the conduction pathway. It would be the answer if the question asked how sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves reach the nodes.
questions.answerText: The bundle branches

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Which conduction structure spreads the signal upward from the apex through the ventricle walls, so the ventricles contract from the apex upward?
options: The AV bundle
The Purkinje fibers
The AV node
The SA node
questions.why: The bundle branches carry the signal down the septum to the apex, and the Purkinje fibers then spread it upward through the walls of both ventricles. Because the muscle near the apex receives the signal first, the ventricles squeeze from the bottom up. This pushes blood toward the pulmonary trunk and aorta, which leave from the top of the ventricles.
notes: The AV bundle carries the signal into the top of the interventricular septum, well before it reaches the apex. Choose it if the question asked for the only electrical link between the atria and the ventricles.
Correct. The Purkinje fibers spread the signal up through the ventricle walls from the apex.
The AV node sits in the floor of the right atrium and briefly delays the signal. It would be correct if the question asked where the signal pauses.
The SA node starts the signal at the top of the right atrium and never reaches into the ventricle walls. Pick it if the question asked which structure fires first.
questions.answerText: The Purkinje fibers

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the role of the autonomic nerves that reach the heart?
options: They generate each heartbeat, and the SA node relays it
They start the heartbeat only during exercise
They adjust the rate that the SA node already sets
They supply the heart's blood vessels but not its nodes
questions.why: The heartbeat is generated by the conduction system itself, starting at the SA node, a property called autorhythmicity. Sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves reach the SA and AV nodes through the cardiac plexus and only speed up or slow down that existing rhythm. A transplanted heart, whose nerves have been cut, still beats for this reason.
notes: This reverses the roles. The SA node generates each beat on its own, and the nerves only change how fast it fires.

The heart beats on its own at rest and during exercise. During exercise, sympathetic nerves speed up the SA node, but they still are not starting the beats; students pick this when they confuse speeding up the beat with creating it.
Correct. The nerves modulate the rate but do not start the beat.
The autonomic fibers do reach the SA and AV nodes through the cardiac plexus. This choice comes from thinking the heart's own rhythm means it has no nerve supply to its conduction tissue at all.
questions.answerText: They adjust the rate that the SA node already sets

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Which conduction structure sits in the superior part of the interventricular septum?
options: The SA node
The Purkinje fibers
The AV bundle
The AV node
questions.why: The AV bundle, or bundle of His, leaves the AV node and enters the superior part of the interventricular septum, the wall between the ventricles. It is the only electrical bridge across the fibrous skeleton from the atria to the ventricles. A little lower in the septum it divides into the right and left bundle branches.
notes: The SA node sits high in the right atrial wall near the opening of the superior vena cava. Pick it if the question asked where the pacemaker is.

The Purkinje fibers spread through the walls of both ventricles rather than sitting at the top of the septum. They would be correct if the question asked which structures reach the ventricular muscle.
Correct. The AV bundle lies in the upper interventricular septum.

The AV node is just above the AV bundle, but it is still in the floor of the right atrium near the interatrial septum. Students mix up the two because their names are nearly the same, so remember the node is atrial and the bundle is septal.
questions.answerText: The AV bundle

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares atrial fibrillation and ventricular fibrillation?
options: Both are slow, organized rhythms that differ only in which chamber sets the pace
In atrial fibrillation the ventricles keep pumping, while ventricular fibrillation stops blood flow
In ventricular fibrillation the heart keeps pumping, while atrial fibrillation stops blood flow
Both stop the heart from moving blood and are equally life-threatening
questions.why: Both disorders are rapid, disorganized signaling that makes chambers quiver instead of contracting, and the name tells you which chambers are affected. In atrial fibrillation only the atria quiver, so the ventricles still pump and the condition is common and treatable. In ventricular fibrillation the main pumping chambers quiver and move no blood, so it is a life-threatening emergency treated with a defibrillator.
notes: Fibrillation is fast and chaotic, not slow and organized. A slow, organized rhythm would describe bradycardia, and a different site setting the pace would describe an ectopic pacemaker.
Correct. Quivering atria still allow ventricular pumping, but quivering ventricles do not.
This reverses the two disorders. The ventricles are the main pumps, so losing them in ventricular fibrillation is what stops blood flow, while quivering atria still let blood reach the ventricles.

Only ventricular fibrillation stops blood flow. Students pick this because both share the word fibrillation, but the atria contribute only the final top-up of ventricular filling, so the heart keeps pumping in atrial fibrillation.
questions.answerText: In atrial fibrillation the ventricles keep pumping, while ventricular fibrillation stops blood flow

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: What is an ectopic pacemaker?
options: A blocked coronary artery
A small implanted electronic device
The heart's normal pacemaker in the right atrium
A site outside the SA node that takes over the rhythm
questions.why: Ectopic means out of place. An ectopic pacemaker is a site outside the SA node that starts firing and takes over the heart's rhythm. When this happens, the normal pacing order of the heart is lost because the beat no longer starts at the SA node.
notes: A blocked coronary artery reduces blood supply to the heart wall and is a vessel problem, not a rhythm disorder. Choose it if the question asked about the cause of a heart attack.
A small implanted device that delivers timed signals is an artificial pacemaker. Pick it if the question asked what can replace a failing SA node or carry the signal past a block.
The heart's normal pacemaker in the right atrium is the SA node itself. It would be the answer if the question asked which structure normally sets the rhythm.
Correct. An ectopic pacemaker is a site outside the SA node setting the rhythm.
questions.answerText: A site outside the SA node that takes over the rhythm

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: A patient's SA node is failing. An implanted device delivers a timed electrical signal to restore an ordered beat. What is this device?
options: A stent
An artificial pacemaker
A replacement heart valve
A defibrillator
questions.why: An artificial pacemaker is a small implanted device that delivers a timed electrical signal to the heart. It takes over the job of a failing SA node, or carries the signal past a block at the AV node, so the heart keeps an ordered beat. It does the same work as the natural pacemaker, just electronically.
notes: A stent is a small mesh tube placed inside a narrowed artery, such as a coronary artery, to hold it open. It would be the answer if the question described a blocked vessel rather than a rhythm problem.
Correct. An artificial pacemaker supplies the timed signal a failing SA node cannot.
A replacement heart valve fixes a valve that leaks or will not open fully. Choose it if the question described a valve problem, not a failing pacemaker.

A defibrillator delivers a single strong shock to stop chaotic signals, as in ventricular fibrillation. Pick it if the question described resetting a quivering heart rather than pacing a slow or failing one.
questions.answerText: An artificial pacemaker

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: In ventricular fibrillation the ventricles only quiver and move no blood. A shock is used to stop all the chaotic signals at once. What is this treatment?
options: Defibrillation
Coronary bypass surgery
Valve repair
Pacemaker implantation
questions.why: Defibrillation delivers a shock that stops all the chaotic signals in the ventricles at once. With the disorganized activity cleared, the SA node has a chance to restart the heart in its normal rhythm. The name means removing fibrillation, which is the quivering it treats.
notes: Correct. Defibrillation uses a shock to stop the chaotic signals so the SA node can take over again.
Coronary bypass surgery reroutes blood around a blocked coronary artery using a graft vessel. It would be the answer if the question described restoring blood supply to the heart wall.
Valve repair fixes a heart valve that leaks or is narrowed. Choose it if the question described a valve problem rather than an electrical one.

Pacemaker implantation places a device that delivers timed signals over the long term for a failing SA node or a heart block. Pick it if the question described a slow or blocked rhythm rather than chaotic quivering.
questions.answerText: Defibrillation

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Following one heartbeat's signal in order, it has just left the AV node. Which structure carries it next?
options: The Purkinje fibers
The bundle branches
The AV bundle
The SA node
questions.why: After its brief pause at the AV node, the signal enters the AV bundle, which carries it across the fibrous skeleton into the superior interventricular septum. From there it continues to the bundle branches and then the Purkinje fibers. The AV bundle is the only route from the atria to the ventricles.
notes: The Purkinje fibers are the last structures in the pathway, two steps after the AV bundle. They would be correct if the question asked what follows the bundle branches.
The bundle branches come after the AV bundle, not directly after the AV node. Choose them if the question asked what the AV bundle divides into.
Correct. The AV bundle is the next stop after the AV node.
The SA node is where the signal started, before it crossed the atria and reached the AV node. Pick it if the question asked which structure fires first.
questions.answerText: The AV bundle

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: An ECG shows a normal P wave that is not followed by a QRS complex, because the signal is delayed or stopped at the AV node. What disorder does this suggest?
options: Tachycardia
Ectopic pacemaker
Atrial fibrillation
Heart block
questions.why: A normal P wave means the SA node fired and the signal crossed the atria as usual. A missing QRS complex means the signal never reached the ventricles. When the signal is delayed or stopped at the AV node, the disorder is heart block, and the atria and ventricles can beat out of step.
notes: Tachycardia is a fast resting heart rate, and each P wave would still be followed by a QRS complex. Pick it if the ECG showed normal beats occurring too quickly.

An ectopic pacemaker means a site outside the SA node starts the beat, so the problem is where the signal begins, not a stop at the AV node. It would be the answer if the beat were described as starting in the wrong place.
Atrial fibrillation replaces the normal P waves with chaotic atrial activity, so there would be no normal P wave at all. Choose it if the question described the atria quivering.
Correct. A normal atrial signal that fails to reach the ventricles points to heart block at the AV node.
questions.answerText: Heart block

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: A transplanted heart has had its nerves cut, yet it keeps beating. What explains this?
options: The autorhythmicity of the conduction system
The contractility of the ventricular muscle
Input from the vagus nerve
Input from the sympathetic nerves
questions.why: Autorhythmicity is the heart's ability to generate its own rhythm, and it belongs to the conduction system, starting with the SA node. Cutting the nerves during a transplant removes only the outside signals that speed up or slow down the rate. The SA node keeps firing on its own, so the heart keeps beating.
notes: Correct. The conduction system generates the beat on its own, with no nerve input needed.
Contractility is the muscle's ability to squeeze once a signal arrives, but it does not create the signal. Pick it if the question asked what lets the ventricles produce force when stimulated.
The vagus nerve carries parasympathetic fibers that slow the heart, and it has also been cut in a transplant. Choose it if the question asked which nerve slows the heart rate.
The sympathetic nerves only speed up the heart, and in a transplanted heart they have been cut. They would be the answer if the question asked which nerves raise the heart rate in an intact heart.
questions.answerText: The autorhythmicity of the conduction system

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: If the AV node passed the signal on with no delay at all, what would most likely go wrong?
options: The SA node would stop firing
The Purkinje fibers would send the signal back to the atria
The atria would contract after the ventricles
The ventricles would contract before they finished filling
questions.why: Normally the AV node holds the signal for a fraction of a second while the atria finish squeezing their blood into the ventricles. Without that delay, the ventricles would be signaled almost at the same moment as the atria. They would start contracting before they were fully loaded, so less blood would be pumped out with each beat.
notes: The SA node fires on its own, upstream of the AV node, so a change at the AV node would not stop it. This choice confuses the delaying node with the pacemaker.

The conduction pathway carries the signal one way, from the atria down to the ventricles, and the fibrous skeleton blocks any return route. Students pick this when they imagine the signal looping back through the heart.
The signal still reaches the atria first, so the atria would not contract after the ventricles. Without the delay the two would contract nearly together, which is the real problem.
Correct. The delay exists to let the atria finish filling the ventricles first.
questions.answerText: The ventricles would contract before they finished filling

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: The Purkinje fibers make the ventricles contract from the apex upward. Why does starting the squeeze at the bottom help the heart pump?
options: It drives blood up toward the pulmonary trunk and aorta at the top
It pushes blood back up into the atria through the AV valves
It sends the signal back to the SA node to trigger the next beat
It lets the ventricles keep filling while they contract
questions.why: The exits from the ventricles, the pulmonary trunk and the aorta, both leave from the top of the heart near the base. Squeezing from the apex upward works like rolling up a tube of toothpaste from the closed end, pushing blood toward those openings. If the top contracted first, blood would be trapped toward the apex.
notes: Correct. Squeezing from the bottom up pushes blood toward the great arteries at the top.

The AV valves close when the ventricles contract, which prevents blood from flowing back into the atria. Pick the AV valves if the question asked what keeps blood from moving backward during ventricular contraction.
The signal does not travel back to the SA node; the SA node fires on its own for each new beat. Students pick this when they imagine the conduction pathway as a loop.
The ventricles fill while they are relaxed, not while they contract. This choice mixes up the filling phase with the pumping phase of the heartbeat.
questions.answerText: It drives blood up toward the pulmonary trunk and aorta at the top

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Cardiac muscle cells pass the signal directly from one cell to the next so a chamber contracts as one unit. Which junctions within the intercalated discs make this possible?
options: Gap junctions
Sarcoplasmic reticulum
T tubules
Desmosomes
questions.why: Intercalated discs are the specialized junctions where neighboring cardiac muscle cells meet end to end. Within them, gap junctions are small channels that let the signal pass directly from one cell to the next. This electrical coupling lets the whole chamber contract together in one coordinated squeeze.
notes: Correct. Gap junctions let the signal pass directly from cell to cell.
The sarcoplasmic reticulum is the network inside a muscle cell that stores and releases calcium. Choose it if the question asked which organelle stores calcium in a muscle cell.

T tubules are inward folds of the cell membrane that carry the signal deep into a single muscle cell. They would be the answer if the question asked how the signal reaches the interior of one fiber, not how it crosses between cells.

Desmosomes are also found in the intercalated discs, but they are anchoring junctions that keep the cells from pulling apart as they contract. Pick them if the question asked what holds neighboring cardiac cells together mechanically.
questions.answerText: Gap junctions

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: The fibrous skeleton between the atria and ventricles does not conduct signals, leaving the AV node and AV bundle as the only route through. What does this arrangement accomplish?
options: It makes all four chambers contract at the same moment
Every signal passes the AV node delay, so the atria contract first
It lets the signal reach the ventricles at many points at once
It keeps the signal from ever reaching the ventricular muscle
questions.why: The fibrous skeleton is a framework of dense connective tissue that electrically insulates the atria from the ventricles. Because the signal cannot cross anywhere else, it must pass through the AV node, where it is delayed, and then the AV bundle. This single gateway guarantees the atria contract first and the ventricles second, in the right order.
notes: The arrangement does the opposite, separating atrial and ventricular contraction in time. Students pick this when they assume the whole heart squeezes at once.
Correct. The single gateway forces the signal through the AV node delay, keeping the chambers in order.
Without the fibrous skeleton the signal might leak across at many points, but the insulation prevents exactly that. This choice describes what would happen if the barrier were missing.
The signal does reach the ventricles, through the AV bundle, bundle branches and Purkinje fibers. A complete stop at the AV node would describe severe heart block, not the normal arrangement.
questions.answerText: Every signal passes the AV node delay, so the atria contract first

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: During exercise, a person's heart rate climbs from 70 to 140 beats per minute. Which statement best explains the change?
options: The AV node took over as the pacemaker
The nervous system began generating each heartbeat directly
Sympathetic nerves made the SA node fire faster
The vagus nerve made the SA node fire faster
questions.why: The SA node keeps setting the rhythm during exercise, but sympathetic nerves reaching it through the cardiac plexus speed up its firing. The nerves adjust the rate to match the body's needs; they do not create the beats. This split lets the heart keep a steady beat on its own while the nervous system fine-tunes the pace.
notes: The AV node takes over only as a slower backup if the SA node fails, so it would lower the rate, not double it. Choose it if the question described a failing SA node.
The nervous system never generates the heartbeat; the SA node does, through autorhythmicity. Students pick this when they confuse adjusting the rate with creating the beat.
Correct. Sympathetic input speeds up the SA node.
The vagus nerve carries parasympathetic fibers that slow the heart, not speed it up. Pick it if the question asked what brings the heart rate back down at rest.
questions.answerText: Sympathetic nerves made the SA node fire faster

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: If the SA node stops firing, which structure is next in line to take over as the heart's pacemaker?
options: The vagus nerve
The AV node
The medulla oblongata
The cardiac plexus
questions.why: Cells of the conduction system other than the SA node can also fire on their own, only more slowly. The AV node is the next fastest, so if the SA node fails it takes over as a backup pacemaker at a slower rate, about 40 to 60 beats a minute. This keeps the heart beating, though more slowly, until the problem is treated.
notes: The vagus nerve carries parasympathetic fibers that slow the heart and cannot start beats. Choose it if the question asked which nerve slows the heart rate.
Correct. The AV node is the backup pacemaker when the SA node fails.

The medulla oblongata holds the cardiac centers that adjust the rate through autonomic nerves, but it cannot generate the heartbeat. Pick it if the question asked where the brain's cardiac centers are.

The cardiac plexus is a network of autonomic nerve fibers that carries signals to the nodes; it does not generate a rhythm. It would be the answer if the question asked how nerves reach the SA and AV nodes.
questions.answerText: The AV node

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: An ECG uses electrodes on the skin to record the heartbeat. What are the electrodes actually detecting?
options: The signals traveling in the vagus nerve
The pressure of each beat pushing on the chest wall
The sound of the heart valves closing
The heart's electrical currents spreading to the skin
questions.why: Each heartbeat produces electrical currents as the signal spreads through the conduction system and heart muscle. Body tissues and fluids conduct electricity, so these currents spread outward and can be picked up by electrodes on the skin. The ECG tracing is a record of those currents over each heartbeat.
notes: Nerve signals in the vagus are far too small to show up on an ECG, and the vagus only adjusts the rate. The ECG reflects the much larger electrical activity of the heart muscle itself.

The force of each beat is felt as the pulse in an artery or measured as blood pressure, not detected by ECG electrodes. This choice mixes up the heart's mechanical action with its electrical activity.
The sounds of the valves closing are heard with a stethoscope, not recorded by ECG electrodes. Pick this if the question asked what a clinician listens to when checking heart sounds.
Correct. The electrodes pick up electrical currents from the heart.
questions.answerText: The heart's electrical currents spreading to the skin

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: A blockage in which coronary artery is most likely to cause a rhythm problem by cutting off blood to the SA node, in most people?
options: The coronary sinus
The left marginal artery
The anterior interventricular artery
The right coronary artery
questions.why: In most people, the SA node receives its blood supply from the right coronary artery, which also usually supplies the AV node. If the right coronary artery is blocked, the SA node can be starved of oxygen along with the heart wall it supplies. That is why a right coronary artery occlusion can cause a rhythm problem as well as damage to the heart muscle.
notes: The coronary sinus is a large vein that drains blood away from the heart wall into the right atrium, so it delivers no blood to the SA node. Choose it if the question asked where the cardiac veins empty.

The left marginal artery is a branch along the left border of the heart, supplying the wall of the left ventricle. It would be the answer if the question asked which branch runs along the left margin.

The anterior interventricular artery, also called the LAD, runs down the front of the heart and supplies the anterior septum and much of the left ventricle. Pick it if the question asked which artery runs in the anterior interventricular sulcus.
Correct. The right coronary artery usually supplies the SA node.
questions.answerText: The right coronary artery

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: What does the moderator band carry?
options: Arterial blood to the interventricular septum
Conduction fibers to the anterior papillary muscle
Chordae tendineae of the tricuspid valve
Venous blood from the heart wall
questions.why: The moderator band carries part of the heart's conduction system, from the right bundle branch, across the right ventricle to the anterior papillary muscle. This shortcut lets the papillary muscle contract at the right time to hold the tricuspid valve shut as the ventricle contracts. It is a muscular band, not a vessel or a cord.
notes: Arterial blood to the septum comes from the interventricular branches of the coronary arteries. Pick the anterior interventricular artery for the front of the septum.
Correct. The moderator band carries conduction fibers to the anterior papillary muscle.
The chordae tendineae run from the papillary muscles to the valve cusps on their own. The moderator band attaches to the base of a papillary muscle, not to the cords.
Venous blood from the heart wall is carried by the cardiac veins and coronary sinus. Pick the coronary sinus for that drainage.
questions.answerText: Conduction fibers to the anterior papillary muscle

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: What is a cardiomyocyte?
options: A fibroblast of the pericardium
A cardiac muscle cell
A smooth muscle cell
A skeletal muscle fiber
questions.why: A cardiomyocyte is a cardiac muscle cell. The name breaks down as cardio (heart), myo (muscle), and cyte (cell). Cardiomyocytes are short, branching cells, usually with a single central nucleus, and they join end to end at intercalated discs to build the myocardium.
notes: A fibroblast is a connective tissue cell that makes fibers, and fibroblasts are found in the fibrous pericardium. It fits a question about the cells that build connective tissue, but it is not a muscle cell and does not contract.
Correct. Cardiomyocyte literally means heart muscle cell.

A smooth muscle cell is a spindle-shaped, nonstriated cell found in the walls of blood vessels and hollow organs. Pick it if the question asked about the cells of the tunica media, not the heart wall.

A skeletal muscle fiber is a long, cylindrical cell with many nuclei, found in a skeletal muscle such as the biceps brachii. It would be the answer for the cell of voluntary muscle, not the cell of the heart wall.
questions.answerText: A cardiac muscle cell

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: What specialized junctions connect neighboring cardiomyocytes end to end?
options: Tight junctions
Neuromuscular junctions
Intercalated discs
Z discs
questions.why: Intercalated discs are the specialized junctions where neighboring cardiomyocytes meet end to end. On a slide they show up as dark lines crossing the fibers, and they are the feature that identifies cardiac muscle. Each disc holds desmosomes, which anchor the cells together, and gap junctions, which let the contraction signal pass from cell to cell.
notes: Tight junctions seal neighboring epithelial cells so substances cannot leak between them, as in the lining of the intestine. Choose them for a question about a leakproof epithelial seal, not about cardiac muscle.

A neuromuscular junction is where a motor neuron meets a skeletal muscle fiber to trigger contraction. It would be the answer for the nerve-to-muscle connection in skeletal muscle, not a cell-to-cell link between heart cells.
Correct. Intercalated discs join cardiomyocytes end to end.
Z discs are the boundaries of each sarcomere inside a single muscle cell. They would be the answer for where thin filaments anchor within a sarcomere, not for the junctions between two cells.
questions.answerText: Intercalated discs

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Within the intercalated discs, which junctions keep cardiomyocytes from pulling apart during contraction?
options: Tight junctions
Desmosomes
Hemidesmosomes
Gap junctions
questions.why: Desmosomes are anchoring junctions that rivet neighboring cells together, much like spot welds. In cardiac muscle they sit in the intercalated discs and hold the cells together as each beat pulls hard on them. Without them, the force of contraction would tear the cells apart.
notes: Tight junctions seal epithelial cells to block leaks between them. They are not the anchoring junction of the intercalated disc, and they fit a question about a leakproof lining such as the intestinal epithelium.
Correct. Desmosomes anchor cardiomyocytes to one another so they do not separate.
Hemidesmosomes anchor an epithelial cell to the basement membrane beneath it, not to another cell. They would be the answer for how the epidermis stays attached to the layer below it.

Gap junctions are the other junction in the intercalated disc. They are channels that let the electrical signal pass directly between cells, so pick them for a question about spreading the signal, not holding cells together.
questions.answerText: Desmosomes

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Which junctions in the intercalated discs let the electrical signal pass directly from one cardiomyocyte to the next?
options: Gap junctions
Desmosomes
Hemidesmosomes
Tight junctions
questions.why: Gap junctions are tiny protein channels that connect the cytoplasm of neighboring cells. In the intercalated discs they let the electrical signal for contraction flow straight from one cardiomyocyte to the next, so the signal spreads quickly through the heart wall. This is why a whole chamber contracts as one coordinated unit.
notes: Correct. Gap junctions pass the signal directly from cell to cell.
Desmosomes are the anchoring junctions in the intercalated disc that hold cells together mechanically. Choose them for a question about cells pulling apart, not about passing the signal.
Hemidesmosomes attach an epithelial cell to its basement membrane. They would fit a question about anchoring the epidermis to the tissue below, not about communication between heart cells.
Tight junctions seal the spaces between epithelial cells to stop leaks. They are the answer for a leakproof lining, and they do not carry electrical signals between heart cells.
questions.answerText: Gap junctions

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: How do gap junctions help the heart contract?
options: They insulate the atria from the ventricles
They spread the electrical signal rapidly from cell to cell
They store calcium to power each contraction
They anchor cells so contraction does not tear them apart
questions.why: Gap junctions are channels that connect the insides of neighboring cardiomyocytes. The electrical signal flows straight through them, so it spreads quickly across the whole chamber and the cells contract nearly together. This rapid spread is what turns millions of separate cells into one coordinated pump.
notes: Insulating the atria from the ventricles is the job of the fibrous skeleton, the rings of dense connective tissue around the valves. Choose that idea for why the AV bundle is the only electrical bridge between the upper and lower chambers.
Correct. Gap junctions let the signal pass quickly between cells so they contract together.
Calcium is stored in the sarcoplasmic reticulum inside each muscle cell, not in gap junctions. This choice mixes up a junction between cells with a storage organelle within the cell.
Anchoring cells against the pull of contraction is the job of desmosomes, the other junction in the intercalated disc. This would be right if the question asked why the cells do not separate.
questions.answerText: They spread the electrical signal rapidly from cell to cell

questions.topic: Cardiac muscle and the conduction system
questions.q: Why do cardiomyocytes need desmosomes?
options: To set the pace of the heartbeat
