The popliteal artery is above the anterior tibial artery, behind the knee. It gives rise to the anterior tibial rather than continuing from it.
questions.answerText: Dorsalis pedis artery

questions.topic: Nerves and vessels of the lower limb
questions.q: Which artery branches from the posterior tibial artery and runs down the leg close to the fibula?
options: Fibular artery
Dorsalis pedis artery
Anterior tibial artery
Deep femoral artery
questions.why: Shortly below its origin, the posterior tibial artery gives off the fibular artery, also called the peroneal artery. It runs down the back of the leg along the fibula, supplying nearby muscles of the posterior and lateral compartments. Its name tells you which bone it follows.
notes: Correct. The fibular artery branches from the posterior tibial artery and follows the fibula.
The dorsalis pedis artery is the continuation of the anterior tibial artery on the top of the foot. Pick it for the pulse on the dorsum.
The anterior tibial artery branches from the popliteal artery, not the posterior tibial, and runs in the front of the leg.
The deep femoral artery branches from the femoral artery in the thigh. It supplies thigh muscles, far above the fibula.
questions.answerText: Fibular artery

questions.topic: Nerves and vessels of the lower limb
questions.q: Which sequence correctly traces blood from the external iliac artery to the top of the foot?
options: External iliac, femoral, popliteal, posterior tibial, dorsalis pedis
Internal iliac, femoral, popliteal, anterior tibial, dorsalis pedis
External iliac, femoral, popliteal, anterior tibial, dorsalis pedis
External iliac, popliteal, femoral, anterior tibial, dorsalis pedis
questions.why: The main arterial pathway of the lower limb is one continuous vessel that changes names as it enters new regions. The external iliac becomes the femoral at the inguinal ligament, the femoral becomes the popliteal at the adductor hiatus, and the popliteal divides into the anterior and posterior tibial arteries. The anterior tibial continues onto the top of the foot as the dorsalis pedis.
notes: The posterior tibial artery goes to the sole, not the top of the foot. Pick this route if the question ended at the medial and lateral plantar arteries.
The internal iliac artery supplies the pelvic organs and the buttock. The femoral artery continues from the external iliac, not the internal iliac.
Correct. This is the arterial pathway to the dorsum of the foot.
The femoral artery must come before the popliteal. The femoral is in the thigh and the popliteal is behind the knee, so this order skips backward.
questions.answerText: External iliac, femoral, popliteal, anterior tibial, dorsalis pedis

questions.topic: Nerves and vessels of the lower limb
questions.q: Which superficial vein begins on the medial side of the foot, passes in front of the medial malleolus, and runs up the medial leg and thigh?
options: Great saphenous vein
Popliteal vein
Small saphenous vein
Femoral vein
questions.why: The great saphenous vein is the longest vein in the body. It starts from the medial end of the venous arch on the top of the foot, passes just in front of the medial malleolus, and climbs the medial side of the leg and thigh. Near the groin it drains into the femoral vein.
notes: Correct. The great saphenous vein runs up the medial side of the limb.
The popliteal vein is a deep vein behind the knee. Pick it for the vessel that receives the small saphenous vein.
The small saphenous vein starts on the lateral side of the foot, passes behind the lateral malleolus, and runs up the back of the calf. It is the lateral counterpart of the correct answer.
The femoral vein is a deep vein that runs with the femoral artery in the thigh. It receives the great saphenous vein rather than running on the surface.
questions.answerText: Great saphenous vein

questions.topic: Nerves and vessels of the lower limb
questions.q: The small saphenous vein drains into which vein?
options: Great saphenous vein
Femoral vein
External iliac vein
Popliteal vein
questions.why: The small saphenous vein starts on the lateral side of the foot, passes behind the lateral malleolus, and runs up the middle of the back of the calf. At the popliteal fossa it pierces the deep fascia and empties into the popliteal vein behind the knee.
notes: The great saphenous vein runs on the medial side of the limb. Although small connections link the two saphenous veins, the small saphenous vein ends in a deep vein behind the knee.
The femoral vein receives the great saphenous vein near the groin. Pick it for the drainage point of the longer, medial saphenous vein.
The external iliac vein is the continuation of the femoral vein above the inguinal ligament. It is too far up to receive a calf vein directly.
Correct. The small saphenous vein drains into the popliteal vein.
questions.answerText: Popliteal vein

questions.topic: Nerves and vessels of the lower limb
questions.q: A surgeon needs a long length of vein to bypass blocked coronary arteries and harvests one from the medial side of the patient's leg and thigh. Which vein is most often used?
options: Femoral vein
Small saphenous vein
Great saphenous vein
Popliteal vein
questions.why: The great saphenous vein is long, runs near the surface along the medial leg and thigh, and is a superficial vein whose job can be taken over by the deep veins. That combination makes it the standard vein to remove and use as a graft in coronary artery bypass surgery. Its location on the medial side matches the description.
notes: The femoral vein is a deep vein that carries most of the blood back from the limb. Removing it would seriously impair drainage, so it is not harvested.
The small saphenous vein is also superficial but is shorter and runs up the back of the calf, not along the medial thigh.
Correct. The great saphenous vein is the usual graft for coronary bypass.
The popliteal vein is a deep vein behind the knee. It is short and essential for drainage, so it would not be taken for a graft.
questions.answerText: Great saphenous vein

questions.topic: Nerves and vessels of the lower limb
questions.q: The deep veins of the lower limb follow the arteries. After passing under the inguinal ligament, the femoral vein continues as which vein?
options: Great saphenous vein
Internal iliac vein
Inferior vena cava
External iliac vein
questions.why: The deep veins of the limb run beside the arteries of the same name. The femoral vein lies medial to the femoral artery in the femoral triangle, and when it passes under the inguinal ligament into the pelvis it becomes the external iliac vein, just as the external iliac artery became the femoral artery going the other way.
notes: The great saphenous vein is a superficial vein that drains into the femoral vein. It comes before the femoral vein in the pathway, not after it.
The internal iliac vein drains the pelvic organs and buttock. It joins the external iliac vein to form the common iliac vein but is not the continuation of the femoral vein.
The inferior vena cava forms where the two common iliac veins join, higher in the abdomen. Blood from the femoral vein reaches it only after passing through the external and common iliac veins.
Correct. The femoral vein becomes the external iliac vein at the inguinal ligament.
questions.answerText: External iliac vein

questions.topic: Nerves and vessels of the lower limb
questions.q: A clot forms in a patient's popliteal vein and breaks loose. Traveling toward the heart, which vein does it enter next?
options: External iliac vein
Femoral vein
Small saphenous vein
Great saphenous vein
questions.why: Blood in the deep veins of the lower limb flows upward in the reverse order of the arteries: popliteal vein, femoral vein, external iliac vein, common iliac vein, inferior vena cava, and then the right atrium. A loose clot follows the same path. From the popliteal vein, the next vessel is the femoral vein, which it enters through the adductor hiatus.
notes: The external iliac vein comes after the femoral vein, above the inguinal ligament. The clot would reach it one step later.
Correct. The popliteal vein continues upward as the femoral vein.
The small saphenous vein drains into the popliteal vein, so blood flows from it into the popliteal vein, not the other way. It is one step before the popliteal vein, not after.
The great saphenous vein is a superficial vein that drains into the femoral vein. Blood does not flow from the deep popliteal vein into it.
questions.answerText: Femoral vein

questions.topic: Nerves and vessels of the lower limb
questions.q: A cardiologist inserts a catheter into the right femoral artery in the groin and advances it toward the heart. Which artery does the catheter enter first after leaving the femoral artery?
options: Abdominal aorta
Common iliac artery
External iliac artery
Internal iliac artery
questions.why: Moving toward the heart means traveling backward along the arterial pathway. The femoral artery is the continuation of the external iliac artery below the inguinal ligament, so the catheter enters the external iliac artery first. From there it passes into the common iliac artery and then the abdominal aorta.
notes: The abdominal aorta is reached third, after the external and common iliac arteries. Pick it as the vessel the catheter enters once it leaves the common iliac.
The common iliac artery is reached second, after the external iliac. It is one step too far along.
Correct. The catheter enters the external iliac artery first.
The internal iliac artery is a separate branch of the common iliac that dives into the pelvis. The catheter would not enter it while traveling from the femoral artery toward the heart.
questions.answerText: External iliac artery

questions.topic: Nerves and vessels of the lower limb
questions.q: A patient with poor circulation has a strong popliteal pulse, but no pulse can be felt on the top of the foot. Along which artery is a blockage most likely?
options: Femoral artery
External iliac artery
Anterior tibial artery
Posterior tibial artery
questions.why: The pulse on the top of the foot is the dorsalis pedis, which continues from the anterior tibial artery. A strong popliteal pulse shows that blood is getting past the knee normally. So the narrowing must lie below the popliteal artery along the route to the dorsum of the foot, which is the anterior tibial artery.
notes: A blockage in the femoral artery would weaken the popliteal pulse as well, because the femoral artery feeds the popliteal. The strong popliteal pulse rules it out.
The external iliac artery lies above the femoral artery. Blockage there would weaken every pulse below it, including the popliteal.
Correct. A blockage in the anterior tibial artery fits a strong popliteal pulse and a missing dorsalis pedis pulse.
The posterior tibial artery supplies the sole and is felt behind the medial malleolus. A blockage there would remove that pulse, not the one on top of the foot.
questions.answerText: Anterior tibial artery

questions.topic: Nerves and vessels of the lower limb
questions.q: A patient has twisted, bulging superficial veins running along the inner side of the leg and thigh. Which vein is most likely affected?
options: Small saphenous vein
Great saphenous vein
Femoral vein
Anterior tibial vein
questions.why: Varicose veins are superficial veins that have become stretched and twisted, often because their valves fail and blood pools. The great saphenous vein is the large superficial vein that runs along the medial side of the leg and thigh, so bulging veins in that position point to it and its tributaries.
notes: The small saphenous vein is superficial too, but it runs up the back of the calf and ends behind the knee. Pick it for varicose veins on the back of the calf.
Correct. Bulging superficial veins on the inner leg and thigh involve the great saphenous vein.
The femoral vein is a deep vein lying beside the femoral artery. Deep veins are surrounded by muscle and do not form visible bulges under the skin.
The anterior tibial vein is a deep vein running with the anterior tibial artery between the muscles of the front of the leg. It cannot be seen on the surface.
questions.answerText: Great saphenous vein

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the two vessels that bring blood into the liver?
options: The hepatic portal vein brings oxygen-rich blood from the aorta, and the hepatic artery brings nutrient-rich blood from the intestines
The hepatic veins bring blood in from the intestines, and the hepatic portal vein carries blood out to the heart
The hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein both carry blood out of the liver toward the inferior vena cava
The hepatic artery brings oxygen-rich blood, and the hepatic portal vein brings nutrient-rich blood from the digestive organs
questions.why: The liver has an unusual double blood supply. The hepatic artery, which traces back to the celiac trunk, brings oxygen-rich blood for the liver tissue itself. The hepatic portal vein brings blood that has already passed through the capillaries of the stomach, intestines, spleen, and pancreas, so it is rich in absorbed nutrients but low in oxygen. Both empty into the sinusoids, and the blood then leaves through the hepatic veins.
notes: This swaps the two vessels. Arteries carry oxygen-rich blood from the aorta, so the hepatic artery is the oxygen supply, while the portal vein carries nutrient-rich blood drained from the digestive organs.

This confuses the hepatic veins with the hepatic portal vein. The portal vein brings intestinal blood in, and the hepatic veins carry blood out of the liver to the inferior vena cava and on to the heart.
Both of these vessels bring blood into the liver. The vessels that carry blood out toward the inferior vena cava are the hepatic veins, so pick those for a question about drainage from the liver.
Correct. The hepatic artery carries oxygen-rich blood from the aorta, while the portal vein carries nutrient-rich blood drained from the digestive organs.
questions.answerText: The hepatic artery brings oxygen-rich blood, and the hepatic portal vein brings nutrient-rich blood from the digestive organs

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Which vessel delivers nutrient-rich blood from the stomach, intestines, and spleen to the liver?
options: The inferior vena cava
The hepatic portal vein
The superior mesenteric artery
The hepatic veins
questions.why: The hepatic portal vein forms behind the pancreas where the splenic vein and superior mesenteric vein join, and it carries blood from the digestive organs and spleen into the liver. This blood has already passed through one capillary bed in the gut and then passes through a second one, the liver sinusoids, which is what makes it a portal system. It lets the liver process absorbed nutrients before the blood returns to the heart.
notes: The inferior vena cava receives blood from the hepatic veins and returns it to the heart. It would be the answer for the large vein behind the liver, not the vessel bringing gut blood in.
Correct. The hepatic portal vein carries gut and spleen blood to the liver.

The superior mesenteric artery carries oxygen-rich blood from the aorta to the small intestine. It supplies the intestines rather than draining them, so pick it for arterial supply to the small intestine.
The hepatic veins carry blood out of the liver into the inferior vena cava. Pick them for the vessels that drain the liver, the opposite direction from the portal vein.
questions.answerText: The hepatic portal vein

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Blood from the stomach and intestines travels through the hepatic portal vein to the liver before it returns to the heart. What does this arrangement allow?
options: The intestines receive their oxygen-rich blood supply straight from the liver
Bile can be added to the blood so it travels to the duodenum
The liver can process absorbed nutrients before that blood reaches the rest of the body
Intestinal blood can skip the liver's capillaries and return quickly to the heart
questions.why: The hepatic portal system is a portal system, meaning blood passes through two capillary beds in a row before returning to the heart. Blood picks up absorbed nutrients in the capillaries of the gut, then flows through the hepatic portal vein into the liver sinusoids, the second capillary bed. This lets hepatocytes take up, store, and process nutrients and filter the blood before it enters the general circulation.
notes: The intestines get oxygen-rich blood from arteries off the aorta, such as the superior and inferior mesenteric arteries. Pick those arteries for the blood supply to the intestines.
Bile reaches the duodenum through the bile ducts, not through the blood. Students choose this when they mix up the liver's duct system with its blood supply.
Correct. The portal route lets the liver process nutrients first.
This describes the opposite of a portal system. Portal blood is forced through the liver sinusoids, a second capillary bed, rather than bypassing them.
questions.answerText: The liver can process absorbed nutrients before that blood reaches the rest of the body

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: The ovarian arteries reach the ovaries through the suspensory ligaments. From which vessel do they branch?
options: The abdominal aorta
The renal artery
The internal iliac artery
The external iliac artery
questions.why: The ovarian arteries are the gonadal arteries in females. They branch directly from the abdominal aorta just below the renal arteries and travel down into the pelvis, entering the suspensory ligament to reach the ovary. They start high because the ovaries develop high in the abdomen and move down before birth.
notes: Correct. The ovarian arteries branch from the abdominal aorta.
The renal artery supplies the kidney. The ovarian arteries arise just below it, but from the aorta. Pick the renal artery for the blood supply of the kidney.
The internal iliac artery supplies the pelvic organs, including the uterus through the uterine artery, but it does not give off the ovarian artery. Pick it for the main artery of the pelvic organs.
The external iliac artery continues into the lower limb as the femoral artery. Pick it for the vessel that supplies the leg.
questions.answerText: The abdominal aorta

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Which three unpaired arteries branch from the front of the abdominal aorta to supply the digestive tract?
options: Celiac trunk and both mesenteric arteries
Celiac trunk, renal, and splenic arteries
Splenic, common hepatic, and left gastric arteries
Renal, gonadal, and common iliac arteries
questions.why: Three single, unpaired arteries leave the front of the abdominal aorta for the gut. The celiac trunk, highest of the three, supplies the stomach, liver, spleen and part of the pancreas. The superior mesenteric artery supplies most of the small intestine and the beginning of the large intestine, and the inferior mesenteric artery supplies the final part of the large intestine.
notes: Correct. The celiac trunk and the superior and inferior mesenteric arteries are the three unpaired gut branches.
The celiac trunk is correct, but the renal arteries are paired branches to the kidneys and the splenic artery is a branch of the celiac trunk, not of the aorta.
The splenic, common hepatic and left gastric arteries are the three branches of the celiac trunk. Pick this list for a question about what the celiac trunk divides into.

The renal and gonadal arteries are paired branches that leave the sides of the aorta, one to each side of the body, and the common iliac arteries are the aorta's terminal split. This list fits a question about paired branches.
questions.answerText: Celiac trunk and both mesenteric arteries

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: What does the hepatic portal vein carry, and where does it take it?
options: Filtered blood from the kidneys to the inferior vena cava
Oxygenated blood straight from the aorta to the liver
Nutrient-rich blood from the gut organs to the liver
Processed blood from the liver to the inferior vena cava
questions.why: A portal system carries blood through two capillary beds in a row. Blood leaving the capillaries of the stomach, intestines, spleen and pancreas collects into the hepatic portal vein, which carries it to the liver instead of straight back to the heart. In the liver it flows through the sinusoids, the second capillary bed, so absorbed nutrients and toxins are processed before reaching the rest of the body.
notes: Blood from the kidneys drains through the renal veins directly into the inferior vena cava, without passing through the liver. Choose it for a question about kidney drainage.
Oxygenated blood from the aorta reaches the liver through the hepatic artery, which arises from the celiac trunk. Pick it for a question about the liver's oxygen supply.
Correct. The hepatic portal vein brings nutrient-rich blood from the digestive organs to the liver.
Blood leaving the liver drains through the hepatic veins into the inferior vena cava. That is the answer for the vessels that empty the liver.
questions.answerText: Nutrient-rich blood from the gut organs to the liver

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: The hepatic portal vein forms from the union of which two main veins?
options: Splenic and superior mesenteric veins
Right, middle, and left hepatic veins
Left renal vein and left gonadal vein
Right and left common iliac veins
questions.why: The hepatic portal vein forms behind the neck of the pancreas, where the splenic vein from the left joins the superior mesenteric vein from the intestines. Together these collect blood from the spleen, stomach, pancreas and intestines. The inferior mesenteric vein usually drains into the splenic vein before this junction.
notes: Correct. The splenic and superior mesenteric veins join to form the hepatic portal vein.
The hepatic veins drain blood out of the liver into the inferior vena cava, the opposite direction from the portal vein. They would be the answer for the vessels that empty the liver.
The left gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein, which then empties into the inferior vena cava. This pair is about drainage to the vena cava, not the portal system.
The right and left common iliac veins join to form the inferior vena cava, which returns blood from the lower body to the heart. Pick this pair for a question about how the inferior vena cava forms.
questions.answerText: Splenic and superior mesenteric veins

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Where does the descending aorta become the abdominal aorta?
options: The esophageal hiatus of the diaphragm
The caval opening of the diaphragm
The level of the sternal angle
The aortic hiatus of the diaphragm
questions.why: The descending aorta runs down through the thorax as the thoracic aorta and passes through the diaphragm at the aortic hiatus, an opening at about the level of the T12 vertebra. Below that opening it is called the abdominal aorta. The name changes because the vessel has moved from the thoracic cavity into the abdominal cavity, not because it branches.
notes: The esophageal hiatus is the opening in the diaphragm that lets the esophagus pass into the abdomen to reach the stomach. Pick it for a question about where the esophagus crosses the diaphragm or where a hiatal hernia occurs.

The caval opening is the hole in the diaphragm that carries the inferior vena cava up into the thorax toward the right atrium. It would be the answer for where the inferior vena cava passes through the diaphragm.

The sternal angle marks the level where the aortic arch begins and ends, so it is where the descending thoracic aorta starts, not the abdominal aorta. Choose it if the question asked where the aortic arch ends.
Correct. The aorta becomes the abdominal aorta once it passes through the aortic hiatus.
questions.answerText: The aortic hiatus of the diaphragm

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: The abdominal aorta ends by dividing into which pair of arteries?
options: Internal and external iliac arteries
Right and left femoral arteries
Right and left common iliac arteries
Right and left renal arteries
questions.why: Near the level of the L4 vertebra, the abdominal aorta splits into the right and left common iliac arteries. This split is called the aortic bifurcation. Each common iliac artery then carries blood toward the pelvis and lower limb on its own side.
notes: The internal and external iliac arteries form one step later, when each common iliac artery divides. Choose this pair if the question asked how a common iliac artery ends.

The femoral arteries are in the thighs. Each one is the continuation of an external iliac artery after it passes under the inguinal ligament, two steps beyond the aortic bifurcation. Pick them for the main artery of the thigh.
Correct. The aorta ends at its bifurcation into the two common iliac arteries.

The renal arteries are paired side branches that leave the aorta higher up, near L1 and L2, to supply the kidneys. The aorta keeps going after they branch, so they are not its end. Pick them for the vessels that carry blood into the kidneys at the hilum.
questions.answerText: Right and left common iliac arteries

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Which artery is the first unpaired branch to leave the abdominal aorta just below the diaphragm?
options: Celiac trunk
Superior mesenteric artery
Common hepatic artery
Inferior mesenteric artery
questions.why: The celiac trunk is a short, wide artery that leaves the front of the abdominal aorta almost as soon as the aorta enters the abdomen, at about T12. It is the first of the three unpaired branches that supply the digestive tract. After a short distance it splits into the left gastric, splenic, and common hepatic arteries.
notes: Correct. The celiac trunk is the highest of the three unpaired branches.

The superior mesenteric artery is the second unpaired branch, arising just below the celiac trunk at about L1. Pick it for the artery that supplies the small intestine and the first part of the large intestine.

The common hepatic artery does not come straight off the aorta. It is one of the three branches of the celiac trunk and carries blood toward the liver, so choose it for the celiac branch that heads to the liver.
The inferior mesenteric artery is the third and lowest unpaired branch, arising at about L3. It would be the answer for the artery to the descending colon, sigmoid colon, and upper rectum.
questions.answerText: Celiac trunk

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: The celiac trunk divides into which three arteries?
options: Left gastric, splenic, and common hepatic arteries
Splenic, renal, and suprarenal arteries
Common hepatic, renal, and gonadal arteries
Left gastric, splenic, and superior mesenteric arteries
questions.why: The celiac trunk is short and splits almost at once into three arteries. The left gastric artery goes to the stomach along its lesser curvature, the splenic artery runs to the left toward the spleen, and the common hepatic artery heads right toward the liver. Together these three supply the stomach, spleen, liver, gallbladder, and parts of the pancreas and duodenum.
notes: Correct. These are the three branches of the celiac trunk.

The renal and suprarenal arteries are paired side branches of the abdominal aorta that supply the kidneys and adrenal glands. They come straight off the aorta, so they belong in a list of its paired branches, not the celiac trunk's.

The common hepatic artery is a celiac branch, but the renal and gonadal arteries are paired branches straight off the aorta. Choose renal and gonadal arteries for questions about the kidneys and the testes or ovaries.

The left gastric and splenic arteries are celiac branches, but the superior mesenteric artery is a separate unpaired branch that leaves the aorta just below the celiac trunk. Pick it on its own for the artery to the small intestine.
questions.answerText: Left gastric, splenic, and common hepatic arteries

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Which branch of the celiac trunk runs to the left along the upper border of the pancreas to reach the spleen?
options: Left gastric artery
Common hepatic artery
Superior mesenteric artery
Splenic artery
questions.why: The splenic artery is usually the largest branch of the celiac trunk. It runs to the left along the upper edge of the pancreas, often in a winding path, and enters the spleen at its hilum. Along the way it also sends small branches to the pancreas and to part of the stomach.
notes: The left gastric artery is the smallest celiac branch. It rises toward the lesser curvature of the stomach and also supplies the lower esophagus. Pick it for the celiac branch that feeds the lesser curvature.

The common hepatic artery runs to the right from the celiac trunk, toward the liver and gallbladder. It goes the opposite direction from the splenic artery, so choose it for the celiac branch heading to the liver.
The superior mesenteric artery is not a celiac branch at all. It leaves the aorta separately, just below the celiac trunk, and supplies the small intestine and the first part of the large intestine.
Correct. The splenic artery travels along the pancreas to the spleen.
questions.answerText: Splenic artery

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Which artery supplies the jejunum and ileum?
options: Inferior mesenteric artery
Internal iliac artery
Superior mesenteric artery
Celiac trunk
questions.why: The superior mesenteric artery leaves the front of the aorta just below the celiac trunk and fans out through the mesentery, the fold of peritoneum that holds the small intestine. Its branches supply most of the small intestine, including the jejunum and ileum, plus the cecum, appendix, ascending colon, and most of the transverse colon. It also helps supply the head of the pancreas.
notes: The inferior mesenteric artery supplies the last part of the large intestine, including the descending colon, sigmoid colon, and upper rectum. It would be the answer for those regions.
The internal iliac artery supplies the pelvic organs, such as the urinary bladder, rectum, and uterus or prostate, along with the gluteal muscles. Choose it for structures in the pelvis.
Correct. The superior mesenteric artery supplies the jejunum and ileum.
The celiac trunk supplies the upper digestive organs: the stomach, spleen, liver, gallbladder, and the first part of the duodenum. Pick it for those organs rather than the jejunum and ileum.
questions.answerText: Superior mesenteric artery

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Which artery supplies the descending colon, sigmoid colon, and upper rectum?
options: Superior mesenteric artery
Celiac trunk
External iliac artery
Inferior mesenteric artery
questions.why: The inferior mesenteric artery is the lowest of the three unpaired arteries to the gut, leaving the front of the aorta at about L3. It supplies the last stretch of the large intestine: the far end of the transverse colon, the descending colon, the sigmoid colon, and the upper rectum. Lower parts of the rectum get blood from branches of the internal iliac arteries.
notes: The superior mesenteric artery supplies the small intestine and the first part of the large intestine, from the cecum through most of the transverse colon. Pick it if the question listed the jejunum, ileum, or ascending colon.
The celiac trunk supplies the upper abdominal organs, including the stomach, spleen, and liver. It would be the answer for those organs, not the lower colon.
The external iliac artery carries blood out of the pelvis toward the lower limb, where it becomes the femoral artery. Choose it for the main route of blood into the leg.
Correct. The inferior mesenteric artery supplies the lower large intestine.
questions.answerText: Inferior mesenteric artery

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Which paired branches of the abdominal aorta enter the kidneys at the hilum?
options: Gonadal arteries
Suprarenal arteries
Lumbar arteries
Renal arteries
questions.why: The renal arteries leave the sides of the abdominal aorta at about L1 to L2, usually just below the superior mesenteric artery. Each one travels sideways to its kidney and enters at the hilum, the indented medial border where vessels and the ureter enter and leave. The kidneys receive a large share of the blood the heart pumps out, so these are large arteries.
notes: The gonadal arteries are long, thin paired branches that leave the aorta below the renal arteries and run down to the testes or ovaries. They would be the answer for blood supply to the gonads.
The suprarenal arteries are small paired branches that supply the adrenal glands, which sit on top of the kidneys. Pick them for blood supply to the adrenal glands.

The lumbar arteries are several small pairs that leave the back of the aorta and supply the posterior abdominal wall, including the muscles and vertebrae of the lower back. Choose them for blood supply to the body wall rather than an organ.
Correct. The renal arteries enter each kidney at its hilum.
questions.answerText: Renal arteries

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: The external iliac artery changes its name to the femoral artery as it passes under which structure?
options: The iliac crest
The linea alba
The inguinal ligament
The obturator foramen
questions.why: The inguinal ligament stretches from the anterior superior iliac spine to the pubic tubercle and marks the boundary between the abdomen and the thigh. The external iliac artery runs along the pelvic brim and passes beneath this ligament into the thigh. From that point on, the same vessel is called the femoral artery.
notes: The iliac crest is the curved upper rim of the ilium that you feel at your hip, and no major artery changes its name there. It would be the answer for the landmark used to find the level of the L4 vertebra.

The linea alba is the band of connective tissue running down the midline of the anterior abdominal wall where the abdominal muscle sheaths meet. It contains no major vessels, so choose it for questions about the abdominal wall instead.
Correct. Below the inguinal ligament the external iliac artery becomes the femoral artery.

The obturator foramen is the large opening in the hip bone that the obturator nerve and vessels pass through to reach the medial thigh. Pick it for the route of the obturator vessels, not the femoral artery.
questions.answerText: The inguinal ligament

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Which artery is the main blood supply to the urinary bladder and to the uterus or prostate?
options: External iliac artery
Internal iliac artery
Inferior mesenteric artery
Femoral artery
questions.why: Each common iliac artery splits into an internal and an external iliac artery. The internal iliac artery dives into the pelvis and supplies the pelvic organs, including the urinary bladder, rectum, and uterus or prostate, as well as the gluteal muscles and perineum. The external iliac artery, by contrast, heads out to the lower limb.
notes: The external iliac artery is the other branch of the common iliac artery. It runs along the pelvic brim and leaves the pelvis to become the femoral artery, so pick it for blood supply to the lower limb.
Correct. The internal iliac artery supplies the pelvic organs.

The inferior mesenteric artery supplies the descending colon, sigmoid colon, and upper rectum. It does not supply the bladder or reproductive organs, so choose it for questions about the lower large intestine.
The femoral artery is the main artery of the thigh, continuing from the external iliac artery below the inguinal ligament. It would be the answer for blood supply to the thigh, not the pelvic organs.
questions.answerText: Internal iliac artery

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: The inferior vena cava begins where which two veins join?
options: Right and left renal veins
Splenic and superior mesenteric veins
Right and left common iliac veins
Internal and external iliac veins
questions.why: The right and left common iliac veins join at about the level of L5, just to the right of the midline, to form the inferior vena cava. From there the inferior vena cava runs up the posterior abdominal wall on the right side of the aorta, collects blood from the lower body, passes through the diaphragm, and empties into the right atrium.
notes: The renal veins drain the kidneys and empty into the inferior vena cava partway up, at about L1 to L2. They join a vena cava that already exists, so pick them for tributaries of the inferior vena cava, not its starting point.

The splenic and superior mesenteric veins join behind the pancreas to form the hepatic portal vein, which carries blood to the liver rather than straight to the heart. Choose them for the formation of the portal vein.
Correct. The two common iliac veins unite to form the inferior vena cava.
The internal and external iliac veins join one step earlier to form each common iliac vein. Pick this pair if the question asked how a common iliac vein forms.
questions.answerText: Right and left common iliac veins

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Where does the left gonadal (testicular or ovarian) vein drain?
options: Into the left common iliac vein
Directly into the inferior vena cava
Into the left renal vein
Into the inferior mesenteric vein
questions.why: The two gonadal veins drain differently because the inferior vena cava sits on the right side of the abdomen. The right gonadal vein empties straight into the inferior vena cava, but the left gonadal vein runs up to the left renal vein and empties into it. The left renal vein then crosses in front of the aorta to reach the inferior vena cava.
notes: The left common iliac vein drains the left lower limb and pelvis and joins the right common iliac vein to form the inferior vena cava. The gonadal vein rises far above it, so pick it for drainage of the pelvis and leg.
The inferior vena cava is where the right gonadal vein drains directly. Choose it if the question asked about the right side.
Correct. The left gonadal vein empties into the left renal vein.

The inferior mesenteric vein drains the lower large intestine and is part of the hepatic portal system, carrying blood toward the liver. It would be the answer for drainage of the descending and sigmoid colon.
questions.answerText: Into the left renal vein

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Blood leaves the liver through the hepatic veins. Where do the hepatic veins empty?
options: Into the hepatic portal vein
Into the inferior vena cava
Into the superior vena cava
Into the right renal vein
questions.why: After blood filters through the liver sinusoids, it collects into central veins (small veins at the center of each liver lobule) and then into the hepatic veins, usually three large ones. The hepatic veins leave the back of the liver and empty into the inferior vena cava just below the diaphragm. From there the blood travels a short distance up into the right atrium.
notes: The hepatic portal vein carries blood into the liver from the digestive organs, so it is upstream of the liver, not downstream. Pick it for the vessel that delivers nutrient-rich blood to the liver.
Correct. The hepatic veins drain into the inferior vena cava.

The superior vena cava drains the head, neck, upper limbs, and chest into the right atrium. The liver is below the heart, so its veins join the inferior vena cava instead. Choose the superior vena cava for drainage of the upper body.
The right renal vein drains the right kidney and is a short tributary of the inferior vena cava. It would be the answer for blood leaving the right kidney.
questions.answerText: Into the inferior vena cava

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: The inferior mesenteric vein usually empties into which vein?
options: The inferior vena cava
The left renal vein
The left common iliac vein
The splenic vein
questions.why: The inferior mesenteric vein collects blood from the descending colon, sigmoid colon, and upper rectum. It usually runs upward and empties into the splenic vein behind the pancreas, and the splenic vein then joins the superior mesenteric vein to form the hepatic portal vein. This keeps blood from the lower large intestine in the portal system, so it passes through the liver first.
notes: The inferior vena cava receives veins from the kidneys, body wall, and liver, but veins from the intestines do not drain into it directly. Choose it for veins like the renal or hepatic veins.
The left renal vein drains the left kidney and also receives the left gonadal vein. Pick it for the vein that the left testicular or ovarian vein empties into.
The left common iliac vein drains the left lower limb and pelvis and helps form the inferior vena cava. It would be the answer for drainage of the left leg, not the colon.
Correct. The inferior mesenteric vein usually joins the splenic vein.
questions.answerText: The splenic vein

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: What makes the hepatic portal system a portal system?
options: Its veins have no valves and drain straight into the right atrium
Blood passes through two capillary beds before reaching the heart
Blood passes through the liver before entering any capillary bed
Its veins carry oxygen-rich blood straight from the aorta to the liver
questions.why: A portal system links two capillary beds in a row: blood passes through one capillary bed, collects into a vein, and then enters a second capillary bed before heading back to the heart. In the hepatic portal system, the first capillary bed is in the walls of the stomach, intestines, and other digestive organs, and the second is the sinusoids of the liver. Most veins, by contrast, carry blood from one capillary bed straight back toward the heart.
notes: Whether veins have valves is not what defines a portal system, and portal blood does not drain straight into the right atrium. It first passes through the liver, then the hepatic veins and the inferior vena cava, so this choice mixes up the portal vein with the vena cava.
Correct. Two capillary beds in series define a portal system.

Portal blood has already passed through one capillary bed in the digestive organs before it reaches the liver. This statement leaves out that first capillary bed, which is half of what makes the system a portal system.

The hepatic portal vein carries oxygen-poor blood that has already passed through the digestive organs. Oxygen-rich blood reaches the liver through the hepatic artery, a branch of the celiac trunk, so this statement describes the hepatic artery, not a portal system.
questions.answerText: Blood passes through two capillary beds before reaching the heart

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: The medial umbilical ligament on the inside of the anterior abdominal wall is a remnant of which fetal vessel?
options: Umbilical vein
Ductus arteriosus
Umbilical artery
Ductus venosus
questions.why: Before birth, two umbilical arteries branch from the internal iliac arteries and carry blood from the fetus out to the placenta. After birth, the far portion of each artery closes off and becomes a fibrous cord, the medial umbilical ligament, which runs up the inside of the anterior abdominal wall toward the umbilicus. The part closest to the internal iliac artery usually stays open and supplies the bladder.
notes: The umbilical vein carried oxygen-rich blood from the placenta to the fetus. After birth it becomes the ligamentum teres, the round ligament in the free edge of the falciform ligament of the liver, so pick it for the origin of the round ligament.

The ductus arteriosus was a fetal shunt between the pulmonary trunk and the aortic arch that let blood bypass the lungs. It becomes the ligamentum arteriosum in the thorax, so pick it for that remnant.
Correct. Each medial umbilical ligament is what remains of an umbilical artery.

The ductus venosus was a fetal shunt in the liver that let blood from the umbilical vein bypass the liver tissue and reach the inferior vena cava. It becomes the ligamentum venosum, so choose it for that remnant.
questions.answerText: Umbilical artery

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Which vein runs along the back of the pancreas, carrying blood from the spleen toward the hepatic portal vein?
options: Splenic vein
Inferior mesenteric vein
Left gastric vein
Left renal vein
questions.why: The splenic vein leaves the spleen at its hilum and runs to the right along the back of the pancreas. Behind the neck of the pancreas it joins the superior mesenteric vein to form the hepatic portal vein. Along the way it collects blood from the pancreas and part of the stomach, and it usually receives the inferior mesenteric vein as well.
notes: Correct. The splenic vein runs behind the pancreas to help form the portal vein.

The inferior mesenteric vein drains the lower large intestine and usually empties into the splenic vein. It is a tributary of the splenic vein, so pick it for drainage of the descending and sigmoid colon rather than the spleen.
The left gastric vein drains the lesser curvature of the stomach and usually empties into the hepatic portal vein. It would be the answer for drainage of the lesser curvature, not the spleen.

The left renal vein also crosses the abdomen from left to right, but it drains the left kidney, passes in front of the aorta, and empties into the inferior vena cava. Pick it for the vein that carries blood from the left kidney.
questions.answerText: Splenic vein

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Moving from superior to inferior along the abdominal aorta, in what order do the three unpaired branches to the digestive tract arise?
options: Superior mesenteric artery, celiac trunk, inferior mesenteric artery
Inferior mesenteric artery, superior mesenteric artery, celiac trunk
Celiac trunk, superior mesenteric artery, inferior mesenteric artery
Celiac trunk, inferior mesenteric artery, superior mesenteric artery
questions.why: The celiac trunk leaves the aorta first, at about T12, just below the diaphragm. The superior mesenteric artery follows at about L1, and the inferior mesenteric artery arises lower, at about L3. The order matches the parts of the gut they supply: the stomach and liver at the top, then the small intestine and first part of the colon, then the last part of the colon and the rectum.
notes: This order swaps the first two. The superior mesenteric artery arises just below the celiac trunk, not above it. Students often pick this because the word superior sounds like it should come first.
This is the correct sequence read in reverse, from inferior to superior. Pick it only if the question asked for the order moving up the aorta from the bifurcation.
Correct. The celiac trunk leaves first at about T12, the superior mesenteric follows at about L1, and the inferior mesenteric arises at about L3.
This order puts the inferior mesenteric artery in the middle, but as its name says, it is the lowest of the three. The superior mesenteric artery comes before it.
questions.answerText: Celiac trunk, superior mesenteric artery, inferior mesenteric artery

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the unpaired and paired branches of the abdominal aorta?
options: Unpaired branches supply the pelvis and lower limbs; paired branches supply all of the abdominal organs
Unpaired branches supply the digestive organs; paired branches supply the kidneys, adrenals, gonads, and body wall
Unpaired branches supply the kidneys and gonads; paired branches supply the stomach, intestines, liver, and spleen
Unpaired branches supply only the liver and spleen; paired branches supply the small and large intestine
questions.why: The three unpaired branches (the celiac trunk and the superior and inferior mesenteric arteries) leave the front of the aorta and supply the digestive tract, its accessory organs, and the spleen. The paired branches leave the sides of the aorta in left and right pairs and supply paired structures: the adrenal glands, kidneys, gonads, and, through the lumbar arteries, the posterior abdominal wall.
notes: The pelvis and lower limbs are supplied by the common iliac arteries, the two branches at the very bottom of the aorta, not by its unpaired branches. This choice confuses the way the aorta ends with its branches along the way.
Correct. Unpaired branches go to the gut; paired branches go to paired organs and the body wall.

This statement reverses the two groups. The kidneys and gonads are paired organs, so they get paired arteries (renal and gonadal), while the stomach, intestines, liver, and spleen get the unpaired midline branches.

The liver and spleen are supplied by the celiac trunk, but the intestines are also supplied by unpaired branches, the superior and inferior mesenteric arteries. No paired branch supplies the intestines.
questions.answerText: Unpaired branches supply the digestive organs; paired branches supply the kidneys, adrenals, gonads, and body wall

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Where do the renal arteries usually arise along the abdominal aorta?
options: From the common iliac arteries
Just above the celiac trunk
Just below the superior mesenteric artery
Just below the inferior mesenteric artery
questions.why: The renal arteries usually leave the sides of the aorta at about L1 to L2, just below the origin of the superior mesenteric artery. This places them high in the abdomen, level with the kidneys, which sit against the posterior abdominal wall between about T12 and L3. Knowing that the renal arteries sit just below the superior mesenteric artery helps you find them on a model or cadaver.
notes: The common iliac arteries supply the pelvis and lower limbs and begin at the aortic bifurcation, well below the kidneys. Pick them for the vessels that divide into the internal and external iliac arteries.

At or just above the celiac trunk is where the inferior phrenic arteries usually arise to supply the underside of the diaphragm. The renal arteries come off lower, below both the celiac trunk and the superior mesenteric artery.
Correct. The renal arteries usually arise just below the superior mesenteric artery.

Just below the inferior mesenteric artery would put the renal arteries near L3 or L4, close to the aortic bifurcation and below the kidneys. Students pick this when they mix up the superior and inferior mesenteric arteries.
questions.answerText: Just below the superior mesenteric artery

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: On its way to the inferior vena cava, the left renal vein passes in front of which large vessel?
options: The inferior vena cava
The hepatic portal vein
The left common iliac artery
The abdominal aorta
questions.why: The inferior vena cava lies to the right of the aorta, so the left renal vein has farther to travel than the right one. It crosses from the left kidney toward the right, passing in front of the abdominal aorta just below the origin of the superior mesenteric artery, and then empties into the inferior vena cava. This is why the left renal vein is longer than the right renal vein.
notes: The inferior vena cava is the left renal vein's destination, not a vessel it passes in front of. Pick it for the vein that both renal veins empty into.

The hepatic portal vein forms behind the pancreas and runs up to the liver, above and in front of the left renal vein's path. Pick it for the vessel that carries blood from the digestive organs to the liver.

The left common iliac artery begins at the aortic bifurcation near L4, far below the kidneys, and the left renal vein never reaches it. Choose it for blood flow to the left side of the pelvis and the left leg.
Correct. The left renal vein crosses in front of the abdominal aorta.
questions.answerText: The abdominal aorta

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: The testicular arteries branch from the abdominal aorta near the kidneys, far above the scrotum. What explains this high starting point?
options: The high origin keeps the testes warmer than the other abdominal organs
The testes develop high in the abdomen and descend, bringing their arteries along
The testicular arteries branch from the renal arteries and only appear to start high
Blood must pass through the kidneys first so it is filtered before reaching the testes
questions.why: The testes form on the posterior abdominal wall near the developing kidneys, and they receive their blood supply there. Before birth, each testis descends through the inguinal canal into the scrotum, and its artery, vein, and nerves are pulled along behind it inside the spermatic cord. The ovaries follow a similar but shorter descent into the pelvis, which is why the ovarian arteries also start near the kidneys.
notes: The scrotum keeps the testes slightly cooler than the body core, not warmer, because sperm production works best a little below 37°C (98.6°F). Where the artery branches has nothing to do with temperature.
Correct. The arteries start where the testes first developed.

The testicular arteries usually come straight off the front of the abdominal aorta, just below the renal arteries. The renal arteries enter the kidneys and do not normally give rise to them, so this choice confuses neighboring branches.

Arterial blood does not pass through the kidneys on its way to other organs. Each organ gets its own branch of the aorta, so this choice mixes up the arteries with the filtering path blood takes inside the kidney itself.
questions.answerText: The testes develop high in the abdomen and descend, bringing their arteries along

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares how the right and left gonadal veins drain?
options: The right drains into the right renal vein; the left drains into the inferior vena cava
Both gonadal veins empty into the hepatic portal vein
Both gonadal veins empty directly into the inferior vena cava
The right drains into the inferior vena cava; the left drains into the left renal vein
questions.why: The inferior vena cava runs up the right side of the abdomen, close to the right gonadal vein, so that vein empties into it directly. The left gonadal vein is farther from the vena cava and ends by joining the left renal vein, which then crosses in front of the aorta to reach the inferior vena cava. The same left and right difference applies to the testicular veins in males and the ovarian veins in females.
notes: This is the drainage pattern reversed. It is the left gonadal vein that ends in a renal vein, because the inferior vena cava sits on the right side, near the right gonadal vein.
The hepatic portal vein collects blood from the digestive organs and spleen, not from the gonads. Pick it for veins such as the splenic and superior mesenteric veins.
Only the right gonadal vein empties straight into the inferior vena cava. This choice treats the two sides as mirror images, which is the most common mistake on this question.
Correct. The inferior vena cava lies on the right, so the right gonadal vein empties straight into it, while the left gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein.
questions.answerText: The right drains into the inferior vena cava; the left drains into the left renal vein

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Through its branches, one artery supplies the stomach, spleen, liver, and gallbladder. Which artery is it?
options: Celiac trunk
Splenic artery
Superior mesenteric artery
Common hepatic artery
questions.why: The celiac trunk divides into the left gastric, splenic, and common hepatic arteries, and together those three branches reach every organ in this list. The left gastric and splenic arteries supply the stomach and spleen, and the common hepatic artery supplies the liver and, through its branches, the gallbladder and parts of the stomach and duodenum. No single branch of the celiac trunk covers all four organs, but the trunk itself does.
notes: Correct. The celiac trunk reaches all four organs through its three branches.
The splenic artery supplies the spleen and also sends branches to the pancreas and part of the stomach, but it does not reach the liver or gallbladder. Pick it for blood flow to the spleen alone.
The superior mesenteric artery supplies the small intestine and the first part of the large intestine. Choose it if the list had named the jejunum, ileum, and ascending colon.
The common hepatic artery supplies the liver and gallbladder and parts of the stomach and duodenum, but not the spleen. It would be the answer if the spleen were left out of the list.
questions.answerText: Celiac trunk

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: The transverse colon receives blood from two arteries. Which pair?
options: Superior and inferior mesenteric arteries
Inferior mesenteric and internal iliac arteries
Celiac trunk and inferior mesenteric artery
Celiac trunk and superior mesenteric artery
questions.why: The transverse colon sits at the boundary between the territories of the two mesenteric arteries. The superior mesenteric artery supplies most of the transverse colon, and the inferior mesenteric artery supplies its last part. Connecting vessels run along the colon between the two territories, so each artery can help supply the other's area.
notes: Correct. The superior mesenteric artery supplies most of the transverse colon, and the inferior mesenteric artery supplies its last part.

The inferior mesenteric and internal iliac arteries share the supply of the rectum, at the far end of the large intestine. Pick this pair for a question about the rectum rather than the transverse colon.
The celiac trunk does not reach the colon. The inferior mesenteric artery in this pair is right for the last part of the transverse colon, but its partner should be the superior mesenteric artery.

The celiac trunk supplies the stomach, spleen, liver, and upper duodenum, not the colon. The duodenum is the organ that gets blood from both the celiac trunk and the superior mesenteric artery, so pick this pair for a question about the duodenum.
questions.answerText: Superior and inferior mesenteric arteries

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Glucose is absorbed into a capillary in the wall of the ileum. Which route does it follow on its way to the right atrium?
options: Superior mesenteric vein, inferior vena cava, hepatic portal vein, liver sinusoids, hepatic veins
Superior mesenteric vein, hepatic veins, liver sinusoids, hepatic portal vein, inferior vena cava
Superior mesenteric vein, hepatic portal vein, liver sinusoids, hepatic veins, inferior vena cava
Superior mesenteric artery, hepatic artery, liver sinusoids, hepatic veins, inferior vena cava
questions.why: Venous blood from the ileum drains into the superior mesenteric vein, which joins the splenic vein to form the hepatic portal vein. The portal vein delivers the glucose into the liver, where blood spreads through the sinusoids (wide, leaky capillaries between plates of liver cells) so the cells can take up nutrients. Blood then leaves through the hepatic veins into the inferior vena cava, which empties into the right atrium.
notes: Blood from the intestines does not enter the inferior vena cava before reaching the liver. This route skips the whole point of the portal system, which is to send intestinal blood through the liver first.

This route has the liver vessels in reverse order. The hepatic portal vein carries blood into the liver and the hepatic veins carry it out, so the portal vein must come before the sinusoids and the hepatic veins after them.
Correct. This is the portal route from the ileum through the liver to the heart.

Arteries carry blood toward the intestine, not away from it, so absorbed glucose cannot leave the ileum in the superior mesenteric artery. The hepatic artery does bring oxygen-rich blood into the liver, but it comes from the celiac trunk, not from the intestine.
questions.answerText: Superior mesenteric vein, hepatic portal vein, liver sinusoids, hepatic veins, inferior vena cava

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Why does blood from the stomach and intestines pass through the liver before it returns to the heart?
options: So the liver can add oxygen to blood that the intestines have used up
So the liver can pump the blood upward against gravity to the heart
So the liver can process absorbed nutrients and remove toxins first
So the liver can filter out water and form urine from the absorbed fluid
questions.why: Blood leaving the digestive tract carries everything that was just absorbed, including nutrients, drugs, alcohol, and toxins. Sending this blood through the liver first lets liver cells take up and store nutrients such as glucose, and break down or remove harmful substances before the blood reaches the rest of the body. Macrophages lining the liver sinusoids also remove bacteria that slip in from the gut.
notes: The liver does not add oxygen to blood. Oxygen is added in the lungs, and the liver receives its own oxygen-rich blood through the hepatic artery. Students choose this when they mix up the portal vein with the pulmonary circuit.

The liver is not a pump. The heart is the only pump in the circulation, and blood in the portal vein is moved by the pressure that remains after it passes through the gut capillaries. Students choose this when they picture the liver as a second heart.
Correct. The liver gets the first look at everything absorbed from the gut.
Filtering blood and forming urine is the work of the kidneys, not the liver. That would be the answer for why so much blood flows through the renal arteries.
questions.answerText: So the liver can process absorbed nutrients and remove toxins first

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: A catheter is threaded from the right femoral artery upward toward the heart. Which vessels does it pass through, in order, to reach the abdominal aorta?
options: Right external iliac artery, then right common iliac artery
Right external iliac artery, then right internal iliac artery
Right common iliac artery, then right external iliac artery
Right internal iliac artery, then right common iliac artery
questions.why: The femoral artery is the continuation of the external iliac artery below the inguinal ligament, so moving upward the catheter enters the external iliac artery first. The external and internal iliac arteries are the two branches of the common iliac artery, so the catheter next passes into the right common iliac artery. The right and left common iliac arteries meet at the aortic bifurcation, which opens into the abdominal aorta.
notes: Correct. The femoral artery continues upward as the external iliac artery, which comes off the common iliac artery, which leads straight into the aorta.

This route turns into the internal iliac artery after the external iliac artery, which would send the catheter down into the pelvis instead of up to the aorta. The internal and external iliac arteries are two branches that split from the same common iliac artery.

This is the right pair in the wrong order. Moving upward from the thigh, the catheter reaches the external iliac artery before the common iliac artery. This order describes blood flowing downward from the aorta to the leg.

The internal iliac artery is a side branch that dives into the pelvis to supply the pelvic organs and gluteal muscles. It does not connect to the femoral artery, so it would be on the route only for a catheter aimed at the pelvic organs.
questions.answerText: Right external iliac artery, then right common iliac artery

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Which of these veins does not empty directly into the inferior vena cava?
options: Hepatic vein
Superior mesenteric vein
Right gonadal vein
Right renal vein
questions.why: The superior mesenteric vein drains the small intestine and the first part of the large intestine, and it belongs to the hepatic portal system. It joins the splenic vein to form the hepatic portal vein, so its blood goes through the liver before it can reach the inferior vena cava. Veins from the kidneys, the right gonad, and the liver itself empty straight into the inferior vena cava.
notes: The hepatic veins carry blood out of the liver and empty directly into the inferior vena cava just below the diaphragm. They are the last step of the portal route, so choose them for the vessels that drain the liver.
Correct. The superior mesenteric vein drains into the portal system, not the vena cava.
The right gonadal vein empties directly into the inferior vena cava. Its partner on the left would fit this question, because the left gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein instead.
The right renal vein is short and empties straight into the inferior vena cava, which sits just beside the right kidney. Pick it for the vein that drains the right kidney.
questions.answerText: Superior mesenteric vein

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Which two capillary beds does blood pass through in the hepatic portal system, in order?
options: Capillaries of the lungs, then the liver sinusoids
Capillaries of the kidneys, then the liver sinusoids
Capillaries of the digestive organs, then the liver sinusoids
The liver sinusoids, then capillaries of the digestive organs
questions.why: Blood first passes through capillaries in the walls of the stomach, intestines, pancreas, and spleen, where it picks up absorbed nutrients and other substances. It then collects into the hepatic portal vein and enters the second capillary bed, the liver sinusoids, which are wide, leaky capillaries running between plates of liver cells. Only after the sinusoids does the blood leave through the hepatic veins toward the heart.
notes: The lungs belong to the pulmonary circuit, which carries blood from the right ventricle to the lungs and back to the left atrium. Lung capillaries are where blood picks up oxygen, so choose them for a question about gas exchange.

Kidney blood drains through the renal veins straight into the inferior vena cava, so the kidneys are not part of the hepatic portal system. Pick kidney capillaries for a question about where blood is filtered to form urine.
Correct. Digestive capillaries come first and the liver sinusoids second.
This is the right pair in reverse. Blood reaches the liver after the digestive organs, not before, because the liver's job here is to process what the gut has just absorbed.
questions.answerText: Capillaries of the digestive organs, then the liver sinusoids

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: A clot blocks the superior mesenteric artery near its origin. Which part of the digestive tract is most at risk of losing its blood supply?
options: The jejunum, ileum, and ascending colon
The stomach and the first part of the duodenum
The esophagus and the stomach
The descending colon and the sigmoid colon
questions.why: The superior mesenteric artery supplies most of the small intestine, including the jejunum and ileum, along with the cecum, appendix, ascending colon, and most of the transverse colon. A clot near its origin cuts off flow to all of these branches at once. Without blood, the bowel wall can die, which is why a blocked superior mesenteric artery is a surgical emergency.
notes: Correct. These regions all depend on the superior mesenteric artery.

The stomach and first part of the duodenum are supplied by branches of the celiac trunk, which arises just above the superior mesenteric artery. They would be at risk if the clot blocked the celiac trunk instead.
The lower esophagus and stomach get blood from the left gastric artery and other celiac branches, not from the superior mesenteric artery. Choose these for a problem with the celiac trunk.
The descending and sigmoid colon are supplied by the inferior mesenteric artery, the lowest unpaired branch. Pick them for a blockage of the inferior mesenteric artery.
questions.answerText: The jejunum, ileum, and ascending colon

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: A clot forms at the origin of the celiac trunk. Which of these organs would lose its main arterial supply?
options: Ileum
Spleen
Left kidney
Sigmoid colon
questions.why: The celiac trunk divides into the left gastric, splenic, and common hepatic arteries. The spleen gets its blood from the splenic artery, so a clot at the start of the celiac trunk cuts off its main supply. The stomach and liver would also lose arterial flow from this trunk, although the liver still receives blood through the hepatic portal vein.
notes: The ileum is supplied by the superior mesenteric artery, which arises separately just below the celiac trunk. It would be the answer for a superior mesenteric artery blockage.
Correct. The spleen depends on the splenic artery, a celiac branch.
The left kidney is supplied by the left renal artery, a paired branch that leaves the side of the aorta below the celiac trunk. Pick it for a blockage of the left renal artery.
The sigmoid colon is supplied by the inferior mesenteric artery, the lowest of the unpaired branches. Choose it for a blockage of the inferior mesenteric artery.
questions.answerText: Spleen

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: Scarring from cirrhosis makes it hard for blood to flow through the liver. Which vessel would back up first as blood struggles to enter the liver?
options: The left renal vein
The hepatic portal vein
The hepatic veins
The inferior vena cava
questions.why: The hepatic portal vein delivers blood from the stomach, intestines, pancreas, and spleen into the liver. When scar tissue narrows the paths through the liver, blood has trouble getting through, so pressure rises upstream in the portal vein and its tributaries. This is called portal hypertension, and it can make the splenic vein and spleen swell as blood backs up.
notes: The left renal vein drains the left kidney into the inferior vena cava and is not part of the portal system, so liver scarring does not back blood up into it. Choose it for a question about the left kidney or the left gonadal vein.
Correct. The portal vein is upstream of the liver, so pressure builds there first.

The hepatic veins carry blood out of the liver, so they are downstream of the scarring, and blood that cannot get through the liver does not pile up in them. Pick them for the vessels that drain the liver into the inferior vena cava.

The inferior vena cava receives blood after it leaves the liver, so a blockage inside the liver does not back blood up into it. It would back up from a problem above it, such as failure of the right side of the heart.
questions.answerText: The hepatic portal vein

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: A mass presses on the left renal vein just before it reaches the inferior vena cava. Besides the left kidney, drainage from which organ could be affected?
options: The descending colon
The right testis or ovary
The spleen
The left testis or ovary
questions.why: The left gonadal vein does not reach the inferior vena cava on its own. It empties into the left renal vein, so anything that blocks the left renal vein near its end also slows drainage from the left testis or ovary. This is one reason swollen veins around the testis (a varicocele) are much more common on the left side.
notes: The descending colon drains through the inferior mesenteric vein into the portal system, not into the renal veins. It would be affected by a blockage of the inferior mesenteric or hepatic portal vein.

The right gonadal vein empties directly into the inferior vena cava, so pressure on the left renal vein would not affect it. Pick the right side for a question about which gonadal vein empties straight into the inferior vena cava.

The spleen drains through the splenic vein into the hepatic portal vein, which goes to the liver. It has no connection to the left renal vein, so choose it for a blockage of the splenic or portal vein.
Correct. The left gonadal vein drains through the left renal vein.
questions.answerText: The left testis or ovary

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: During surgery, the abdominal aorta is clamped just above its bifurcation. Which arteries beyond the clamp would lose their blood flow?
options: Both common iliac arteries
Both renal arteries
The superior mesenteric artery
The celiac trunk and its branches
questions.why: The bifurcation, at about L4, is where the aorta ends by dividing into the right and left common iliac arteries. A clamp placed just above it sits below the celiac trunk, the superior mesenteric artery, the renal arteries, and the inferior mesenteric artery, so those branches still fill. The common iliac arteries, and everything they feed in the pelvis and lower limbs, lie beyond the clamp.
notes: Correct. The common iliac arteries start at the bifurcation, below the clamp, while the renal and mesenteric branches all leave above it.

The renal arteries leave the aorta at about L1 to L2, well above the bifurcation, so they are upstream of a clamp placed this low. They would lose flow only if the clamp were placed above the kidneys.
The superior mesenteric artery arises at about L1, far above the clamp, so it keeps its blood supply. It would be affected by a clamp placed high on the aorta near the diaphragm.
The celiac trunk is the highest unpaired branch, arising just below the diaphragm at about T12. It would lose flow only if the clamp were placed above it, right at the top of the abdominal aorta.
questions.answerText: Both common iliac arteries

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: A pill is swallowed and the drug is absorbed through the wall of the small intestine. Which organ does the drug reach first after it leaves the intestine?
options: The heart
The kidneys
The liver
The lungs
questions.why: Drugs absorbed from the small intestine enter capillaries that drain into the superior mesenteric vein and then the hepatic portal vein. The portal vein delivers them to the liver before they can reach the heart or the rest of the body. Liver cells can break down part of the dose on this first pass, which is one reason some drugs need a higher dose when taken by mouth than when injected.
notes: The heart is the next stop after the liver, since blood leaves the liver through the hepatic veins and the inferior vena cava to reach the right atrium. The heart would come first for a drug injected into a vein in the arm.

The kidneys receive the drug only after it has passed through the liver, heart, and lungs and been pumped out through the aorta to the renal arteries. Pick them for where a drug is filtered out of the blood into the urine.
Correct. The hepatic portal vein carries the drug to the liver first.
The lungs are reached only after the liver and the right side of the heart, when blood is pumped through the pulmonary trunk. They would be the first organ reached by an inhaled drug.
questions.answerText: The liver

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: An hour after a large meal, which vessel carries blood with the highest concentration of absorbed glucose?
options: The hepatic portal vein
The hepatic artery
The inferior vena cava
The hepatic veins
questions.why: After a meal, glucose absorbed by the small intestine enters the superior mesenteric vein and then the hepatic portal vein, so the portal vein carries nutrient-rich blood straight from the gut. As this blood passes through the liver sinusoids, liver cells take up much of the extra glucose and store it as glycogen. The blood leaving through the hepatic veins therefore has less glucose than the blood that came in.
notes: Correct. The portal vein carries freshly absorbed nutrients straight from the gut.

The hepatic artery carries oxygen-rich blood from the celiac trunk into the liver. It has not passed through the intestine, so its glucose level matches ordinary arterial blood. Choose it for the vessel that brings oxygen to the liver.

The inferior vena cava carries blood from the lower body and the liver back to the heart. By the time portal blood reaches it, the liver has already removed much of the glucose, and it is mixed with blood from the legs and kidneys. Pick it for the vein that returns lower body blood to the right atrium.

The hepatic veins carry blood out of the liver after liver cells have removed much of the extra glucose. Pick them for the vessels that drain processed blood from the liver into the inferior vena cava.
questions.answerText: The hepatic portal vein

questions.topic: Vessels of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.q: A clot blocks the left common iliac artery. The left leg turns cold and pale while the right leg stays normal. Which statement best explains this?
options: The left leg depends on the inferior mesenteric artery, which joins the common iliac
The left leg depends on the left renal artery, which branches from the common iliac
The left leg depends on the internal iliac artery, which arises above the common iliac
The left leg depends on the external iliac artery, a branch of the left common iliac
questions.why: Each common iliac artery divides into an internal iliac artery for the pelvis and an external iliac artery that continues into the thigh as the femoral artery. Because the left external iliac artery branches from the left common iliac artery, a clot in the common iliac cuts off the main route of blood into the left leg. The right leg is fed by the right common iliac artery, a separate branch at the aortic bifurcation.
notes: The inferior mesenteric artery leaves the front of the aorta at about L3 and supplies the lower colon and upper rectum. It does not join the common iliac artery or feed the leg, so pick it for the descending and sigmoid colon.

The left renal artery leaves the side of the aorta at about L1 to L2 and supplies the left kidney, not the leg. It does not branch from the common iliac artery, so pick it for blood flow to the kidney.

The internal iliac artery is a branch of the common iliac artery, not a vessel above it, and it supplies the pelvic organs and gluteal region rather than the length of the leg. Choose it for blood supply to the bladder or gluteal muscles.
Correct. The external iliac artery, the leg's main supply, comes off the common iliac artery.
questions.answerText: The left leg depends on the external iliac artery, a branch of the left common iliac

questions.topic: Blood
questions.q: What are the three functional categories of blood?
options: Transport, regulation, and protection
Filtration, secretion, and absorption
Conduction, contraction, and secretion
Digestion, storage, and excretion
